The trace persists and the response does not.

## THE STAND-IN SURVIVED ITS OWN SUCCESS, AND EVERY UNKNOWN ADDRESS ANSWERED 200 (2026-08-25)

**Run 36's open finding, diagnosed and fixed: `northgroup-2` answers `/deals` and `/no-such-page` with 200 and the 856-byte placeholder, on a site that published four real routes.** The soft-404 the SEO tier already fixed once, arriving through a door nothing was watching.

- **NEITHER LAYER I SUSPECTED WAS AT FAULT, and the control is what settled it.** `decideFallback` is fail-open BY DESIGN (`if (!manifest) return {kind:"ok"}`), the sweep is behaving exactly as written, and the manifest lives in the sidecar and is read perfectly. What is wrong is one key: **`publishPlaceholder` writes `sites/<slug>/index.html`, and under Start a dist contains NO top-level document** — so a real publish never overwrites that key. The platform's extensionless fall-through then reads it for any address the site does not have and serves it. **Measured against `oak-and-ash`, built before the early write existed: 404, 9 bytes**, on the same code, the same day. One site has the object and one does not; nothing else differs.
- **THE SWEEP DOES GET THERE, ONE PUBLISH LATE, AND THAT IS NOT GOOD ENOUGH.** `sweepPlan` DEFERS a stale key by one publish, so the stand-in would go on the publish AFTER the one that made it obsolete — **and a site published once and never edited again serves it for ever.** The grace period exists for code-split CHUNKS an already-open session may still ask for; nothing on any site ever asks for this key. So the fix is a deliberate delete rather than a change to the sweep.
- **GUARDED BY THE MARK, NEVER BY THE KEY, and the archive is why that is load-bearing rather than defensive.** Every version archived before Start holds a REAL `index.html`, and `rollbackVersion` copies it back — so a delete keyed on the name would take a restored home page down. `clearPlaceholder` READS the object and removes it only if it carries the placeholder tag. **Measured on four live sites (`fold-lane-bakery`, `harbourside-roast`, `the-lido-cafe`, `lido-axes-b`): all four now serve an SSR document and all four 404 an unknown address**, so the live population is already Start-shaped and it is the archive that makes the guard matter.
- **THE TAG IS ONE CONSTANT NOW (`PLACEHOLDER_META`) BECAUSE TWO SIDES READ IT.** The writer emits it and the clearer looks for it, and the second is a DELETE at a customer's own public address — so two spellings drifting apart does not read as "the mark stopped being recognised", it reads as a publish that silently stops taking its own stand-in down.
- **IT RUNS FROM `putSiteWorker`'s SUCCESS PATH, NOT FROM `writeSiteDistToR2`, and that placement is the whole safety argument.** Under Start the script is the ONLY thing that renders a document, so "the pages are in R2" is not evidence the site serves anything — and **a publish whose script did not land still answers `ok:true, page:"app"`**. Clearing in the writer would take the customer's one remaining page away on exactly the build that needed it. `putSiteWorker`'s own comment already makes this argument for the confirm-wait one line above: three call sites, and one that forgot would be indistinguishable from one that did it.
- **NOT GATED ON `confirmed`**, because that wait is explicitly never fatal and a slow confirmation must not leave a stand-in standing over a site that really is serving. **Being wrong toward keeping it costs a stale page the next publish sweeps; being wrong the other way costs a 404 at the customer's own address.**
- **DRIVEN, NOT SOURCE-READ, and both halves are exported so they can be.** The one mistake that matters — deleting a real page — is a fact about what the guard does with BYTES, which no regex over `worker.js` can see; `siteWebResearch` set the precedent for exporting a function so a test can run it. The fixture is produced by the REAL writer, so the two halves cannot agree with each other and with neither end (the `routeOf` lesson).
- **TWO EXISTING GUARDS WENT RED ON A CORRECT CHANGE AND BOTH WERE THE SAME OWN-GOAL.** One pinned the inline `PLACEHOLDER_MARK + "\" content=\"placeholder\">` concatenation and failed the moment it was NAMED — a test about word order. The other two windowed `publishPlaceholder` by slicing to `function svcHeaders(`, **five declarations away**, so they swept in whatever was declared between and reported that the scan "lost its bounds" about code that had not moved. Both re-anchored on `topLevel()`, which closes at the next top-level declaration **or its doc comment** — the first draft of that helper swallowed 2,600 characters of prose arguing for the new function and failed for a third reason.
- **THE ONE OTHER READER OF THAT KEY IS THE STATIC FALLBACK, AND WHAT IT LOSES IS A LIE RATHER THAN A SITE.** The serve path dispatches to the site's own script first and drops to the static read only when that THROWS — *"Worker not found"* or a script that broke — on the stated reasoning that *"the visitor getting the last published build beats a 503"*. **True of a pre-Start site and empty for a Start one**: its dist has no top-level document and no per-route `.html`, so the static path could only ever have served the stand-in there. So a Start site whose script later dies goes from *"still being put together"* on a site that has been live for months to an honest 404. It was never protection either — the sweep would have taken the same object on the next publish.
- **AND THE EXISTING SITE IS NOT RETROACTIVELY FIXED.** `northgroup-2` keeps its stand-in until its next publish, like every other publish-time fix here. One republish through the rebuild queue would clear it; not done for one site.
- **AND I WALKED INTO THE ABBREVIATED-SHA TRAP THIS FILE ALREADY RECORDS.** `?head_sha=63e8755` answers `total_count: 0`, my watch read that as "nothing pending", broke out of its loop and **exited having printed nothing** — silence indistinguishable from a quiet build, which is the exact failure the run-36 entry describes. Recorded again because the entry alone did not stop it: **query the full 40 characters, and make a watch that finds no runs SAY SO rather than fall out of the loop.**
- **AND ONE MUTANT NEVER APPLIED AND WAS REPORTED AS SUCH RATHER THAN COUNTED.** `read -r` does no escape processing, so the doubled `\\"` I wrote in the mutation list could never match the single `\"` in the source — the sweep edited nothing and the suite passed. **A mutant that never applied reports as coverage that is not there**, which is the mirror of the inert-mutant trap and the reason the runner md5s the file rather than reading the result. Re-run with the corrected pattern.
- 4149 tests (+7 in `test/site-placeholder.test.mjs`), **9/9 mutations as expected** from a verified-green isolated baseline with a comment-only control that had to survive — including the two that read alike from outside: the clear never running, and the clear running BEFORE the upload's own refusals. **PROVEN LIVE on run 37 — see the entry above.**

## RUN 36, PROVEN LIVE: THE PLACEHOLDER, AND A 45% SWING THAT KILLS A TREND OF ONE (2026-08-25)

**`https://northgroup-2.gofarther.app/` — the same CRM brief that died as `northgroup`, published in 10m 31s.** `done: true, ok: true, page: "app", total_ms: 630734`, 13 credits, four routes, no database. A fresh slug because the dead run still owns the old name.

- **THE PLACEHOLDER IS PROVEN, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING THIS RUN SETTLES.** Live at **3m 49s** — `<meta name="gofarther-page" content="placeholder">`, 856 bytes, serving EVERY address — while generation still had six minutes to run. For those six minutes the site had a real page at its real address. That is the half of the ship-anyway change that needs nothing of ours to be alive at the moment of failure, and until now it had never run.
- **THE FULL TRACE**: auth 166 · body 0 · gate 494 · **design 172,736 (in 166, out 3,432)** · owner 489 · **provision 222 (db: 0)** · **schema 0 (tables: 0)** · seed 0 · merge 1,054 · fonts 416 · gen 150 · **img 340,277** · **compile 151** · container 82,531 · og 167 · pages 31,881.
- **`img` 340,277 AGAINST RUN 35's 619,822 — 45% LESS, SAME BRIEF, SAME PICKER, SAME MODEL.** So the 620s was an unlucky draw and **not a property of CRM briefs**, which is the hypothesis I offered a day earlier off one sample. The eight-build median (~390k) predicted this run far better than the one observation did. **A trend in one sample is not a trend**, recorded again because I drew one anyway.
- **`compile` IS 151ms — IT BOUGHT NO PHOTOGRAPHS AT ALL, and that is the measurement the owner's fal check earned.** Run 35's same span was 28,089ms, squarely in the band of builds that DID buy one (24.7k–32.6k), against `smoke-mt6fxehk`'s 110ms for one that did not. So the two runs of one brief differ in whether the designer declared an image, on a brief whose own words are *"no photographs anywhere"*. **The owner read fal, saw nothing, and was right; I argued from the span and was wrong about what it meant.** What it costs is 28 seconds a run 35 turned out to need.
- **NEITHER DEADLINE FIRED AND BOTH HAD MARGIN**: 630,734 against our 780,000 (2m 29s spare) and Cloudflare's 900,000 (4m 29s spare). So this run does NOT prove the budget fires — it proves a build fits under it. The refusal path remains unexercised.
- **THE SOCKET DIED AT 258.3s AS USUAL** — tenth recorded instance — and cost the answer and nothing else. The build ran seven more minutes with nothing connected.

**AND THE HARNESS CALLED A RUNNING BUILD PUBLISHED, WHICH IS MY BUG AND THE ONE WORTH KEEPING.**

- **IT PRINTED THE DISPROOF ON THE SAME LINE.** `step 4b — +0.0m site 200 | done=false ok=null at=gen` followed immediately by `step 4b — PUBLISHED after 0.0 minutes of waiting`. The watch polls for a 200 and **the placeholder is a 200**, served at the site's own address.
- **I DOCUMENTED THIS HAZARD THE DAY BEFORE AND WIRED IT TO NOTHING.** The entry below says in as many words: *"a watcher polling for the site to come up reads the stand-in as a finished build. One `<meta name="gofarther-page" content="placeholder">`."* The marker shipped, the unit suite asserts exactly one kind of page carries it, and **the single watcher that needed to read it never did** — the wiring layer, for the thirteenth recorded time, in the change whose own notes describe the failure.
- **RIGHT BY LUCK IS NOT RIGHT.** This build published, so the run's verdict was correct; on run 35, which never published, the identical code would have reported a site that does not exist.
- **THE BODY DECIDES AND THE TRACE ONLY DECIDES WHEN TO STOP.** A 200 carrying the marker is not published — read off the body, which cannot lag the way a row can, so a trace that is behind never blocks a genuine success. The trace answers the other question: `done === true` **strictly** while the page is still a stand-in means the build FINISHED and left it standing, which ends the wait honestly instead of polling a settled site for the rest of the job. An unreadable trace answers `{err}` and keeps waiting, because "Supabase blinked" and "the build gave up" want opposite responses.
- **THE MARKER IS DERIVED FROM `worker.js`, NEVER RESTATED, and that guard is the whole durability of this fix.** Rename `PLACEHOLDER_MARK` there and the watch silently stops recognising a placeholder — no error, bug restored. The test rebuilds the tag from that constant AND from the line that emits it, so a marker declared and never rendered fails too.
- **AN EXISTING GUARD WENT RED ON THE CORRECT CHANGE**, pinned to `traceLine(slug)` — a reader I split so the watch could SEE `done` as well as print it. Re-anchored on the ARGUMENT rather than the function's name, since what has to hold is which slug is read. This repo's most repeated own-goal.
- 4142 tests (+5), **3/3 mutations as expected** with a comment-only control that had to survive — including the silent one: `worker.js` renaming the marker with the harness left behind.

**AND AN ADDRESS THE SITE DOES NOT HAVE SERVED THE PLACEHOLDER RATHER THAN A 404** — `/deals` and `/sign-in` both 200 with the 856-byte stand-in on a site that published four real routes. Recorded here as undiagnosed and **diagnosed and fixed the same day; see the entry above.** Neither candidate named here was right: the fallback and the sweep are both behaving exactly as designed, and it is the stand-in surviving its own success.

## EVERY CEILING WE HAD WAS LONGER THAN THE ONE CLOUDFLARE ENFORCES (2026-08-25, owner's call)

**"the whole site cant no go live if one step breaks, we need to fix that, if one step breaks its gotta ship like that, however it is."** Two builds are 404 today — `helm` killed mid-generation, `northgroup` mid-container — and every fallback path in this repo was intact and none of them was reached.

- **THE ARITHMETIC IS THE WHOLE FINDING.** A queue consumer is guaranteed **fifteen minutes**; `BUILD_BUDGET_MS` was **two hours**, `CONTAINER_CALL_MS` and `BUILDER_CALL_MS` **an hour** each, `QUEUE_WAIT_MS` sixteen minutes. So not one of our own bounds could fire — the isolate is stopped first, and **a stopped isolate does not publish a fallback, log a reason or answer a customer.** `publishPages` has four honest bail-outs, all of which publish the data-model page; none can run when nothing is running.
- **THE MODULE'S OWN DOCSTRING SAID SO BEFORE IT HAPPENED**: *"a budget that expires after its container has already been torn down refuses nothing — it just fails later, which is what happens today."* Written about the 30-minute runner cap and true of the consumer's fifteen. **A rule that goes stale because a layer beneath it moved**, for the fourth recorded time.
- **THIS TOUCHES AN EARLIER OWNER'S CALL AND IS NOT A REVERSAL OF IT.** The two hours came from *"just let the model work, forget about time"* — right against a ceiling of OURS and inert against one of Cloudflare's. A two-hour budget buys the model no time at all; it guarantees that when the real ceiling arrives we have published nothing.

**THE HALF THAT SURVIVES BEING KILLED IS THE PLACEHOLDER, PUBLISHED EARLY.** Every other fallback needs our code to run at the moment of failure. A write that has ALREADY happened needs nothing.

- **`publishPlaceholder` IS ONE WRITER CALLED AT TWO MOMENTS.** The late call is unchanged and still says what failed; the new early one goes up the instant the design lands, before the ten expensive minutes begin. From that point there is no failure — ours, the model's or Cloudflare's — that can leave the customer with nothing.
- **IT IS AWAITED, and that is not fussiness.** Started and not awaited, the isolate can be stopped between deciding to publish it and doing so — the same failure moved a few hundred milliseconds.
- **THE GUARD IS THE LIVENESS MARKER AND A THROW IS NOT AN EMPTY SLUG**, both unchanged from the late call: a revise of a working site is skipped, and an R2 blip read as "nothing is published" would overwrite a live site with a stand-in — the outcome this exists to prevent.
- **A THIRD VOICE, because the page is now published at a moment when nothing has gone wrong.** The failure wording would be a lie there — and the wording used instead has to stay true if the build then dies, since this page is what the owner is left holding. *"Still being put together, send it again if it is still here"* is true either way; *"refresh in a minute"* is not.
- **AND IT SAYS IT IS A PLACEHOLDER.** It is served at the site's REAL address, so from outside it is a 200 like any other — and it now goes up while the build is still running, so a watcher polling for the site to come up reads the stand-in as a finished build. One `<meta name="gofarther-page" content="placeholder">`, asserted to be carried by exactly one kind of page.

**AND THE CURE: THE PHOTOGRAPHS GIVE WAY TO THE CLOCK.**

- **WHICH STEP YIELDS IS NOT ARBITRARY.** The build runs `gen → img → compile → container → og → pages`, so running out of time at the PICTURES still leaves a complete set of pages that can be compiled and published, with `SafeImage`'s own placeholder where a photograph would have been — the fallback that whole file is designed around. Every later step degrades to nothing.
- **CORRECTED 2026-08-25, BY THE OWNER, AND THE CORRECTION REVERSES WHY THIS SHIPPED.** This bullet read *"MEASURED, AND IT IS EXACTLY WHY THE CRM HAS NO SITE — `northgroup` spent 619,822ms there, 74% of the 836s it had lived"*, attributing that span to the PHOTOGRAPHS. **It is the page-generation model call.** The owner checked fal, saw no image jobs on that build, and said so.
  - **THE MARK NAMES ARE OFF BY ONE AND THAT IS WHAT I MISREAD.** Each mark is written at the START of the step it NAMES, so its `ms` is the step that just ENDED. `mark("gen")` sits before `generateSitePages`, `mark("img")` at the top of the `images` dep — i.e. AFTER generation returned. So **`img.ms` is generation and `compile.ms` is the photographs.**
  - **PROVEN OFF THE ROW RATHER THAN REASONED**: on `oak-and-ash`, `img` is 304,402ms and its own `genMs` extra is **304,402ms** — identical to the millisecond. `container` is 111,717 and `buildMs` is 111,717, the same way. A number that equals `genMs` is not the image step.
  - **SO THE REAL SPLIT ON `northgroup` IS: generation 619,822ms (10m20s), photographs 28,089ms (28s).** A CRM is not picture-led, so there was almost nothing to buy — which is why fal was empty and why the owner's read of it was the thing that settled this.
  - **WHICH MEANS `photoWait` DOES NOT ADDRESS THIS FAILURE.** It bounds a WAIT that took 28 seconds. It is not wrong and it is not what saved anything here; **claiming otherwise is what this correction exists to stop.** What actually bites on this build is `BUILDER_CALL_MS` (1 hour → 10 minutes) composed with the 13-minute budget: generation starts at 188,548ms, so `capMs` gives it 591,452ms and it needed 619,822 — **cut 28 seconds short.** The build still fails; it fails at 13 minutes with the placeholder already live instead of being killed silently at 15.
  - **AND THE STANDING ANSWER IS THE CONTAINER.** Generation is not optional — it IS the site — so no yielding rule can save a call that needs longer than the Worker can ever offer. Cloudflare Containers have **no fixed maximum runtime** (their words) and we already run one; the generation call is in the Worker. That is where this goes when it goes.
- **`photoWait` IS IN `site-images.mjs`, NOT INLINE, and that is why it is DRIVEN rather than read.** Three answers, and collapsing any two is a bug: `all` (no clock — the old behaviour exactly, so a second caller is not cut off by a bound it never set), `race` (wait only for the time ABOVE the reserve — racing `remainingMs()` ends the wait with nothing left to publish with, which is a bounded image step and still no site), `none`.
- **WHATEVER LANDED IS KEPT.** Each shot writes into the map as it resolves, so giving up on the WAIT discards no photograph already bought. Nothing already paid for is lost.
- **A BROKEN CLOCK IS NO CLOCK**, which is `build-budget.mjs`'s own rule: refusing a healthy build is the more expensive mistake.
- **CALIBRATED AGAINST BOTH REAL BUILDS, not chosen.** `PUBLISH_RESERVE_MS` is 4 minutes against a measured tail of 173,161ms (compile + container + og + pages on `oak-and-ash`); `BUILD_BUDGET_MS` is 13 minutes, above that build's whole 594,054ms so the one run known to work is untouched, and below the consumer's fifteen with two minutes for the deadline to fire while the isolate is still alive. **Both are asserted against those measurements**, so a number moved past either goes red naming which.
- **MY OWN TWO GUARDS WENT RED TEN MINUTES AFTER I WROTE THEM**, both pinned to the inline expression I then extracted — the spelling-pin own-goal, twice in one sitting, in checks written for this very change. Replaced by driven tests, which is what the extraction was for. Two older guards went the same way on `publishPlaceholder`; both re-anchored, and one is **stronger** now: with one writer it can assert that nothing else builds the page.
- 4138 tests (+10 in `test/ship-anyway.test.mjs`), template typechecks, **10/10 mutations as expected** from a verified-green baseline with a comment-only control that had to survive. **One mutant reported a clean run without having applied** — the mark line is full of escaped quotes and the shell ate the pattern; caught by an md5 check rather than by reading the result, and re-run from a file. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against any of it.

## THE WHOLE PLATFORM HAD ONE BUILD CONTAINER, AND NOBODY MEANT IT TO (2026-08-25, owner's call)

**"we need to fix that get container thing, it has to be so anybody at any time can build while other are too."** `getContainer(binding)` takes an optional NAME and every one of the five call sites omitted it — and the library's default is the literal string `cf-singleton-container`. One name is one Durable Object is **one container instance**, so every build this platform has ever run — every site, every customer, every cheap edit, every game — resolved to the same one.

- **THE DESIGN WAS ALREADY RIGHT AND ITS SECOND HALF WAS NEVER SWITCHED ON, which is why this is one argument rather than a rewrite.** `builder/build-server.mjs`'s own comment states it: *"Serialised rather than given a directory each … **Cloudflare scales container INSTANCES; this only has to make one instance honest.**"* `oneAtATime` was written on 2026-07-29 after two real builds destroyed each other in a shared `src/routes`, and it protects an INSTANCE from itself. It was never meant to be the platform's queue — but with one instance it became one, which is the state `worker.js` recorded in three separate comments as *"`oneAtATime` for the WHOLE PLATFORM"*. All three said what was happening and none of them said it was an accident.
- **`max_instances: 5` HAS THEREFORE NEVER BEEN REACHABLE.** Both classes have declared it since they were written and exactly one instance has ever existed. **The fix needs no config change at all** — it uses the capacity already declared, so there is zero deploy risk, which matters because a `wrangler.jsonc` value the platform refuses is not a slower build, it is NO DEPLOY AT ALL (three merges shipped nothing that way on 2026-08-07). Raising the ceiling is now one number in two places with a guard holding them together.
- **BUCKETED, NOT KEYED BY SLUG, AND THE REASON IS A MEASURED ABSENCE.** The obvious fix is `getContainer(binding, slug)` — one instance per site, total concurrency. It is rejected because **what Cloudflare does when a Worker asks for more instances than `max_instances` allows is documented on neither container page, and the client library has no knowledge of the limit at all** (`max_instances` appears nowhere in `@cloudflare/containers`). So the boundary is enforced somewhere we cannot see, in a way we cannot predict, on the platform's primary feature. Hashing into a FIXED five lanes makes that boundary unreachable by construction — and **a collision degrades to today's behaviour rather than to an undocumented error**, because two builds sharing a lane share an instance and `oneAtATime` serialises them exactly as it serialises everything today. That is the whole argument.
- **`oneAtATime` STAYS, and the source says why.** A lane is one instance with one working directory, so "finishing the job" by deleting the chain reintroduces the 2026-07-29 failure on a path that now LOOKS concurrent and is not.
- **FNV-1a, NOT A SUM OF CHARACTER CODES** — this repo's own recorded lesson from the favicon hue, where a sum hashes `ab` and `ba` identically. Two slugs that are anagrams (`fold-lane` / `lane-fold`) are exactly the pair that would share a lane for ever.
- **IT NEVER ANSWERS `undefined`, which is the one return value that would be catastrophic AND silent.** `getContainer(binding, undefined)` takes the default parameter and lands back on `cf-singleton-container`: the exact bug, restored invisibly, with every test green. Anything unusable answers lane 0, which is a real lane. A non-string is not coerced either — `String(["a","b"])` is `"a,b"`, the coercion this repo has shipped as a real bug three times.
- **THE KEY IS THE UNIT OF WORK AT EACH SITE, and they differ honestly.** Both site call sites key by **slug**: two customers compile at once, two edits of one site share a lane on purpose. The game REVISE keys by slug for the same reason. The game BUILD keys by **account**, because a game names itself only AFTER it compiles — the slug is minted from the model's own answer further down, so there is nothing narrower in scope. The game health probe passes a literal, since a probe has no build to be keyed by and any lane answers *"can I reach a container at all"*.

**AND SPLITTING THE LANES FOUND A REAL CORRUPTION IN THE GAME TIER: its build server had no queue at all.** `wipeSrc()`/`wipeDist()`/`wipeAssets()`/`wipeModels()` clear four SHARED directories at the top of every game build and nothing serialised them — so two builds arriving together interleave and one deletes the other's sources mid-compile.

- **IT WAS SURVIVING ON THE ACCIDENT BEING FIXED HERE.** Everything resolved to one instance, so the Worker's own arrival order was all that stood between two game builds. **Lanes make a collision five times rarer and never impossible** — two builds by one user share a lane BY DESIGN — so the protection has to be in the server rather than inferred from how requests happen to arrive.
- **THE PRIMITIVE IS COPIED RATHER THAN SHARED, deliberately.** These are two container images that share no code, and a helper reached across that boundary is one `COPY` line in a Dockerfile away from a build service that cannot start — the failure the Dockerfile guard already exists for.
- **THE QUEUE STARTS AT THE FIRST WIPE, not at the top of the handler**, so a malformed body is still refused immediately rather than behind whatever is compiling.
- **AND IT IS DRIVEN RATHER THAN SOURCE-READ, because NOTHING in CI runs this server.** `builder-game/smoke.mjs` tests a built GAME in a browser, not the build service, so a structurally wrong edit here would have shipped on `node --check` alone. Run against the real server with a stub `APP_DIR`: it boots, **three concurrent requests all answer** — each returning from INSIDE the queue, past all four wipes, at the `no valid files written` exit — the wipes are observed to have run, and the three pre-queue refusals (`invalid json`, `no files`, a wrong route) come back in **6ms, 1ms and 0.7ms**, which is what proves the queue starts where it claims to.

- **THE SWEEP FOUND ONE REAL GAP AND IT WAS MINE, TWICE OVER, IN THE SAME SHAPE.** The coercion check asserted `laneName(["a","b"]) === laneName("")` — and **over five lanes two distinct hashes collide about one time in five by arithmetic**, so that assertion was measuring luck rather than the property, and the mutant replacing the type check with `String(key)` SURVIVED. My anagram check had the identical flaw and went red against correct code on its first run. Both are asked at a WIDE lane count now, which isolates the claim about the HASH from the bucketing. **An assertion whose outcome depends on the modulo is not an assertion about the hash.**
- **TWO EXISTING GUARDS WENT RED ON A CORRECT CHANGE and both were pinned to `getContainer(env.SITE_BUILD_CONTAINER)` — an ARGUMENT LIST.** Each failed the moment an honest second argument joined it, one of them reporting *"the container call is gone from the build path"* about a call that is right there. This repo's most repeated own-goal; both re-anchored on the binding.
- **AND THE PROCESS FAILURES ARE WORTH MORE THAN THE CODE HERE.** I backgrounded a second mutation batch while the first was still running **against the same isolated tree**, and they raced: batch 2 restored and deleted a `.orig` out from under batch 1's restore, and reported a SURVIVOR from a tree the other process had left dirty. **A sweep whose isolation was violated proves nothing** — the whole thing was re-run serially from a tree verified byte-identical to the source. Then `pkill -f "lane-sweep"` killed my own shell at exit 144, for the **tenth** recorded instance: the harness wraps a command in a shell whose command line CONTAINS the pattern.
- 4128 tests (+11 in `test/build-lane.test.mjs`, half of them asserting the WIRING because this is the layer twelve features have shipped dead in), template typechecks, **8/8 mutations as expected** from a verified-green baseline with a comment-only control that had to survive. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against it, and what a unit suite structurally cannot show is that two real builds now occupy two real instances.

## RUN 34, PROVEN LIVE: A SITE WITH NO DATABASE, AND THE CTA IS INVISIBLE (2026-08-25)

**`https://oak-and-ash.gofarther.app/` — a joinery workshop, published in 9m54s, with NO Neon project.** `done: true, ok: true, at: "pages", total_ms: 594054`, 70 credits, 2 photographs. The first build this platform has ever made that has no database, and the split below is proven end to end.

- **THE TRACE IS THE PROOF AND IT IS NOT THE LINE I ADDED.** `provision` carries **`db: 0`** and `schema` carries **`tables: 0`** — the marks that only exist on the no-database path. The step-5 log line written for exactly this claim **never ran**, because the socket died at ~263s and step 5 sits inside `if (!disconnected)`. **The one line this run existed to produce is on the branch that did not execute**, which is a gap in my own change; the trace answered the same question independently, which is the only reason the run still settles it.
- **THE RESET COST NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE SECOND PROOF.** The ordinary ~285s edge reset, ninth recorded instance — and `discoverSlug` recovered `oak-and-ash` off `site_backends` **on a build that provisioned no database**, which is precisely what `claimSiteSlug` was written to keep working. The watch branch then rode the build to 200. Without the claim this run would have had no name to watch.
- **THE FULL TRACE**: auth 349 · body 0 · gate 459 · **design 113,610 (in 11,981, out 2,591)** · owner 631 · normalize 0 · **provision 184 (db: 0)** · **schema 0 (tables: 0)** · seed 0 · merge 1,042 · fonts 52 · gen 164 · img 304,402 · compile 27,326 · container 111,717 · og 122 · pages 33,996.
- **THE DESIGN CALL HALVED AGAINST RUN 33 AND THE FRESH INPUT FELL BY ~7,000 TOKENS.** 113.6s against the CRM's 233.5s, and `in: 11,981` against arm A's 20,313 and arm C's 18,998 — close to the 41.4% / ~7,300-token cut measured on the wire before the run. **Stated as a direction rather than an attribution**: the brief also changed, so this is one build against builds of a different shape, and only the tool measurement is controlled.
- **THE FOUR THINGS THAT WOULD HAVE INVALIDATED THE CHANGE ARE ALL CLEAN.** No table declared. **No data call anywhere** — `useRows`, `usePublicRows`, `useCreateRow` and six siblings, zero hits across 7 modules and 498,485 bytes of bundle. **No form and no `onSubmit`**, on a brief whose natural build is a quote form — it wrote *"We would much rather talk at the bench than write an email"* instead. And **every figure from the brief is on the page**: all three prices, the phone number, the hours, the town.

**AND THE ONE REAL DEFECT, WHICH IS BACKLOG #192 REPRODUCED AND NOW DIAGNOSED.** The header's *"Ring the workshop"* — the site's primary call to action, on a brief whose whole point is that people ring — renders **brand-on-brand and is invisible**: `color: rgb(106,67,40)` on `background: rgb(106,67,40)`, measured.

- **THE CAUSE IS THE CASCADE LAYER, NOT SPECIFICITY, and asking Chrome is what settled it.** The model's own stylesheet ends `a{color:var(--primary);text-underline-offset:.18em}` — a perfectly reasonable "links are brand-coloured" rule. `CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode` reports four rules setting `color` on that element, and the winner is `a` at **`layer=(unlayered)`** over `.text-primary-foreground` at **`layer=utilities`**. Tailwind v4 puts utilities in `@layer utilities` and `writeFreeCss` appends the model's sheet unlayered, so **an unlayered rule beats a layered one whatever its specificity** — the exact mechanism this file already records for the `display` axis, arriving from the other direction.
- **IT HITS BUTTON-SHAPED ANCHORS SPECIFICALLY.** `<a href="tel:…" class="bg-primary text-primary-foreground">` is how every CTA in this kit is built, so a bare `a` colour rule is guaranteed to blank them while leaving prose links correct — which is why it looks fine everywhere else on the page.
- **THE TOKEN WAS NEVER WRONG**, checked before blaming it: `--primary-foreground` resolves to `#f4efe6` at the element and at every ancestor, and `.text-primary-foreground{color:var(--primary-foreground)}` is in the compiled sheet. Three plausible causes ruled out by measurement before the fourth was found.
- **WHETHER OUR OWN RENDER CHECK SAW IT IS UNANSWERED, and the disconnect is why.** A 1:1 contrast is far under the floor of 3, so it ought to have been reported — and `contrast` is deliberately NOT in `SERIOUS`, so the repair pass would not have acted on it either way. The report rode on the response, which died with the socket. **Not knowing is itself a finding**: the reset costs the render report as well as the cost breakdown.
- **NOT FIXED IN THIS RUN.** It is a live customer-facing defect with a precise diagnosis now rather than a reasoned-about backlog line, and the fix is a decision (layer the free CSS, or scope the model's selectors, or re-emit the button colour after it) rather than a patch.

**AND ONE FALSE ALARM OF MINE, CAUGHT BEFORE IT WAS REPORTED.** The `fullPage` screenshot has a huge cream void where six sections should be — the documented capture artifact, since a fullPage shot expands the viewport WITHOUT scrolling and scroll-driven reveals stay at `opacity: 0`. Measured per section with each centred in view: **all ten at opacity 1.** This file already records walking into that trap twice; the mirror harness now measures rather than believes the picture.

- **A FRONTEND-ONLY SITE MIRRORS FAITHFULLY, which is a real consequence rather than a convenience.** Every previous mirror had to stub `/api/db/*` with `[]` so lists rendered their empty state instead of an error, and the screenshot then had to say which parts were the stub. There is no data API here, so there is nothing to stub and the mirror IS the site.

## A FIRST BUILD IS FRONTEND ONLY — NO BACKEND FIELD, NO DATA RULES, NO DATABASE (2026-08-25, owner's call)

**"in the design step we are gonna divide backend and frontend, and in the generator step we are gonna do the same, so at build time model only does frontend, the backend comes at later, when editing and when addon and whatever comes."** Steps 2, 3 and 4 of the four-step plan whose step 1 is the entry below. A first build now designs a site, writes its content into the pages, and creates **no Neon project at all**.

- **THE THREE ARE ONE CHANGE AND THAT IS NOT A CONVENIENCE.** A designer that declares no tables beside a generator still told to wire pages to them writes `useRows("menu")` against a schema with nothing in it; a designer that declares nothing while the route still refuses a tableless build 422s every first build on the platform. Each of the three is broken without the other two.
- **`backend` IS 41.4% OF THE TOOL ON THE WIRE — 29,189 of 70,594 characters of serialised JSON, ~7,300 tokens off the cached block.** **A first draft of that number said 69.7% and 51,348**, which is the SOURCE region including its own ~22,000 characters of explanation — a figure that never leaves the file. Measured through `readSchemaTool`, which builds the real tool: **what a prompt costs is what is sent**, and slicing worker.js measures the comments.
- **THE SAVING IS REAL AND IT IS NOT THE POINT.** A designer handed five backend fields ANSWERS them, and every table it invents on a brochure site is a Neon project against a platform-wide cap of 100, an access decision, and a page wired to rows nobody will ever write.
- **THE PAGE PROMPT GOES 42,201 → 30,495 CHARACTERS (27.7%), 15 hard rules to 6, 10 sections to 8** — eleven data rules and three data sections. Same argument one call along: what a prompt full of worked `useRows` examples buys is a model that copies them, which is this repo's own finding about worked examples.
- **SURGERY ON ONE SOURCE, NEVER A SECOND LITERAL.** `frontendRules(PAGE_RULES)` drops by RULE NUMBER and by SECTION NAME and renumbers; **keep is the default**, so a rule added tomorrow lands in both prompts unless somebody names it. Being wrong that way puts a sentence about data in front of a model with no data — which the derived guard catches — where being wrong the other way silently drops a craft rule from every first build.
- **RENUMBERING IS SAFE AND THAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The whole prompt holds exactly ONE `rule N` cross-reference — `(rule 10)` — and it lives inside `## Visitor accounts`, which is dropped. A guard asserts none survives, so a reference added to a KEPT rule fails here rather than shipping a prompt that points at the wrong rule.
- **THE DERIVED GUARD FOUND A LIVE CONTRADICTION IN A KEPT REGION ON ITS FIRST RUN, which a drop list could never have reached.** `## Charts` told the model *"prop-driven — hand it `useRows(...)` data, never a copied array"* — the exact opposite instruction, in a section that has to stay. Three more like it (the `display`-table picture-column bullet, "pass it the site's own rows", and the closing line naming "the hooks, the access levels"). They are REPLACEMENTS rather than edits to `PAGE_RULES`, because every one is TRUE on a site with a database — **and each is asserted to have applied**: a replacement whose `from` stops matching is silent, so `frontendRules` throws rather than shipping a prompt it could not correct.
- **THE POSITIVE HALF IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS.** Deleting the data instructions leaves a model that still knows every business site it has ever read fetches its menu from somewhere — so it invents the somewhere. That is the `publicView` failure this repo has paid for twice: a capability conditioned on a fact the model was never given. Both new prompts therefore say WHERE THE CONTENT LIVES before they say anything else, and the frontend rule 2 says not to draw a form that submits nowhere — a control that silently does nothing is worse for the business than not having one, because a customer who fills it in believes they are booked.
- **`neon_db: ""` MADE THE SLUG CLAIM POSSIBLE WITH NO MIGRATION, and CLAUDE.md's own note was wrong about why.** It records claim-first as *"considered and rejected: `neon_db` is NOT NULL so it needs DDL"* — right about the column, **wrong about what NOT NULL forbids**. Measured against the live schema: `text NOT NULL`, no default, and the empty string is perfectly legal — and `siteBackendRowFresh` has ALWAYS answered `{conn: null, uid, brief}` for a falsy `neon_db`. So the ownership half works today and the connection half is honestly absent.
- **THE ROW IS NOT OPTIONAL AND IT IS NOT A DATABASE RECORD.** `site_backends` is what the 409 refuses against, what `existing` reads to decide the next message is a revise, what the delete route authorises against, and what the Data panel, version history and the backups sweep all key off. A site with no row can be overwritten by name and can never be deleted through the route.
- **PROVISION IFF THE SPEC DECLARES TABLES OR THE SITE ALREADY HAS A DATABASE — a FACT, never the `firstBuild` flag.** Keyed on the flag the answer would be wrong the moment anything adds a site's first table; keyed on the spec it cannot go stale, so *"the backend comes later"* needs no second mechanism. **`ownerConn` is the other half and it is not optional**: a revise that declares nothing (a colour change) must still resolve the database the site already has, or `pageSpec` falls back to this request's empty spec and the generator rewrites every page believing the site stores nothing.
- **CANNOT-TELL IS A REVISE, NOT A FRESH SITE.** `namedRow` has three states — a row, `null` (the name is free), `undefined` (the lookup threw) — and everything reads the third as "a site is there". Being wrong that way costs a bigger prompt; being wrong the other way hands a revise of a real site a tool with no backend in it, silently, on the one path where the customer is asking to change what it stores. The `loadConfig` rule, one layer up.
- **AND `ownerConn` IS READ OFF THE LATE CHECK RATHER THAN THE EARLY ONE, for the same reason inverted.** The early ownership check fails OPEN by design (a cheap refusal, not the authority); the late one 503s on a throw. So by the time provisioning is decided the answer is fresh and known.
- **THE FLAG DEFAULTS TO FALSE AND THAT DEFAULT IS THE SAFETY.** Three lanes call `designSiteSchema` and only the build route can ever be a first build; a fourth added tomorrow gets the whole tool by saying nothing. **Not derived from `current`**, though it is null on every first build and an object on both edit lanes: `editState` also stays null when the config read blips.
- **AND THE EDIT SWAP NOW COMPOSES OFF `req.tools[0]` RATHER THAN OFF THE CONSTANT.** Rebuilding from `SITE_SCHEMA_TOOL` was harmless with one tool and is the exact trap the free-CSS comment three lines below it already warns about — two lines each rebuilding from one source means the second silently undoing the first. Belt-and-braces today (`frontendOnly` implies no `current`) and it says so, which is the convention `built.ok &&` and the `pressed` axis already live under.
- **FIVE GUARDS WENT RED ON CORRECT CHANGES AND EVERY ONE WAS PINNED TO A SPELLING** — the design call's exact `tools:` expression, the exact `required` swap, `if (!spec.tables.length && !existing) {` (an honest third term), `const editSlug = cleanSlug(` (one cleaning FEWER, not one more), and `const slug = cleanSlug(`. All re-anchored on properties, and two of them now assert the split itself: both tools must be reachable from the `tools:` line, or a ternary collapsed to one branch would silently un-split the prompt.
- **TWO SOURCE-READING HARNESSES WERE ANCHORED ON A PHRASE INSIDE AN EXPRESSION.** `readSchemaTool` and the member-shapes guard both found `text: "You design the data model` — a POSITION inside `designSiteSchema` — and lifting that string into `SITE_SCHEMA_SYSTEM` moved the position while changing not one byte of what is sent. Both read the named constant now: a landmark that is a phrase inside another expression is one the next edit moves; a `const` has a name.
- **AND MY OWN GUARD COUNTED ITS OWN COMMENT.** The one-reading check found `cleanSlug(body.slug)` twice — once in the code and once in the note explaining why the second one was removed. **Prose containing the thing it forbids**, this repo's most-recorded own-goal, walked into inside the guard's own subject. Comments blanked, length-preserving, whole-line only. And a `[^)]*` parameter scan read the signature four short, because `modelsFor().design` closes at the first `)` — the fifth recorded flat-scan instance.
- **`build smoke` STOPS WITH ONE HONEST FAILURE RATHER THAN FORTY MISLEADING ONES.** Its data tier — a Neon project, `_meta` endpoints, seeded rows, a data read, a form that submits, the owner's table door — was calibrated for a build with a database, and a frontend build correctly has none of it. **Not a skipped pass**: the run stops and stays red, because rewriting that tier is real work that has not been done, and a harness that quietly shrank to fit would report a platform smaller than it is. The `else` each tier needs is written down in the source so the next person does not re-derive it. `build as owner` is unaffected — it reads `site_backends` only to recover a slug when the connection dies, and the claim keeps that working.
- 4116 tests (+18 in `test/frontend-build.test.mjs`, all derived and all asserting BOTH directions so a collapsed split cannot pass), template typechecks. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against any of it.

## THE SITE'S LOOK LIVES WHERE THE SITE IS SERVED FROM (2026-08-24, owner's call)

**"that stuff should be stored in the hosting provider right?"** — and it should. `site_look`, `site_css`, `site_logo`, `site_icon`, `site_verify` and `site_lang_strings` were in `_meta`, a key-value table inside the site's OWN Neon database, beside the things that genuinely describe a database. **None of the six is a row.** They are config for the compiled output, and the compiled output is in R2. `site-config.mjs` is one object per site at `config/<slug>.json`, injected store, `_meta` as a read-only fallback.

- **THIS IS STEP 1 OF FOUR AND THE OTHER THREE DEPEND ON IT.** The owner's plan: split the design tool so `backend` comes off a first build (69.7% of `design_schema`), split the generator so no data wiring is written, and **skip provisioning entirely — no Neon project on a first build at all**. That last one is only possible if the look has somewhere else to live, because otherwise a frontend-only site's publish path has nothing to write to and eight edit lanes refuse. **This step changes nothing observable**; it is the prerequisite.
- **THE TIER MAP WAS WRONG IN ONE PLACE AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART.** Asked whether "Workers assets → compiled files, R2 → uploads, Neon → structured data" describes this platform: **we use neither Pages nor Workers Static Assets.** Each published site is its own Worker SCRIPT and every byte it serves comes out of the bucket — `site-dispatch.mjs:74` binds R2 to it as `SITES`, `template/src/server.ts:137` does `env.SITES.get("sites/" + SITE_SLUG + url.pathname)`. So it is **two** tiers: R2 is everything that is not rows (`sites/`, `source/`, `uploads/`, `versions/`, `backups/`, `sitemeta/`, `orphans/`, `jobs/`, and now `config/`), Neon is rows. The six were filed one tier down from the thing they describe, and nothing else was misfiled — `schema`, `auth_info`, `data_api`, `jobs`, `webhook_last` and `invite_only` are all genuinely about the database and stay.
- **ONE OBJECT, NOT SIX, and the read sites are why.** The publish spine reads every one of them on every cheap edit, so six keys is six round trips where the `_meta` query was one.
- **A READ THAT THROWS IS NOT AN EMPTY CONFIG, and that distinction is the whole safety property.** It was learned by losing it: until 2026-08-14 the spine's look read swallowed its own error and fell through, so one blip during ANY cheap edit republished the live site with no theme, no stylesheet, default fonts and its SLUG as its title — told the customer it worked, and archived the stripped version to history. `loadConfig` answers `{ok:false}` for all three cannot-tell paths (the bucket, a corrupt object, the legacy database) and each names itself, because an operator reading a log cannot otherwise tell a bucket outage from a corrupt object from a database blip. **A corrupt object refuses rather than falling back**: R2 writes are whole and strongly consistent, so garbage there is a bug to surface, not to route around by publishing stripped.
- **THE NEON FALLBACK IS A MIGRATION RAMP AND IS READ-ONLY.** Every site published before this has its six values in `_meta` and nothing in R2, so a miss falls back and backfills — the `site-routing.mjs` shape, where a fallback makes an empty store slow rather than wrong. **Nothing ever writes back**: one writer, or the two stores drift and whichever is read first wins. A failed backfill costs a slow read next time and never the read it rode on.
- **A MISSING BUCKET THROWS RATHER THAN ANSWERING EMPTY**, which is the same rule one layer down. `SITES_BUCKET` is also what SERVES the site, so its absence is not a degradation to ride out. And the legacy reader is **omitted** for a site with no database, which is the state every frontend-only site will be in — that is the one thing steps 2-4 need from this.
- **ONE PLACE WHERE "NO DATABASE" AND "COULD NOT RESOLVE ONE" MUST NOT SHARE AN ANSWER.** `buildAndPublishPages` resolves its own backend for the translation-cache write, and with no legacy reader `patchSiteConfig` has nothing to fall back to — so on a site not yet migrated it would write a cache-only config over an empty key, every later read would find R2 non-empty and stop falling back, and **the site's whole look would be unfindable.** Skipping costs one re-translation. Theoretical today because both callers have already read-and-backfilled by then, and that is a property of another function one edit away from changing.
- **DELETING A SITE DELETES ITS CONFIG, and this is the sharpest of the five private prefixes.** It lives outside `sites/<slug>/` so the publish wipe walks past it, and left behind, **whoever claims the slug next inherits a stranger's Search Console tokens from the very first request** — a standing way for the previous owner to keep claiming the new owner's site at Google. The design and the translation cache go with it. Same class as the Neon projects, the version archive, the orphan marker and the backups, and the reason each of those has its own line there.
- **`editState` ON THE BUILD ROUTE HAD NEVER WORKED, found while rewriting the line.** It read `sqlQuery(conn, …)` on `siteNeonProject`'s return, which is the raw Supabase ROW — and `neon()` refuses anything that is not a connection string ("Connection string: [object Object]", measured). So the query threw into its own catch on every revise this route has handled, `editState` stayed null, and the designer was never told to change only what was asked. The same misread is recorded twice in `recompileAndPublish`'s own header. Fixed as part of the line being rewritten, because passing a row knowingly is not an option; **it is a behaviour change and is called out rather than folded in silently** — a revise's designer is now anchored where it was not.
- **AND THE SAME MISREAD KILLED THE WHOLE SCHEDULED-JOBS TIER, which is NOT fixed here.** Three call sites in the jobs runner pass the row the same way. **Measured against the live ledger: 26 jobs, all enabled, `last_result` is 12× "this job is no longer part of the site" + 10× "the site's database is unreachable" + 4 null. Zero sends, ever** — and both sentences name the wrong cause. Left alone deliberately: fixing it starts 26 real email and SMS senders, which is the owner's call rather than a storage refactor's side effect. Backlog #206.
- **SEVENTEEN GUARDS WENT RED AND EVERY ONE WAS PINNED TO A `_meta` SPELLING.** Most became STRONGER on re-anchoring, because the property they were written for is now structural: "every look-assembling read carries the stylesheet", "every publish-payload read loads the verification", "a read asking for the logo must ask for the icon" were all scans over hand-written `SELECT … WHERE k IN (…)` lists, and a reader could legitimately ask for five of six keys. `loadConfig` answers with every field or refuses, so there is no key list left to leave one out of — what is asserted instead is that the field is still declared, that both payload paths BIND it (loading and not destructuring is the select-and-drop shape this repo has lost a feature to), and **that nothing reads a config field out of `_meta` any more**, which is the absence that makes one-store true rather than merely likely.
- **AND THE BYTE-WINDOW OWN-GOAL, TWICE MORE ON ONE LINE.** `if (priorBrief) { [\s\S]{0,400}` went red because my own comment above the read outran it — a test about how much prose sits in between. Bounded by the block's own catch now.
- 4102 tests (+21), template typechecks, **19/19 mutations as expected** across two sweeps from verified-green baselines. **Both first-sweep survivors were real gaps in my own tests**: `writeConfig` skipping `normalize` was invisible because the round trip asserted through `readConfig`, which normalises too (asserted on the STORED BYTES now), and the logo lane swallowing a failed save would have told a customer their logo landed with nothing holding it. **AND THE ROUND-2 CONTROL NOT-APPLIED ON ITS FIRST ATTEMPT** — the anchor was a comment I had since edited, so the line printed after it was the unmutated file passing. **A sweep whose control never applied is a sweep with no control**, recorded here for the sixth time; re-run with a verified anchor and an md5 proving the bytes moved, it survives as it must. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build or edit has run against it.

**Owner: "ok make a build, do crm". `helm` never published.** Design, provisioning and the schema all worked in **257 seconds**; the pages call was entered at that mark and no answer ever arrived. 9 credits (88 → 79), a claimed slug, a live Neon project, a 404. The husk shape this file records for runs 3, 4, 9, 10, 13 and arm C.

- **THE MEASUREMENT WORTH KEEPING IS THE RATE, AND IT COMES OFF `site_builds` RATHER THAN OFF MEMORY.** Every build since the queue landed (2026-08-23): `smoke-mt5igr76` published · `lido-cafe` **died at gen** · `smoke-mt6fxehk` published · `the-lido-cafe` published · `helm` **died at gen**. **Three of five.** Small n, and it is the first time the number has been counted rather than recalled — the pre-queue failures (`lido-axes`, `css-axes-lido`, `lantern-lido`) are excluded on purpose, because back then a dropped connection really did kill the build.
- **A CRM BRIEF COSTS 2.2x THE DESIGN CALL AND 1.7x ITS OUTPUT, measured against every café this account has built.** `design_ms` 233,502 and `design_out` 4,242, against 48,784-106,514 and 1,572-2,546 for the eight café runs. Four tables, four pages, a layout each and a manifest is simply a bigger plan. **So a CRM spends nearly four minutes of the consumer's fifteen before the expensive call starts** — which is the margin problem the arm D entry above is about, arriving from the other end.

A long design is a real cost and it does not discriminate — reading it as the explanation is exactly the trend-in-three-samples mistake this file already records.
- **NOTHING OF OURS CAN SEPARATE "still generating" FROM "the isolate is gone", still.** The trace writes on a MARK; `gen` is written at the START and `img` closes it, so a stale `gen` is what both look like. The site was 404 at +62 minutes and the consumer's guarantee is fifteen, so it is dead — but that is inferred from the clock rather than reported by anything.
- **THE 18-MINUTE POST CEILING DID NOT FIRE AND COULD NOT HAVE.** `ECONNRESET` at **261.1s** — the ordinary edge reset, an eighth instance alongside 264.6 · 274.3 · 285.3 · 286.0 · 289.3 · 291.9 · 549.6. A real socket error arrives first, so the ceiling still has no live proof; what it bounds is the SILENT death, which this was not. Recorded rather than implied, because a fix that was never reached must not be reported as one that worked.

- **THE WATCH BRANCH WORKED PERFECTLY AND THAT IS THE ONE THING PROVEN HERE.** The reset at 261s cost the answer and not the run: `discoverSlug` recovered `helm` off `site_backends` (written at 13:55:40, four minutes before the reset would have mattered), and the trace line named the mark on every poll for 62 minutes. Without it this run would have exited at 261 seconds saying nothing.

## THE RENDER CHECK COULD NOT SEE A CRASHED PAGE, AND NOW IT FIXES ONE (2026-08-24, owner's call)

**"after the page generation step, can there be a revise step that literally checks everything that it generated, checks what's wrong and fixes before launching it?"** — then, told that fixing meant a second generation: **"can it just edit it?"** Both halves right. `builder/site-repair.mjs` is the wire from the detector to a fix, and the detector had a hole in it.

- **THE MEASUREMENT THAT CHANGES WHAT THIS IS: the render check would have called today's crashed `/book` CLEAN.** `the-lido-cafe` published with a dead booking form (`useFormField should be used within <FormItem>`), the check ran, and the finding it produced was `logged` — which is not in `SERIOUS`. **Two mechanisms stacked, and both are ours.** `ErrorPage` is the router's `defaultErrorComponent`, so React CATCHES the throw and never rethrows — `page.on("pageerror")` therefore never fires. And the card prints **109 characters** of apology, comfortably over `BLANK_TEXT_CHARS` (40), so `blank` cannot fire either. **A working safety net hiding the fault from the one check written to find it**, and no amount of wiring a repair pass to `SERIOUS` would have helped while it was invisible.
  - **A `data-slot` ATTRIBUTE, NEVER THE COPY.** Sites are bilingual since 2026-08-19, so matching the apology's words fails on every non-English site — silently, and precisely on the sites least likely to be checked by hand. `probe()` reads `[data-slot="error-page"]` and `readPage` turns it into `threw` **carrying the first console error as the detail**, which on the measured case names the fault, the component and the fix in six words.
  - **RAISING `BLANK_TEXT_CHARS` IS THE OBVIOUS WRONG FIX and is pinned against.** 109 characters is not blank; a floor above it flags every short-but-correct page.
- **WHY THIS IS NOT THE 2026-08-04 REPAIR PASS, stated because the name is the same.** That one re-ran `generateSitePages` — the whole ~36,000-token prompt, a fresh write of every page, ~80% of a build's cost, so a failing build cost roughly twice a working one. **This edits ONE FILE through the `tweak` rung**: Haiku, the page's own source, a short prompt. ~3 credits against ~10, ~1 on a refusal. **That was a second GENERATION; this is a second EDIT**, and the economics that killed the first do not apply.
- **NOT ONE GUARD IS COPIED — `runTweak` is called unchanged.** `sameProse` (0 false alarms over 1,640 real tweaks, catching a rewording on 329 of 329 pages), `routeIdOf`, the truncation floor and `tweakLint`'s differential all live in `site-tweak.mjs` and `readTweak` applies them in one place. What could NOT be reused is the SYSTEM PROMPT: `TWEAK_RULES` opens *"the customer has asked for one visual change"* and lists `cannot` for anything that is not one — handed a page that threw, it is an instruction to refuse. So `tweakRequest` took a `rules` (and `heading`) parameter, both additive, **and a guard asserts the tweak lane still sends exactly what it sent before** — a drifted default would quietly put every customer tweak on the repair prompt.
- **THE FAULT IS ASSERTED AS OBSERVED, and that sentence is load-bearing.** A model handed a page that looks reasonable answers that it looks reasonable; this one was WATCHED FAILING IN A BROWSER, so *"I can't see anything wrong"* is not available. It keeps `cannot`, which escalates honestly rather than inviting a guess. **The cause list is fitted to TWO observed failures and says so** — `useFormField` today and `message-scroller` (which this repo already records as typechecking, bundling and hard-crashing the page) — offered as examples rather than a taxonomy, and first to re-measure once real reports exist.
- **ONLY `SERIOUS`, DEDUPED BY PAGE, AND ONLY PAGES THIS BUILD WROTE.** `contrast`/`overflow`/`image`/`logged` are judgement calls that fire on correct sites; this rung spends money and rewrites a customer's page, so it gets the narrow half. The check opens every route at BOTH widths, so a crash is two findings — undeduped, the commonest real report spends two calls on one file and the second is handed a file the first already changed. A route with no page behind it is the site's own 404 or a layout: nothing to send.
- **A CHECK THAT COULD NOT RUN BUYS NOTHING.** `report.ok === false` is a browser that would not start, which reports zero findings — and zero findings must never read as a clean site OR as a broken one. No report, no repair, no spend.
- **`MAX_REPAIRS` IS 3 AND WHAT IT DROPPED IS REPORTED.** A site has at most 5 pages, so this is a sanity bound rather than a cost one: a report naming every page as broken is far likelier to be the check having a bad day than five independent faults, and spending five calls on that is the false-alarm failure paying for itself. **A silent cap reads as "covered everything"** — the repo's own rule.
- **A FAILED RECOMPILE KEEPS THE ORIGINAL BUILD, which is the whole safety argument.** `built` at that line already compiled and would have published; if the repaired source does not, the customer gets exactly the site they were getting a moment ago — one page rendering an apology — rather than nothing. Never worse, the rule `salvagePlan` already lives under. **ONE ATTEMPT**, then publish whatever we have.
- **IT NEVER THROWS.** It sits in front of a build that has already succeeded, so a provider outage, a null answer and a malformed reply all have one correct outcome: publish. An exception escaping turns *"the repair was unavailable"* into *"the build failed"*.
- **THE USAGE RIDES BACK ON EVERY PATH, REFUSALS INCLUDED, and joins the ONE variadic `pageCredits` call.** These are real model calls. Added as a separately-rounded total they would charge twice for the rounding — the measured `sumUsage` bug.
- **A SUCCESSFUL REPAIR IS SILENT; A FAILED ONE NAMES THE PAGE.** A repair is our business, and announcing one invites the customer to hunt for damage. A page still broken afterwards is actionable, so it is named.
- **`built.ok &&` IS BELT-AND-BRACES TODAY AND SAYS SO IN THE SOURCE.** Measured: the render step runs only after a compile succeeds, so a failed build carries no `render` and `repairBrief` answers with no work whatever it is handed — driven with `undefined` and with `{ok:false}`. The mutant removing it survives ON PURPOSE. Kept because what makes it inert is a property of ANOTHER function one edit away from changing, which is the convention `site-css.mjs` and the `pressed` axis already live under.
- **THE WIRING IS ONE LINE AND IT HAS ITS OWN GUARD**, because `publishPages` gates on `typeof deps.repair === "function"` — so a route that supplies none produces a build byte-identical to before, every test green, and not one broken page ever fixed. **The shape twelve features in this repo have died in.** The guard blanks comments length-preservingly first, since `worker.js`'s own explanation spells `repair:` and `deps.repair`: **prose containing the thing it asserts**, now recorded in a lint, a router guard, an absence check, a scope scan, a mutation and here. Both mutants (the line deleted with the comment left; the dep reaching no model) die, and a comment-only control survives.
- **AND MY OWN COMMENT TRIPPED AN EXISTING GUARD, the same trap one file over.** `THE PROBE CLOSES OVER NOTHING` scans `probe()`'s source for outer identifiers, and my new comment inside it names `BLANK_TEXT_CHARS` — so a correct change went red. Fixed by blanking comments in the GUARD (length-preserving, with a length assertion) plus **a planted reference proving the scanner still catches a real one**, since a blanker that ate too much would report a clean probe.
- **THE FIRST DEDUPE MUTATION WAS PARTIALLY INERT AND REPORTED A GAP THAT WAS NOT THERE.** `if (!perPage.has(page.path))` → `if (true)` still yields ONE Map entry per path, because the Map is keyed by path — it loses accumulated kinds, not the dedupe. Re-run honestly (key per FINDING: `page.path + "|" + f.viewport`) it dies against the test written for it. **A mutant that changes no behaviour reads exactly like a test gap**, for the umpteenth recorded time.
- **AND IT SHIPPED WITH A FIELD COLLISION, FOUND BY READING THE FUNCTION RATHER THAN BY A TEST.** `out.repaired` is already owned ~190 lines up by `repairImports` — the deterministic export-name rewrite — whose own note says *"a clean build must report NO repairs at all; `repaired: []` reads in the response and in the eval as a generator that keeps getting names wrong."* The browser repair wrote the same key, so **on a build where BOTH fired the import fix vanished from the response**, on exactly the run that had two things wrong with it, and one field carried module names on some builds and routes on others. **The `cost`-means-two-things bug, one field over.** No test could have caught it: the repair harness's fixture pages have no bad imports, so the two writes can never both fire there. `renderRepaired`/`renderRepairFailed`/`renderRepairRefused`/`renderRepairDropped` now, **the whole family prefixed rather than just the one**, or the next field added to either feature re-collides — and a derived guard scans every `out.X =` in the file and fails if any repair field is written twice, **paired with a check that both features still report at all**, since a scan over a file where one stopped writing passes vacuously.
- 4082 tests, template typechecks, **13/13 mutations as expected** across three sweeps from verified-green baselines, each with a comment-only control proved to have APPLIED before it was believed. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against it.

## THE HARNESS WAITED 75 MINUTES FOR AN ANSWER THAT ARRIVED AN HOUR EARLIER (2026-08-24)

**`build as owner` run 32723813218: the build FINISHED at 12:02:02Z — `site_builds` says `done: true, ok: true, total_ms: 528542`, and the site answered 200 — and step 5 was still running at 13:17Z.** `postLong` had **no ceiling of any kind**: `req.on("error")` fires only on a REAL socket error, so a connection that dies silently (no FIN, no RST — a middlebox dropping state on a long-idle connection) hangs until the 350-minute job cap.

- **IT SURVIVED BECAUSE ITS JUSTIFICATION WENT STALE A DAY BEFORE IT BIT.** The docstring's central claim was *"hanging up KILLS THE BUILD MID-FLIGHT… the client staying connected is what lets the build finish at all"* — **true until 2026-08-23 and false since**: the build is a queued job, so a dropped connection costs the ANSWER and not the SITE, proven live by a socket destroyed at 30.0s and a site published 11m58s later. While hanging up really did kill the build, having no ceiling was CORRECT and there was nothing to weigh; the queue reversed that and nobody re-asked the timeout question. **A rule true because of something one layer down expires when that layer moves, and nothing announces it** — the `#/` href failure and the `fonts`-becomes-required failure, a third time.
- **THE BOUND IS THE WORKER'S OWN, NOT A SECOND GUESS AT BUILD LENGTH.** `QUEUE_WAIT_MS` is 16 minutes: past it the Worker stops waiting on the consumer and answers, so a reply that has not arrived by **18** has no path left to arrive by. The harness's copy of that 16 is **read out of `worker.js` by the guard** rather than restated, and the ceiling must be `QUEUE_WAIT_MINUTES + slack` — a bare literal fails, because the point is that there is one meaning.
- **IT REJECTS RATHER THAN RESOLVING, so it lands in a branch that already exists** — `disconnected = true`, then watch the trace and the site. That path is proven (arm C, 2026-08-23), is strictly better than waiting because it can SEE a build that finished, and **until now the only way to reach it was a reset.** No new failure path, asserted.
- **AND IT NAMES ITSELF.** The catch prints `e.code || e.message`, so a bare timeout would read as a network fault on a run where the network was fine — the fifth recorded instance of a failure that could not say what it was.
- **`build smoke` HAD THE IDENTICAL HOLE AND RUNS ON EVERY PUSH.** Its `cutMs` is the DELIBERATE cut for the disconnect proof, never a bound. Both are fixed and both are asserted, over the FUNCTION rather than the file — "a timeout exists somewhere in here" is satisfied by the cut. The deliberate cut is unaffected: it is far shorter, destroys the socket first, and clears the ceiling through `close`.
- **THE GUARD BLANKS BLOCK COMMENTS NOW, not only line comments** — `postLong`'s docstring argues the ceiling at length and therefore spells `POST_CEILING_MS` and `destroy`, so a line-only blanker left the check matching its own prose. Length-preserving, asserted so, and the pairing was **measured** before widening it (2 opens / 2 closes here, all paired) rather than assumed — a block blanker on `worker.js` eats 46% of the file.
- **AND MY CONTROL NEVER APPLIED THE FIRST TIME**, for the fifth recorded time: the anchor did not match, `python` threw, and the line printed after it was the UNMUTATED file passing. **A sweep whose control never applied is a sweep with no control.** Re-run with a real anchor and an md5 proving the bytes moved: it survives, as it must.
- 4081 tests, **6/6 mutations caught** from a verified-green baseline plus a control proved to have applied. The site, the ledger and the trace were all verified correct before a line was changed — **the build was never the problem.**

## ARM D, LIVE: THE PAGES CALL IS 44% FASTER AND THE MARGIN CAME BACK (2026-08-24)

**One Grok build on today's three cuts — the kit named once, `MAX_COMPONENTS` 24 → 50, thirteen look fields → one stylesheet.** `https://the-lido-cafe.gofarther.app/` published. **`img` (the page-generation call) 492,562ms → 275,335ms; the whole build 739,174ms → 528,542ms (12m19s → 8m49s).**

- **THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS IS THE MARGIN, NOT THE MINUTES.** The queue consumer is guaranteed **fifteen minutes** and the 2026-08-23 proof run took 12m28s — this file's own words for it were *"the margin is thinner than this file has been saying"*. 8m49s puts ~6 minutes back under a ceiling that had ~2.5.
- **A LEGITIMATE COMPARISON, and the reason it is legitimate is worth stating**: the same brief shape, the same picker, the same slug discipline, on the queue path. Not a controlled experiment — three changes landed together — so what it establishes is the DIRECTION and the total, not an attribution to any one cut.
- **THE PROMPT SHRANK AND THE OUTPUT DID NOT.** Rule 3's deletion is ~8,600 cached tokens off the input; the manifest widening is ~1,561 tokens ONTO the fresh per-site block. Net still down, and the fall in wall-clock is far larger than either — consistent with the model spending less time reading and none of it re-deriving what the designer already chose.
- **THREE FINDINGS FROM THE SAME RUN, none of them fixed by it.** (1) **The booking form was dead** — `useFormField should be used within <FormItem>` — which is what the repair pass above exists for and what exposed the render check's blindness. (2) **Sections run edge-to-edge where others are inset**: `SiteChrome`'s `<main>` carries no container BY DESIGN, the reference `index.tsx` put `mx-auto max-w-5xl px-6` on all 7 of its sections, and **`PAGE_RULES` contains ZERO occurrences of any container concept** — so the four worked examples were the only thing teaching it, and they left the prompt this morning. **Measured, not inferred.** (3) **A bare `a` selector in the free CSS blanks the primary CTA** — backlog #192, now reproduced live rather than reasoned about. **DIAGNOSED 2026-08-25 (run 34): the cause is the CASCADE LAYER, not specificity** — Tailwind v4 emits utilities into `@layer utilities` and `writeFreeCss` appends the model's sheet UNLAYERED, so `a{color:var(--primary)}` beats `.text-primary-foreground` whatever the specificity, and every CTA in this kit is `<a class="bg-primary text-primary-foreground">`.
- **AND ONE FALSE ALARM OF MINE, CAUGHT BEFORE IT WAS REPORTED, TWICE.** The huge cream gap in the `fullPage` screenshot is the documented capture artifact — a `fullPage` shot expands the viewport WITHOUT scrolling, so scroll-driven reveals stay at `opacity: 0`; measured per section centred in view, **all of them opacity 1**. And a "clipped `£7`" was my crop: `scrollWidth === clientWidth` at both widths, zero overflow. **This file already records both traps and I walked into both.**

## THE KIT IS NAMED IN THE DESIGNER AND NOWHERE ELSE (2026-08-24, owner's call)

**"only call the whole kit in designer."** The same 2,112 module names were printed TWICE in one build — once in `design_schema`'s `components` field, which is where the choice is made, and again in `PAGE_RULES` rule 3, **after the designer had already chosen.** The second copy is gone. **`PAGE_RULES` 72,736 → 42,201 characters, 42% off the cached block**; rule 3 alone 37,470 → 6,925.

- **THE REDUNDANCY WAS FOUND BY THE OWNER ASKING THE OBVIOUS QUESTION**, and it is the right one: page generation runs AFTER the designer, whose whole job is to narrow. The designer needs the list because it is choosing from it; the page writer is handed a manifest and does not.
- **MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED: 30,991 characters, ~8,600 tokens, 43% of the cached block — 0.54 credits on every warm build and 2.15 once per prompt version.** More than the whole 24→50 manifest widening cost (0.39). Both figures come from the repo's own rate table at the default picker.
- **THE CONSTRAINT FLIPPED FROM NEGATIVE TO POSITIVE, and that is the whole replacement.** It read *"these are every name under that path, and nothing else exists there"* — an absolute that needed the list to be true. It now names the two places the model may import from (the always-on signatures, and the per-site manifest later in the same message) and says the designer already picked. **A positive constraint needs no inventory.**
- **THE PROPS PARAGRAPH WAS LOAD-BEARING AND UNDERCUT ITSELF.** It said everything in the list *"is real and you may render it — but you would be calling it blind."* So the prompt handed over 2,112 names and then discouraged reaching past the ~80 with props. The list mostly enabled a behaviour the next sentence argued against.
- **THE CHART LIST STAYS AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A SIZE JUDGEMENT.** `COMPONENT_MENU` holds `@/components/ui/` names ONLY, so the designer's manifest **can never name a chart** — delete that list too and the whole 865-component tier is unreachable, which is exactly the failure rule 3's scoping was written after. Asserted, with the premise (`COMPONENT_MENU` covers no chart) asserted beside it so the day that changes the guard says so.
- **THE SAFETY NET WAS ALREADY THERE, TWICE.** `lintPages` refuses an import of a module that does not exist and names the real ones in its message; `tsc` refuses it again. What is given up is catching it in the PROMPT, which is cheaper than catching it at compile — and is why this is worth an eval run rather than a shrug.
- **TWO GUARDS ASSERTED THE DELETED POLICY.** One demanded rule 3 print every kit name and close on *"nothing else exists there"*; **INVERTED** rather than deleted, on the standing precedent — it now requires the names to be ABSENT, probing one from the frozen head of the menu and one from its alphabetical tail so a mutant restoring either half of `COMPONENT_MENU` is caught. The other's substring-trap self-check read `PAGE_RULES.includes("visibility-toggle")`, true only because rule 3 printed the kit; the trap is a fact about the KIT, so it reads `UI_COMPONENTS` now — **and additionally proves the word boundary discriminates**, since asserting the trap exists says nothing about whether the pattern survives it.
- **AND MY OWN CHART GUARD SURVIVED ITS FIRST MUTATION — the prose trap, in the guard written for this deletion.** It probed `salon`, `restaurant`, `bullet`, and deleting the ENTIRE catalogue passed: rule 12's own prose says *"a barber shop's page reaches for `salon`, a cafe's for `restaurant`"* and an `import { Bullet }` example spells the third. **Prose describing a list contains that list's words** — this repo's most repeated own-goal, ninth recorded instance. Probed on EXPORT names now (`MortalityTable`, `PrintTimeStack`, `FlightEnvelope`), which appear in the catalogue and nowhere else, each asserted to still be in the kit first.
- **A MUTANT THAT NEVER APPLIED REPORTED A CLEAN SWEEP**, for the fourth recorded time: `${CHART_NAMES}` is not an identifier in this repo (`CHART_CATALOGUE` is), so the first run of that mutation edited nothing and passed. Caught by `grep -c` answering 0 rather than by reading the result.
- 4057 tests, **4/4 mutations as expected** with a comment-only control that had to survive. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — the Anthropic account is dry.
- **THE ONE THING NOT MEASURED, STATED PLAINLY: whether the model still avoids inventing an import.** `page gen eval` samples generation with no database, no publish and no account, and counts distinct compile errors BY SHAPE — that is the instrument for this question and it has not been run. Worth one run when the account is funded.

## THE MANIFEST IS A CAP NOW, NOT A RANGE — 24 → 50 (2026-08-24, owner's call)

**"i wanna put 50 components instead of 10-24, 50 max, so the model chooses how many it needs."** `MAX_COMPONENTS` 24 → 50, and **the FLOOR went with it**: the field asked for `10-24`, and a range makes a site that genuinely needs eight components pad to ten. What is left is a ceiling and a judgement.

- **THE COST IS THE PER-SITE BLOCK AND IT IS NOT CACHED, which is the whole reason to measure rather than assume.** `components` is a MANIFEST: `siteComponentApi` prints the exact props of every name on it **into the USER message**, deliberately — a block that varies per site inside the cached prefix would miss the ~27,000-token prefix on every build, measured at thirteen times the input cost. So this is FRESH INPUT at 1x, every build.
- **DRIVEN AGAINST THE REAL `componentApiFor`, not estimated: 24 names is 3,872 characters (~1,076 tokens) and 50 is 9,494 (~2,637).** +1,561 tokens, which at the default picker's own rate is **+$0.0031 — 0.39 credits, about 1% of a 38-credit build.** And it is only paid by a site that really names 50: a shop that needs twelve sends twelve, which is exactly what dropping the floor is for.
- **THE MENU IS UNCHANGED AND THAT DISTINCTION IS WHAT THE COMMENT GOT WRONG.** `COMPONENT_MENU` went to all 2,112 names on 2026-08-21 and its note claimed *"`MAX_COMPONENTS` is unchanged, so the MANIFEST does not grow; only the menu it is chosen from."* True then and false now — corrected in place, because a comment that stops being true is what gets believed.
- **THE CAP IS STILL IN CODE AS WELL AS IN THE DESCRIPTION**, which is this repo's standing distinction: `normalizePlan` slices to `MAX_COMPONENTS`, so a model naming sixty gets fifty. A cap a model is merely told about is not a cap.
- 4057 tests. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — the Anthropic account is dry, so no designer has answered the wider field.

## THE LOOK IS THE STYLESHEET, AND THE OTHER SIX FIELDS WERE ALREADY DEAD (2026-08-24, owner's call)

**"lets delete this and let it just be css, when the model makes the css."** The merge step reconciled thirteen look fields across two publish spines and the look edit lane; `css` is the only one left. **worker.js 1,162,152 → 1,143,050 characters**, 21 imported names down to 1.

- **ALL SIX WERE FIELDS THE DESIGNER CANNOT ANSWER, AND MEASURING THAT IS WHAT MADE THE CUT DECIDABLE.** Driven against the real tool: of the seventeen things the merge reads off `designed`, **`seeds`, `fonts`, `tokens`, `style`, `tokensPage` and `pageFonts` are not properties of `design_schema` at all** — they came off it on 2026-08-23 when five look fields became one. So `designed.tokens` has been `undefined` on every build since, `mergeTokens(prior, undefined)` handed back exactly what was stored, and `parseTokens(undefined)` reported nothing asked for. **The machinery was carrying values forward and could no longer receive one.**
