- **AND THREE TERMS OF THE NO-CHANGE GATE WENT WITH THEM, HAVING BEEN INERT SINCE THE DAY BEFORE.** The look lane's `named` check read `designed.tokens`, `designed.style` and `designed.tokensPage` — three of the six fields the tool cannot answer — so all three were `hasValue(undefined)` on every look edit there has been, and two terms decided a check that read as considering five. **A guard that cannot fire reads as protection that is not there**, which is this repo's own rule; what stops them returning is the `site_*` key guard below rather than the terms themselves.
- **THE ONE REASON IT SURVIVED WAS MEASURED AND IS GONE.** `worker.js`'s own header said it: *"the merges below survive the deletion on purpose… no-ops that hand back what the site already wears, which is exactly what 'one deploy re-styles no site' means in code."* True, and the platform is **25 sites, every one ours** — `wassup`, `esmoke-fixture`, the four `lido-*` CSS experiment arms, the `smoke-*` runs. Queried before a line was cut, because that sentence is the whole justification and it is a fact about the database rather than about the code.
- **WHAT IT COSTS, WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN GLOSSED, and one of the three is real.** The 31-token derived palette goes and **`normalizeSeeds`' contrast floors go with it** — `site-freecss.mjs` reads and never validates by design, so nothing now proves a site's body text is legible. A site whose `css` sets no token renders on the template's own shadcn defaults, which is a real working plain look rather than a broken one. And **the favicon falls back from the brand accent to the hue hashed from the business name** — driven, not assumed: `normalizeSeeds(undefined)` answers `{theme: null, why: "no seeds"}`, `markGround` answers null, and the mark renders `hsl(264 62% 34%)`. **That is the PRE-2026-08-20 form specifically, and it is the weaker of the two**: swept over all 360 hues the hsl mark bottoms out at **3.55:1** against the OKLCH one's 6.95:1. Still above the 3.0 bar a 32px mark in bold caps has to clear, so it is legible everywhere and no longer matches the site.
- **PER-PAGE COLOURS AND PER-PAGE TYPEFACES ARE NOT LOST, THEY MOVED.** `<body>` carries the route as `data-page` and the `css` field's own description says so, so a stylesheet scopes anything to one page itself. What went is the stored per-page MAP and the machinery deriving readable ink for each scope.
- **`EDIT_FIELDS` STILL NAMES `seeds` AND `fonts`, DELIBERATELY, and that is the opposite of tidy.** `mergeLook` rebuilds its output from that list alone, so a name dropped there **destroys** a stored value on the owner's next unrelated edit rather than merely ignoring it. Kept and unused beats deleted and lossy — the rule `family` has already lived under since 2026-08-20.
- **THE CONTAINER IS UNTOUCHED AND THAT IS A STAGE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT.** `writeTheme`, `writeTokens`, `writePageTokens` and the style parse are all still there and now receive nothing; `writeTheme(null)` returns `{applied:false}` and writes nothing, which is the fall-through the harness already covers. Deleting them means also deleting `site-seeds.mjs` — which `site-identity.mjs` needs for the favicon — so it is its own change with its own verification.
- **A WINDOW-BASED CUT SWALLOWED A LIVE READ, AND A GUARD CAUGHT IT.** `site_lang_strings` sat BETWEEN `site_page_fonts` and `site_style` in the build path's `_meta` loop, so deleting the four dead branches took the translation cache with it — the query went on asking for the row and nothing read it. That is the select-and-drop shape `site-freecss.test.mjs` watches for, and **that guard is what found it**; without the cache a revise re-translates the whole site every time, a Haiku call per language spent on strings already answered.
- **THE SUBSTRING TRAP, IN THE DELETION SCRIPT'S OWN ASSERTIONS.** `"      let priorPageFonts"` (6 spaces) is a SUBSTRING of the edit lane's `"              let priorPageFonts"` (14), so a `count(old) == 1` check saw two and a bare replace could have taken the wrong one. Same class as the RTL sweep's first grep, where `items-center` contains `ms-`. Anchored on the line start.
- **AND MY FIRST ABSENCE GUARD FALSE-ALARMED ON THE TTS VOICE TUNER.** `\n\s+style: ` matched `style: { type: "number", description: "…style exaggeration 0-1…" }` — a completely unrelated feature — which is the false alarm this repo rates strictly worse than the miss. Scoped to the container payloads by BRACE DEPTH instead, and the payloads are identified by what they carry (`worker: true` / `fontFiles:`) rather than by a byte window.
- **36 GUARDS WENT RED AND EVERY ONE ASSERTED THE DELETED POLICY.** 25 were removed with the feature they described; 11 were INVERTED rather than deleted, on the standing precedent — an absence rots silently where a presence goes red. Two floors were lowered rather than dropped (`look.X` reads 5 → 4, the look lane's patch writes 2 → 1) because a scan that stops matching reports a lane with nothing to roll back and passes vacuously.
- **AND ONE NEW DERIVED GUARD HOLDS THE WHOLE PROPERTY: exactly one `_meta` key decides what a site looks like.** Found from the keys themselves rather than a hand-kept list — four dead stores is what a list produces — with the four deleted names asserted by name as well, since a scan that silently stopped matching would pass the derived half. **Proved to fire**: restoring `site_tokens` to one query goes red naming it.
- 4057 tests. **NOT MUTATION-SWEPT and NOT PROVEN LIVE** — the Anthropic account is dry, so no build has run against it.

## THE FOUR WORKED PAGES AND THE CRAFT RULES ARE DELETED — THE MODEL LAYS THE PAGES OUT (2026-08-24, owner's call)

**"we are going to delete most of this, we are gonna give the model freedom to create the pages."** `PAGE_RULES` goes **123,397 → 72,736 characters, 41.1% off the cached block**; 21 rules → 15, **12 sections → 9** (four deleted, `## The gate` added — an earlier draft of this line said "10 → 8" and was wrong at both ends, counted rather than recalled). Same act as deleting the 100 family exemplars and the 500-theme registry, one call further down the pipeline.

- **THE BLOCK SPLITS INTO TWO THINGS THAT FAIL DIFFERENTLY, and separating them is what made the cut decidable.** ~20k of it is API VOCABULARY the model cannot get anywhere else — `useRows` exists and `fetch` does not, `useCreateRow` resolves to `void`, `PublicRow` has no `id`, the managed columns, `useCart`/`useCheckout`, the motion classes, `createFileRoute`. Given freedom there, a model writes `fetch("/api/menu")`, because that is what every React app in its training data does: it compiles, bundles, publishes and 404s for ever. **Deleting that half does not change a build, it stops builds working** — so the owner kept it exactly as it is. The other ~103k is inventory and craft, and that is where the cut is.
- **THE ASYMMETRY WITH THE FREE-CSS CHANGE, stated because it is the reason this needed measuring rather than just doing.** There, a bad answer is an ugly stylesheet. Here it is a compile error, and **there is no repair pass** — one `tsc` failure and the whole site becomes the placeholder, charged. The free-CSS arm is also evidence in the other direction: given a blank page the model wrote **7 rules against the axes' 24**. That was a stylesheet; the equivalent failure here is a thin site rather than an ugly one, and it is unmeasured.
- **THE FOUR REFERENCE PAGES ARE THE ACTUAL CHANGE — 42,698 characters, 34.6% of the block.** `index.tsx` · `book.tsx` · `manage.tsx` · `account.tsx`, four real compiling pages of one barber shop. **The one thing a model reliably does with a worked example is copy it**, which is the whole finding the family-exemplar deletion rests on, and it is what stopped the model laying a page out for the brief in front of it.
- **THEY STAY AS DATA AND ONLY THEIR PRINTING GOES, and that was forced rather than tidy.** `ALWAYS_API_CORE` — the 32 signatures every build gets — is DERIVED from their imports, and **11 of the 32 come from nowhere else in this repo**: `button`, `form`, `select`, `textarea`, `card`, `data-list`, `skeleton`, `hero`, `open-now`, `team-grid`, `availability-grid`. Deleting the array would have shipped a prompt whose signature block omits the primitives every page uses. **The derivation's stated reason changed and the set did not** — it was *"the prompt SHOWS these in use, so the model will copy them"*, and it is now *"these are what a complete compiling site of this kit reaches for"*, which is the better measurement and was true all along. Corrected in the source rather than left as a comment that has quietly stopped being true.
- **THE LINT CALIBRATION IS UNTOUCHED, and it is why the pages are not deleted outright.** They are the only complete, compiling, house-style pages of this kit there are, so they are what the lint's FALSE-ALARM RATE is measured against — a rule that flags one of them is a rule that would flag a correct generated page. That is worth exactly as much now as when the model could see them.
- **THE TEN CRAFT REGIONS: rules 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20, plus `## Every list handles four states`, `## Every form must`, Motion's "WHEN TO REACH FOR THEM" half and `## Definition of done`.** ~9,000 characters of category ordering, one-h1-per-page, no-comments, structured data, per-page `head`, footer contact details, the four list states, the three form musts, when to reach for which motion class, and the copy advice. **The rule kept from `Definition of done` is the one that is a FACT about our pipeline** — `tsc` then `vite`, neither advisory, no second attempt and nothing repairs the output — and it closes on the line that says what the split now is: everything above is what this platform IS; how the site reads and what it says are the model's.
- **WHAT EACH DELETION COSTS IS WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN GLOSSED, because two of them are real.** The h1 rule: a section-built page's title now comes from its first `<h2>` — `pageMeta`'s fallback, which is asserted by DRIVING it, since a source-read for "h2" passes against a file that merely mentions one — so a worse title rather than the home page's. The structured-data rule: **`localBusinessJsonLd`'s argument shape appears NOWHERE else the model can see**, so it will not call it and a shop's hours and address stop reaching a search result as JSON-LD. **That is the safe direction and is why it is cheap to lose**: the failure that rule was written around is a `TS2322` on the HOME page, which salvage refuses to stub, so a wrong call cost the whole site while not writing one costs a richer snippet. Both are asserted from both ends, so putting either rule back has to bring its worked shape with it.
- **THE FOOTER WOULD HAVE GONE BACK TO UNREACHABLE, AND THE FIX IS 250 CHARACTERS INSTEAD OF 1,822.** Rule 20 existed because `contact?: SiteContact` is a type NAME and `COMPONENT_TYPES` is per module — `site-chrome.tsx` imports that type from `site-footer`, so it documents nothing of its own and the signature stopped at a bare name on the ONE component every site uses. Rule 3 correctly tells the model not to invent fields on a bare name, so the slots were unreachable from the signature alone. **`componentApiFor` and `shapeOf` now resolve a type from the component's own module first and then from a platform-wide index** — and **ONLY where the name has exactly one shape kit-wide, measured: 309 of 323 do, 14 do not** (`Activity` is two different objects, `Tier` and `Rule` three each). Those 14 stay bare, because a confidently WRONG shape leads the model into a compile error where a missing one only leaves it cautious — the rule `repairImports` already lives under. **7 components of 2,040 gain a resolution, 766 characters kit-wide, exactly one of them (`site-chrome`) in the cached core.** The discriminating case is asserted: `checkbox-tree` cites `TreeNode` without owning it and must stay unresolved.
- **THE REFERENCE PAGES WERE SUPPRESSING A FALSE ALARM, which only removing them showed.** The hook guard excluded a hook the rules import from somewhere ELSE — derived, and it worked because those pages imported `useState` and `useNavigate`. With no imports left, both read as OURS and would have been reported missing from `rows.ts`: a false alarm on correct code, which this repo rates worse than the miss. Two names now, each with its reason, and **each asserted NOT to be exported by `rows.ts`**, so the day one becomes ours the exclusion goes red rather than hiding it. **The backtick half of that scan finds 21 hooks where the old pair found 16**, so nothing was lost but redundancy.
- **A GUARD CAUGHT ITS OWN DELETION, exactly as its comment predicted.** The paid-table window ended at `NO EXPLANATORY COMMENTS` — the rule that used to follow — and `indexOf` answered -1, which its `from > 0 && to > from` assertion reports as an empty window instead of looping over nothing. That check exists because renumbering once left `slice(-1, -1)` returning the empty string with the whole suite green.
- **TWO GUARDS WOULD HAVE GONE VACUOUS AND ARE REBUILT TO PROVE THEIR OBSERVER IS ALIVE.** The kit-import check ran over an empty set once the worked examples went, so it asserts the ABSENCE and then fires both halves against a fabricated prompt — an invented module (the measured `hero-split` failure) and a real module with unstated props. The rest were replaced by their INVERSE, on the precedent that replaced the repair-pass tests with *"a second call never happens"*: an absence rots silently where a presence goes red, and every one of these is one template literal from coming back.
- **THE COST, MEASURED THROUGH THE REPO'S OWN RATE TABLE: 4 credits saved on a cold build, 1 on a warm one.** ~12,665 fewer tokens on the cached block, and the whole page-generation request goes **128,047 → 75,828 characters**. The saving was never the point and is worth stating so nobody reads it as one.
- **THE SWEEP'S ONE SURVIVOR WAS INERT AND THE TEST WRITTEN TO HOLD IT WAS VACUOUS — seventeenth recorded instance, and the first where I had written both.** Asking the platform index BEFORE the component's own module cannot change any answer: `UNIQUE_TYPES` holds only names with one shape kit-wide, so where it answers it answers the SAME STRING, and where it does not it is `undefined` and falls through. **Measured over all 630,390 (component, type-name) pairs either order can answer: ZERO differ.** So *"own-module always wins, so both Activity components keep their own fields"* passed by reading two components whose answers the mutation could not move.
  - **THE THREE CASES WERE DRIVEN RATHER THAN REASONED, and the wording in the source is what they measured.** The WIDENING alone (`UNIQUE_TYPES` → every name, last one wins — the obvious tidy-up) is caught without the ordering, by the ambiguous-name guard and by `shapeOf`'s: **2 failures**. The ORDER SWAP alone is inert. **Both together: 7 failures**, including the replacement. So the ordering is belt-and-braces TODAY and one edit from load-bearing, and it says exactly that rather than being deleted or credited with something it does not do.
  - **THE REPLACEMENT ASSERTS THE INVARIANT THAT MAKES IT SAFE — no component is ever shown a type shape that is not its own** — swept over all 332 typed modules with a floor of 100 resolutions, since a walk that resolved nothing would report a clean kit. It is the line that goes red if somebody ever removes the other two as redundant.
- 4069 tests (+5), template typechecks, `site build` **233/0** against the real container, **13/13 mutations as expected** with a comment-only control that had to survive and one survivor proved inert by measurement. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against it, so no model has yet laid out a page with nothing to copy, and the Anthropic account is dry as of 2026-08-24 (`page gen eval` printed *"Your credit balance is too low"* and correctly refused to record a 0% compile rate).

## THE DESIGNER DECIDES THE PHOTOGRAPHS NOW (2026-08-23, owner's call)

**"lets move image generator to the designer."** How many pictures a site got was a RULE, and what each one was OF came from a different model call — so the one step that has read the brief AND written the stylesheet had no say in either. `design_schema` gains `images: [{page, describe}]` at property 17, last of all.

- **THE MEASUREMENT THAT SAYS WHERE IT BELONGS: `page-gen.mjs` holds ZERO references to `css`.** The model choosing what the photographs SHOW had never seen the palette — it could not know it was dressing a near-black recording studio. Counted, not inferred: the design tool's only image mentions are an image COLUMN in `tables` (a URL in the database, which is data rather than a picture on a page), the `url()` refusal in `css`, and component NAMES in the alphabetical menu. **The designer could not ask for a photograph and could not say what of.**
- **LAST, PAST `shape`, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE ORDERING ARGUMENT.** A tool's property order is its generation order, so by field 17 the palette is written (9), the pages are chosen (11), the verb is fixed (12), the manifest is picked (13) and every page is arranged band by band (16). *"The hero on `/`"* is a slot this model just placed rather than one it is guessing at — the same reasoning that put `shape` after `components`, one level further out.
- **THE PAGE WRITER STILL PLACES THEM, and splitting it further would be worse.** It writes the JSX, so it writes the token; the designer decides the picture EXISTS and what it shows. Asking the designer to name a component slot means naming one whose props it cannot see.
- **ABSENT IS NOT EMPTY, and that is what makes it safe against every site already published.** Their stored plans predate the field, so reading a missing `images` as "none" would suppress photographs on the next revise of all of them — the `publicView` shape, a rule correct about its own case and wrong about the one beside it. Missing falls through to the derived rule (home page 1, picture-led pages 1 each); `[]` is a site that says no, which a CRM or a terminal-styled site legitimately is.
- **THE BUDGET IS STILL THE LAW.** `budgetFor` answers **0** on a revise of a site that already has photographs, so the declared list is sliced to it — an unbounded one re-buys a set the owner already paid for at ~19 credits each. `imagesAffordable` still runs after generation on the MEASURED cost of this build's model calls, so a declared picture the account cannot pay for is a token nothing buys and the sweep turns it into the theme's own placeholder: exactly what an overflow token already does.
- **THE DIRECTIVE HANDS OVER THE EXACT TOKENS, page by page, and says VERBATIM** — the words inside a token are the prompt an image model is paid to draw, so a word changed is a different picture bought. It also says not to invent an extra one, or the count is advisory and the page writer spends photographs nobody authorised. **A count is not legacy**: `budgetFor` still answers one for every pre-field site, and the edit and addon lanes pass a literal `0`.
- **THE DESIGNER IS SHOWN THE PICTURES IT ALREADY HAS**, as SENTENCES rather than a count — "3 photographs" is nothing a model can return unchanged. Without it a revise re-describes the set on a request about a colour, and the failure is worse than churn: the budget is 0 on such a revise, so what a re-roll produces is **tokens nothing buys and placeholders where bought photographs used to be.** Caught by the derived note guard, which is exactly what it exists for.
- **A PICTURE FOR A PAGE THE SITE HAS NOT GOT IS DROPPED, and one with no description with it.** The token must be written into that page's source for a URL to land anywhere, so a picture declared for a route nobody generated is bought and shown to nobody; and `planImages` already refuses an empty prompt for the stated reason — the same answer belongs one step earlier, where it costs a slot rather than a photograph.
- **THE DECISION IS A FUNCTION BECAUSE A SOURCE-READ COULD NOT HOLD IT.** Written inline in `worker.js`, two mutants survived the wiring guard: **`false && plan.images` still contains the words `plan.images`**, and dropping the bound still leaves `imgBudget` mentioned one clause away. A presence standing in for a property, fourth recorded instance. `imageBrief(plan, budget)` is driven instead, and both mutants die.
- **MY OWN DIRECTIVE'S PROSE SPELLED THE DELIMITERS**, so the round-trip test's extractor matched the EXPLANATION rather than a token — *"the text between `@@IMG:` and `@@`"* parses as a token. Prose containing the thing it describes, which has now bitten a lint, a router guard, an absence check, a scope scan and this. Reworded to "the words inside a token"; the test that caught it stays.
- **THREE GUARDS WENT RED ON CORRECT CHANGES AND ALL THREE WERE POSITION PINS.** `components is last of PLAN_KEYS` — but two plan fields are spliced separately and deliberately later, so the claim is that it is last of the SPREAD. `PLAN_FIELDS` order equals `PLAN_KEYS.filter(k => k !== "shape")` — a hand-written exclusion that went stale the moment a second spliced field existed; derived now. And **`shape is the LAST of required`**, which is this assertion's THIRD wrong form: it was `shape > mode` (a landmark that was another field's spelling), then last-of-required (a claim about POSITION that reads as derived). What each field actually promises is a DEPENDENCY — shape says the pages, the verb and the manifest are decided; `images` says every band is arranged — so a field landing after either cannot falsify it, and only moving one above what it depends on can.
- **+1,282 characters on the tool** (68,995 → 70,277), in the cached block. 19 fields, 12 required.
- 4064 tests, template typechecks, **13/13 mutations as expected** across two sweeps from verified-green baselines, each with a comment-only control that had to survive — and the second sweep exists because three survived the first, every one a gap in my own tests and two of them the wiring layer. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against it, so no designer has yet described a photograph.

## `mode` IS DELETED — LIGHT OR DARK IS A COLOUR, AND COLOUR IS `css` (2026-08-23, owner's call)

**"for the shape and mode, lets delete it, thats part of css."** Half of that was right and half was not, and separating them is the useful part: `mode` really was `css` wearing a second field, and `shape` is not CSS at all — it is the per-page section list handed to page GENERATION, so it is deferred rather than done.

- **IT MADE SENSE WHILE A THEME WAS A NAME, and stopped when that went.** The 500-row registry shipped a DESIGNED dark half per theme, so `mode` chose which of two solved palettes was activated — a genuinely separate decision from the palette itself. The registry left the product on 2026-08-20 and the model writes the stylesheet now, so "make it dark" is: write dark values on `:root`. **The field survived that change and stopped having a job.**
- **AND ITS POSITION SAID SO.** A tool's property order is its generation order; `mode` sat at **16** against `css` at **9**, so its own description — *"the theme already has a dark half drawn for it"* — described a theme the model had written seven fields earlier. It could only ever ratify what `css` had already decided.
- **THE COMMENT DEFENDING IT WAS MEASURABLY FALSE, which is what settled it.** `build-server.mjs` argued the class *"flips every `dark:` utility in the kit, which is why this beats emitting the dark values as `:root`"*. Measured before pulling anything: **ZERO of the 2,112 kit components carry a `dark:` utility.** Nothing in the kit branches on the class, so the whole of dark mode was token values — and token values are the one thing `css` is for.
- **`.dark` STAYS AND IS NOT DEAD, which is the check that had to come before the deletion rather than after.** `theme-toggle.tsx` does `document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", next)`, so a page that renders one lets a VISITOR switch. What went is the BAKED default — the owner's decision — which is now just where the designer put its colours. The two premises that make the toggle work (`@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))` is a CLASS, and `themeCss` emits a DIFFERENT palette under it) are still asserted, because each is one edit from false and neither has any other guard.
- **THE MIGRATION RISK WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: 24 sites, 19 of them from the last week**, all smoke tests. A site published as dark stores its palette under `.dark` and would flip to `:root` on its next publish; with no real customers that is free. It would not have been.
- **REMOVED AT EVERY HOP, because a value computed and dropped is this repo's most-recorded shape.** The tool field, both publish payloads, `EDIT_FIELDS`, `currentStateNote`, `normalizeMode`, the container's `writeSiteBrand` argument and its `SITE_MODE` emission, the template placeholder, `__root.tsx`'s `className`, the router's look clause and the client's `SAY` map. Four of those are asserted as an ABSENCE in one test, since a half-removed feature is a payload argument with nowhere to land.
- **THE DELETION IS ONLY HALF THE CHANGE.** Removing the field without saying where darkness now lives leaves the model unable to answer *"make it dark"* at all — the `publicView` failure, which has cost a whole build twice: a capability conditioned on a fact the model was never given. So the `css` description gained **`:root` IS WHAT THE SITE LOOKS LIKE** — a dark site is dark values there — plus what `.dark` is now for, or the model writes one on every site and ships a second palette nothing can reach. Both halves asserted.
- **THREE GUARDS WENT RED AND ALL THREE WERE LANDMARK PINS ON `mode`.** A `langs` window that ended at `mode: {` reported that the LANGS field had moved when nothing about it had changed — closed by BRACE DEPTH now, because a landmark that is another field's spelling is one the next deletion moves. And `shape is answered LAST` was spelled `shape > mode`, which stopped meaning anything the moment `mode` went; it is **derived** now — shape must be the last of `required` in property order, which is the same claim with no field name in it, and it fires when `shape` is moved above the plan spread.
- **`shape` IS DEFERRED AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING.** It is `{path, sections}` per route, handed to the page-generation call as the layout brief; CSS styles what exists and cannot decide that the home page has a hero then a price list then a map. Deleting it is "let the page writer arrange everything from `purpose` + `pages` + `components`" — which its own description already permits (*"A page you leave out is one the page writer arranges itself"*) — and that is a page-layout decision with a different risk, not a tidy-up.
- **AND A FOURTH GUARD WENT RED IN THE ONE PLACE `npm test` CANNOT SEE, which is the process failure worth recording.** I committed on a green unit suite and a green typecheck with the CONTAINER harness still running, said so, and it came back **232/2**: `site build` drives the real build service and had a five-assertion `mode` block in it — *"the container reports which it drew"* and *"the dark site's document carries the class on `<html>`"* both asserting the deleted behaviour. Nothing in `npm test` runs that file, so a signature change to `writeSiteBrand` is invisible to it by construction. **The count is the tell**: 232 + 2 = 234, the same total as the last green run, so two checks flipped rather than any being lost.
- **BOTH BECAME THEIR INVERSE rather than being deleted**, on the precedent that replaced the repair-pass tests with *"a second call never happens"*: the brand object must report **no** mode, and **no** build may bake a dark class onto `<html>`. An absence rots silently where a presence goes red, and the tidy-up that reintroduces this is one line. **The second build deliberately still SENDS `mode: "dark"`** — a caller somewhere may carry it — so a half-read field is caught as well as a re-applied one.
- **AND MY REPLACEMENT THEN OVER-ASSERTED, which cost one more run and produced the useful measurement.** I demanded the two documents be **byte-identical** and it failed at **equal length** — 3873 vs 3873 — which is the signature of a fixed-width value moving rather than of anything being wrong. The original length-only comparison was DELIBERATE and I had read it as weak.
- **ONE BUILD RENDERED TWICE SEPARATES A PER-BUILD LEAK FROM A PER-REQUEST VALUE COMPLETELY, and that is the general instrument.** It is per-request: TanStack serialises each router match as `{i:"__root__",u:1787486551694,s:"success"}` and `u` is `Date.now()` at render, so two renders of ONE build differ and **no cross-build byte comparison can ever hold**. `\d{10,}` is the narrowest normalisation that works — **checked, not assumed: with it the two are identical, so nothing else moves** — and it cannot hide what the check is for, since a class, a colour, a token and an asset hash (`WQmi5Cd-`, mixed alphanumeric) all survive it.
- **THE PROBE COULD NOT FAIL HONESTLY ON ITS FIRST RUN, for the umpteenth time.** It polled `/health` and counted ANY response as the service being up — and a stale static server from the design mirror was squatting on the port I picked, so it POSTed a build at it and reported a JSON parse error instead of *"wrong server"*. It requires the body to start with `ok ` now.
- **AND A `pgrep -f` WAIT LOOP HUNG ON ITS OWN COMMAND LINE — the `pkill -f` trap inverted, ninth recorded instance.** `until ! pgrep -f "site-build.mjs"` matches the SHELL RUNNING IT, so it can never exit. The kill form takes the harness down; the wait form waits for ever, and both look like the thing being watched misbehaving.
- 4054 tests, template typechecks, **`site build` against the real container**. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against it.

## `ctx.waitUntil` IS THIRTY SECONDS, AND EVERY BUILD THIS PLATFORM HAS EVER RUN SURVIVED ON LUCK (2026-08-23, owner's call)

**"i just want the http connection fix for now, meaning if i close the app the build is still running."** The build leaves the request now: the POST stores the job, sends a message, and waits; a **queue consumer** — a non-HTTP invocation, which Cloudflare guarantees 15 minutes of — is what actually runs it. A dropped connection costs the ANSWER and no longer costs the SITE.

- **THE FINDING THAT CHANGES WHAT THE LAST TEN ENTRIES MEAN, and it is Cloudflare's own documentation rather than an inference.** Two pages, in as many words: `ctx.waitUntil()` *"can extend execution for up to 30 seconds after the response is sent or the client disconnects"*, and *"if any Promises have not settled after 30 seconds, they are canceled."* **Thirty seconds against a six-to-twelve-minute build.** So the 2026-08-22 entry below — *"`ctx.waitUntil` IS THE REASON THERE IS A SITE AT ALL"* — is wrong, and every build that published after a reset published for a different reason.
- **THE REASON THEY SURVIVED IS THAT CLOUDFLARE DID NOT OBSERVE THE DISCONNECT.** A Worker has *"no hard limit on duration … as long as the client remains connected"*, and a reset at a hop between the client and the edge leaves the socket looking connected from our side. **Run 14 ran 300 seconds past its own reset and arm A 332 — both impossible under a 30-second rule**, which is what makes this a measurement rather than a reading of the docs. **Arm C is the case where Cloudflare DID observe it**: cancelled mid-generation, 7 credits spent, a claimed slug, no site, and our own one-hour `AbortSignal` never fired, because a timer inside a dead isolate cannot fire.
- **SO IT FAILS HARDEST ON THE ORDINARY CASE.** Somebody closing the tab is the disconnect Cloudflare is guaranteed to see. Every other entry in this file treats the ~285s reset as the hazard; the hazard was always a customer deciding not to watch.
- **THE ORDER WAS RESOURCE, THEN PLUMBING, THEN TRAFFIC, and it is the process worth keeping.** A binding naming a queue the account does not hold fails the WHOLE deploy — three merges shipped nothing that way on 2026-08-07 — so the deploy CREATES `site-builds` and prints `QUEUE OK` one step before anything reads it; the binding and an ack-everything consumer shipped and were proved to deploy while still unreachable; the build was lifted into `runSiteBuild` and proved **byte-identical, 1,918 lines**; only then did traffic move. Zero deploy risk was taken at any step.
- **THE BODY GOES TO R2 AND THE MESSAGE CARRIES AN ID.** A queue message is capped at **128KB** and a build body reaches **24MB** with attachments — three images and a PDF — so the message is the smallest thing that can name the work.
- **THE JOB HOLDS THE CALLER'S OWN ACCESS TOKEN, and the alternatives are worse rather than the storage being free.** `use_credits` reads `auth.uid()`, so a service key **cannot charge a user at all** — measured against the live function — and the four ledger calls inside the build need a real one. Minting a fresh token in the consumer means a GoTrue admin call plus an email lookup on the one path that has to be reliable: new failure modes bought in exchange for not keeping something we were already sent. It is short-lived by construction (an hour against a build of minutes), it lives under `jobs/`, which nothing serves, and **the consumer deletes it the moment it is read**.
- **NO RETRIES, AND THAT IS A MONEY DECISION.** A retry runs the build FROM THE TOP: a second designer call, a second page-generation call, a second set of photographs — charged to somebody who asked once, and read as a *revise* of the husk the first attempt left, since a half-built site has already claimed its slug. The handler acks every message whatever happened, and `max_retries` is **0** so the isolate-crash path cannot do it either. The guard asserts the ABSENCE, because a well-meaning *"give it another go"* restores the double charge with every other test green. Same argument that removed the repair pass on 2026-08-04.
- **THE FALL-THROUGH NEEDED A REPLAY, AND WITHOUT ONE IT FAILED WORSE THAN THE THING IT FELL BACK FROM.** `enqueueSiteBuild` reads the body to store it and **a request body reads ONCE** — so running the original inline afterwards hands the build an unreadable body and answers *"couldn't read that request"*. `replayRequest` is built by ONE expression used by both the fall-through and the consumer, so the two paths present `runSiteBuild` with the same request. **Two headers and nothing else, measured rather than trimmed by instinct**: with comments blanked the build touches `request` exactly three times — `authUser`, `readJsonBody`, `useQuota` — and all three read only the Authorization header and the body. Copying the rest would carry a stale `content-length` onto a body that has been through `JSON.parse` and back, which `readJsonBody` checks FIRST.
- **EVERY FAILURE OF OURS FALLS THROUGH; NONE OF THEM REFUSES.** The store write, the send — each is infrastructure between the customer and a build they asked for, so the caller runs it inline exactly as before. Degrading costs the disconnect protection for one build; refusing costs the build. And the binding is the switch, so a namespace that goes away degrades to today's behaviour rather than to no builds at all — the shape `SITE_ROUTES` and `SITE_API_CACHE` already ship under.
- **THE WAIT IS BOUNDED BY THE CONSUMER'S CEILING, NOT THE BUILD BUDGET.** Sixteen minutes: the consumer's guaranteed fifteen plus a minute for delivery. Past that no answer is coming, and holding the socket for the two hours `BUILD_BUDGET_MS` allows would be waiting for something that cannot happen. **The mismatch is real and is NOT fixed here** — the owner removed every ceiling on 2026-08-22, every build ever measured finished inside twelve minutes, and a build that genuinely needs more than fifteen needs a different mechanism rather than a bigger number. **On the queue path `raceDeadline` is already over when it is set up** (the poll is awaited inside the hand-off), which is one bound rather than two, and it is said in the source because it reads as live.
- **A STATUS HAS TO SURVIVE THE ENVELOPE AND THE SUCCESS IS THE HALF NOBODY WOULD NOTICE.** `build smoke` and `build-as-owner` both read real HTTP statuses off this route — 402, 409, 422, 503 — so a flattening envelope would break the harnesses that verify it while every success still looked perfect. Asserted per status.
- **THE SWEEP FOUND A REAL GAP IN MY OWN TESTS BY HANGING FOR A QUARTER OF AN HOUR.** The mutant that stores a job and never sends the message leaves the poll waiting its full sixteen minutes — right in production, and in a test it means *"the answer never came"* reads as a hang rather than a failure, on exactly the bug those tests exist to catch. The four tests that reach the wait are bounded at 8s (the happy path answers on the first look with no sleep at all), and the runner bounds each mutant and **reports a hang AS a catch**, which it is.
- **AND `pkill -f` KILLED MY OWN SHELL AGAIN**, seventh recorded instance: the harness wraps a command in a shell whose command line CONTAINS the pattern, so killing the sweep killed the thing running it, at exit 144 with an empty log.
- **TWO GUARDS WENT RED ON CORRECT CHANGES AND BOTH WERE THE SAME OWN-GOAL, TWICE EACH IN ONE HOUR.** `const buildDone = (async () => {` → `const buildDone = ` → `let buildDone;`: two tests pinned each spelling in turn while every property they exist for held. One is anchored on the NAME now; the other on the RACE at both ends — `raceDeadline` is called in exactly one place, so the call it races is the last `runSiteBuild(` above it, which is neither the function's own declaration nor the consumer's `await`ed call. **Both of those come earlier in the file and both would satisfy a bare `indexOf`**, which is the mutation-matches-its-own-declaration trap wearing a caller.
- **AND ONE REAL FINDING FROM A DERIVED GUARD: a `queued` trace mark reached nothing.** `budgetStage` is derived over every mark the build path writes and went red on it — correctly. The producer's recorder never learns a slug (the designer names the site, on the other side), so `makeRecorder` buffers everything it is given and can never flush; the mark was decoration that additionally had to be given a stage for a deadline it cannot reach. Deleted rather than given one.
- 4051 tests (+23), **21/21 mutations as expected across two sweeps** from verified-green baselines, each with a comment-only control that had to survive — and the second sweep exists because three survived the first. Two were real gaps of mine (nothing drove an unusable envelope through the WAIT, only through the module; and the auth gate was held by NOTHING — making it inert still produced a 401 with an empty queue, because `packJob` reads `bu.id` and throws on a null user, which the store's own try catches into the inline fall-through). **The third was my mutation hitting the wrong target**: perl replaced the FIRST `SITES_BUCKET.delete(jobKey(id))`, which is the producer's send-failure cleanup rather than the consumer's — re-run against the consumer's own line, caught. **A mutant applied to the wrong target proves nothing**, recorded here for the third time. **`build-job.mjs` is a pure vocabulary and that is asserted** — no `fetch`, no bucket, no queue — so every decision the two sides must agree on is driven with literals, and the wiring is driven through the REAL router with a fake bucket and a fake queue, because that is the layer twelve dead features lived in. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against it, and what a unit suite structurally cannot show is that Cloudflare really keeps a consumer alive across a real disconnect.

## PROVEN LIVE: THE CONNECTION WAS DESTROYED AT 30 SECONDS AND THE SITE BUILT ITSELF ANYWAY (2026-08-23)

**`smoke-mt5igr76-jdd38.gofarther.app` — a real barber's site, published by a build that spent ELEVEN MINUTES AND FIFTY-EIGHT SECONDS with nothing connected to it.** POST 07:54:03.98, socket destroyed 07:54:34.01 (**30.0s**, `req.destroy` — what closing a tab does), build finished 08:06:41, site 200 at 08:06:47. `done: true`, `total_ms: 748122`, **28 credits**, `at: "pages"`.

- **THE TRACE ROW IS THE PROOF, AND IT IS PROOF FOR A REASON WORTH KNOWING.** `site_builds` is written by the recorder, and **the producer's recorder can never flush** — `makeRecorder` buffers until it has a slug, and the producer never learns one. So a row for this slug can only have been written by the CONSUMER, and `done: true` on it means the consumer ran the build to the end. The site answering 200 is the outcome; the row is who did it.
- **THE DISCONNECT HAD TO BE DELIBERATE, and that is a consequence of the previous fix rather than a contrivance.** `postLong` removed our own 300-second ceiling, so the harness now HOLDS the connection for a whole build and a run left to itself produces no disconnect at all. `SMOKE_CUT_MS` destroys the socket N ms in — inert unless set, strictly a positive number so nothing vaguely truthy can sabotage an ordinary paid run, and its switch is OUT of the workflow now that the proof is in.
- **THE BUILD IS THE LONGEST EVER RECORDED HERE AND THE MARGIN IS THINNER THAN THIS FILE HAS BEEN SAYING.** 12m28s, against a consumer's guaranteed FIFTEEN. `img` alone — the page-generation call — was **502,972ms, 8 minutes 23 seconds**, two thirds of the build; design was 81.1s on Grok, the container 80.2s, the publish 22.8s. Every earlier entry says "every build ever measured finished inside twelve minutes"; that stopped being true on the run that proved the queue.
- **AND THE HARNESS CALLED IT A FAILURE BY SEVEN SECONDS.** It waited twelve minutes from the cut, gave up at 08:06:34, and the build finished at 08:06:41. **A false red on the one check that can prove this feature** — which reads as the queue failing and would have sent the next person into `worker.js` after a bug that is not there. Twelve was not careless (no build had ever taken longer); it was a second estimate that had to be right on its own. It is **sixteen minutes now, taken from the Worker's own `QUEUE_WAIT_MS`** — one number, one meaning.
- **THE INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENT IS WHAT SETTLED IT**, and that is the durable lesson: the run's own verdict said no site, and a `curl` nine seconds later said 200. When a harness reports a negative about something outside itself, check the thing rather than the report.
- **WHAT WAS ALSO PROVED, INCIDENTALLY:** the site is served by its OWN Worker script (`x-site-build: mt5ius1n-gvm4g2`), it is a real app rather than the placeholder (title "Ridgeway Barbers", four real headings, `/book` answering 200), and the whole path — design, Neon provisioning, schema, seed, generation, compile, prerender, publish, script upload — ran with nobody watching.
- **STILL TRUE AND STILL NOT FIXED: `BUILD_BUDGET_MS` IS TWO HOURS AND A CONSUMER HAS FIFTEEN MINUTES.** Nothing today reaches it and this build came within 2.5 minutes of it. A build that genuinely needs longer needs a different mechanism rather than a bigger number, which is the same sentence as before with a much smaller margin under it.
- **The two router checks failed for the recorded reason and nothing else**: `/api/site/route` is Haiku and the Anthropic account is dry (`failed: true`, `cost: 0`). Grok did the design work, which is why the build ran at all.

## `build smoke` DIED AT 300 SECONDS AND THEN DESTROYED THE BUILD IT WAS WATCHING (2026-08-23)

**The first run against the queue failed, and neither cause was the queue.** `UNCAUGHT: fetch failed` at **exactly 300.0s**, mid-build — and one second later the harness's own cleanup tore down the build's Neon project.

- **undici GIVES UP AT 300 SECONDS AND THE FETCH OPTIONS CANNOT RAISE IT.** An `AbortSignal` set longer does not help: the headers timeout fires first. `scripts/build-as-owner.mjs` was given `postLong` (`node:https`, which has no such timeout) months ago for this exact failure; **`build-smoke.mjs` was the one that never was**, and the first build had always died before the revise could reach the same ceiling. Both POSTs use it now.
- **AND THE ABORT IS WORSE THAN IT USED TO BE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT IS NEW.** It used to matter because hanging up KILLED the build. Since the build became a queued job it does not — so what a 300-second abort costs now is that the `finally` deletes the throwaway user, **cascading `site_backends` away and dropping the site's own Neon project while the build is still running**. Measured to the second: fetch failed at 07:04:00, the teardown row for `polished-cake-64431446` was written at 07:04:01. **The harness destroyed the thing it exists to observe** — and the site being 404 afterwards read as the queue failing when the build had got past design and provisioning perfectly well.
- **A DROPPED CONNECTION IS NOW THE MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A REASON TO GIVE UP.** It is the one condition under which this harness can prove the queue at all, and no unit test can reach it — what is under test is whether Cloudflare really keeps a consumer alive with nobody connected. So a reset watches the site for twelve minutes and records `THE BUILD SURVIVED A DROPPED CONNECTION` as a real result. **The slug is ours**, so unlike `build-as-owner` there is nothing to discover: this run sends an explicit one because a name is claimed by whoever builds it first, and that pays off here.
- **WAITING IS ALSO WHAT KEEPS THE TEARDOWN HONEST.** By the time cleanup runs the build is over either way, which is the property the 300-second abort broke.
- **THE RUN ITSELF WAS NOT WASTED, and the evidence is a row nobody would have thought to look for.** `neon_teardown` held `polished-cake-64431446` — and provisioning only runs after `designSiteSchema` RETURNS TABLES, so the design call succeeded and the build was past its first model call. That is what rules out the queue as the cause without spending a second build.
- **THE ANTHROPIC ACCOUNT IS DRY AND IT IS NOT WHAT BLOCKED THIS.** `schema gen eval` printed it in words on the same commit — *"Your credit balance is too low"*, 20 of 20 samples — and it explains both routing failures (`/api/site/route` is Haiku) and nothing else: `DEFAULT_PICKER` is grok, which is why the design call worked. Worth stating because "the account is empty" is the reading this file has reached for four times and it was the wrong one here.
- **TWO OF MY OWN GUARDS SURVIVED THE FIRST SWEEP AND BOTH ARE RECORDED TRAPS.** `/import https from "node:https"/` matched its own **commented-out** form, so deleting the import passed — prose containing the thing it asserts, eighth instance. And the drop-path check windowed 1,200 bytes past the branch into the next block's `ok("build returns 200"`, so demoting the headline to a `console.log` survived — the overlapping-window own-goal, fourth instance. Anchored at line start and on the branch's own close.
- **AND AN EXISTING GUARD WENT RED ON THE CORRECT CHANGE**, pinned to `fetch(` — the transport that was the bug. Re-anchored on the route and the body, with a new guard asserting the property this fix is about: **neither build POST may go through `fetch`**, derived over every post to that route with a floor of two, since a loop over zero matches reports a clean sweep.
- 4053 tests (+2), **13/14 mutations as expected across two sweeps** from verified-green baselines with a comment-only control that had to survive. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — the harness can now observe a disconnect and no run has produced one.

## ARM C: GROK'S PAGES CALL HUNG, AND THE HARNESS THREW AWAY THE ONE THING THAT COULD HAVE WATCHED IT (2026-08-23)

**`lido-cafe` never published.** Same brief, same picker, third arm — and the pages call did not return. The trace sat at the `gen` mark for **35+ minutes** and the site was 404 throughout. **7 credits** (148 → 141), a claimed slug and a live Neon project: the husk shape this file already records for runs 3, 4, 9, 10 and 13.

- **RUN 9's SHAPE EXACTLY, AND THAT IS THE SECOND INSTANCE RATHER THAN A NEW FAILURE.** That one was Arabic on Grok, 25m46s in generation, no answer. The half that worked is identical too: design 76.4s, a Neon project, two tables applied and seeded, **all inside 86 seconds** — so the designer read the brief and answered it, and everything before page generation is proven on the new field.
- **NOTHING OF OURS CAN REFUSE IT ANY MORE, WHICH IS THE COST OF THE CEILING REMOVAL STATED PLAINLY.** `BUILDER_CALL_MS` is an hour and the whole-build budget two, so from outside *"still generating"* and *"the isolate is gone"* are one observation. The trace cannot separate them either — it writes on a MARK, and `gen` is written at the START of generation with `img` closing it, so a stale `gen` is exactly what both look like. **The fix for that is #175 (the build as a job, not a held socket), not another bound.**
- **AND THE HARNESS LOST THE BUILD BEFORE THE BUILD LOST ITSELF, which is the half that was fixable.** The reset at **264.8s** is ordinary — seven instances now — and is survivable BY DESIGN: the script watches the site instead of the socket. It could not, because `OWNER_SLUG` was unset and the designer-chosen name existed **only in the answer the reset destroyed**. Arms A and B rode the identical reset purely because they had been handed explicit names. **So "the designer names the site" and "a reset is survivable" were mutually exclusive**, which is backwards — a customer's build names itself too. The script printed the fix in its own fatal line and exited.
- **`discoverSlug` READS THE CLAIM OFF `site_backends`, which is written at PROVISIONING (~90s in) and therefore already in the database by the time the socket dies.** Two filters and they are the whole correctness argument, asserted apart: the row must belong to **this account** AND have been created at or after **this build's own POST**. Without the window a build that died BEFORE provisioning hands back a site published hours ago — already 200, so the watch reports a **success that did not happen**, the most expensive wrong answer this harness can give. It retries for two minutes and then fails honestly, because a build that never claimed a slug has no address and never will.
- **THE COST QUESTION IS HALF-ANSWERED, AND THE HALF IT ANSWERED IS REAL.** Arm A and arm C were both COLD on the design call, so they compare: **input 20,313 → 18,998** (−1,315, the tool going 84,691 → 69,088 chars) and **output 1,572 → 2,265** (+693, **+44%**). The predicted trade, measured rather than reasoned: a smaller cached input bought with a bigger output, on a provider that prices output at **3× input**. Net **~+$0.0015** on that call — both still round to 7 credits, so at this scale it is a wash and only the DIRECTION is established. **The pages call is where it would bite and is exactly what this run did not produce.** (Arm B's `in: 17` is a warm prefix cache, not a smaller tool — it does not belong in the comparison.)
- **AND THE TWO ARMS' TOTALS NEVER ANSWERED IT EITHER, which is worth saying because 72 vs 49 reads as though they did.** A photograph is ~19 credits of real fal spend and arm A bought a third one; strip it and the arms are ~4 credits apart, inside variance. `img` was **407.9s** on arm A and **361.6s** on arm B — two thirds of each build, and nothing to do with the stylesheet.
- **THE OVERLAPPING-WINDOW OWN-GOAL, FOURTH INSTANCE, IN THE GUARD WRITTEN FOR THIS FIX.** There are TWO `if (!slug)` in a row — the one that triggers the lookup and the one that gives up — and a window opened at the first reaches the second's `fail(` inside 200 characters, so the obvious spelling passed with the fatal deleted. Anchored past the lookup now.
- **AND A MUTATION THAT MATCHED THE FUNCTION'S OWN DECLARATION**, for the umpteenth time: `traceLine(slug)` hits `async function traceLine(slug)` first, so the sweep renamed a parameter and reported a survivor. **A mutant applied to the wrong target proves nothing.** Re-run against `await traceLine(slug)`: caught.
- 4023 tests, **8/8 mutations as expected** with a comment-only control that had to survive. **The site is not fixed and is not meant to be** — the build is gone; what is fixed is that the next reset does not cost the answer.

## FIVE LOOK FIELDS BECAME ONE — THE MODEL WRITES THE STYLESHEET (2026-08-23, owner's call)

**"for the look, the css, we are gonna delete those 5 steps into 1 step, which is gonna be called css, and we are gonna give the model freedom, so with no words, the model is gonna make the css."** `seeds` (three anchor colours), `fonts` (a pairing off a 24-name enum), `style` (29 axes, each with its own selector and property allow-list), `tokens` (24 named colours) and `tokensPage` (a route to scope them to) are gone from `design_schema`. **23 fields → 19, 13 required → 11, and the tool went 84,691 → 69,088 characters — 18% off the cached block.**

- **ARM A IS NOT EVIDENCE AGAINST THIS, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT.** Yesterday's free-CSS arm wrote 7 rules against the axes' 24 and the entry below records it as the axes winning. **That arm kept `seeds`** — so there was still a field asking for the palette, and the palette is exactly what landed. This repo's own words for that shape: *"a hatch beside a full menu is a hatch nobody opens"*, measured on run 14, where two axes had an authored escape hatch beside twenty-three enums and the model reached for neither. With nothing else to answer the question is unavoidable. **Whether that is enough is live and unanswered** — the first build against this field is what settles it.
- **EXISTING SITES ARE UNTOUCHED BY CONSTRUCTION, and that is the whole compatibility story.** Every site published before today stores `site_look.seeds`, `site_look.fonts`, `site_tokens` and `site_style`, and both publish spines still READ and SEND all four on every republish — a typo fix included. **Nothing stopped carrying them; the TOOL stopped asking.** `EDIT_FIELDS` deliberately still names `seeds` and `fonts` for the same reason `family` is still there: `mergeLook` rebuilds its output from that list alone, so a name dropped there strips the value off a live site on its owner's next unrelated edit.
- **THE CONTAINER WRITES IT LAST**, after the theme, the token patch and the per-page scope — so a site with both wears its stored look with the model's rules on top rather than fighting it, and a new site gets them over the template's plain defaults. Proved against a real Tailwind build: the model's `--background` is the LAST one in the compiled sheet and the stored theme's is still there underneath.
- **REPLACED, NEVER MERGED, AND THE ANTI-RE-ROLL GUARANTEE MOVES INTO THE PROMPT.** `mergeTokens` and `mergeStyle` accumulate because a revise names one axis and the rest must survive; a stylesheet is one whole thing, and "merging" two means concatenating and letting later win — which grows without bound and leaves dead rules from every earlier design in a customer's bundle for ever. So the designer is SHOWN the current sheet by `currentStateNote` and told to return it with only the asked-for change made, which is the contract `pagesRequest` already puts on a revise. **A `.slice()` on that note would be worse than the cost it saves**: the model returns the truncated sheet, that answer REPLACES the stored one, and the tail of the design is gone silently on a request about a phone number. `MAX_CSS` bounds it once, at the door, where it refuses rather than destroys.
- **`builder/site-freecss.mjs` READS AND NEVER VALIDATES, which is the opposite of `site-css.mjs` and `site-authored.mjs` and is deliberate.** What it does instead is REPORT, because **every failure this door can produce is silent**: a font we did not fetch renders in a system face, a sheet that sets no token renders the whole kit on shadcn's defaults, a remote `url()` is refused by the published-site CSP with nothing in the page to say so. None throws, none fails a build, and all three look from outside like the model having taste we did not expect.

**AND CHECKING THAT HALF FOUND A LIVE BUG ON EVERY SITE THE PLATFORM HAS EVER PUBLISHED: NO TYPEFACE WAS LOADING AT ALL.** The container assertion *"a family the stylesheet names is really bundled"* went red, and the cause was not the new field.

- **THE NPM IMPORT EMITS THE FILES AND NOT ONE RULE.** `writeFonts` writes `import "@fontsource-variable/lora"` into `src/fonts.ts`, which `routes/__root.tsx` imports. Measured on a real build: all **seven** `lora-*.woff2` land in `dist/client/assets/` and there is **ZERO `@font-face` anywhere** — not in `dist/client`, not in `dist/server`. So the browser has the files and nothing telling it to use them, falls through the stack, and renders the system face. **True of the template's own `geist` default too**, so it is every published site, not a free-CSS problem.
- **IT WAS INVISIBLE FROM EVERY DIRECTION AT ONCE, which is why it lasted.** The build reports `fonts: {heading:"geist", body:"geist", applied:true}`, the `--font-sans` token names the family perfectly, the woff2 assets are in the bucket, and `tsc`, vite, the lint and 4,020 unit tests are all green. Only asking the compiled stylesheet whether a RULE exists can see it — the exact failure shape `site-fonts.mjs`'s own header is written around, and the reason this repo's rule is to assert on the real compiler's output.
- **THE FIX IS `@import "<pkg>";` FROM `styles.css`, and it is a mechanism the template already relies on**: `@import "tw-animate-css"` is an npm CSS package resolved by the same Tailwind resolver. Measured on the same build shape: **7 `@font-face` rules, `font-family:Lora Variable`, `font-weight:400 700`** — the real variable range — every subset, and each `url()` rewritten to its hashed asset. Both families now carry a rule and the asset counts are unchanged, so the two importers resolve to one module.
- **FIRST IN THE FILE, or it does nothing** — an `@import` after any rule is ignored per spec, and `decls.faces` (the fetched families' own `@font-face`) is written into the same string. The guard asserts that ordering as a property, and both mutations die: dropping the imports, and putting them second.
- **SENDING EVERY FAMILY DOWN THE FETCH PATH WAS THE OTHER CANDIDATE AND IS WORSE.** It demonstrably works — a fake `wOF2` blob proved `@font-face{font-family:Cormorant Garamond;src:url(/fonts/cormorant-garamond.woff2)}` reaches the compiled sheet as its first rule — but the Fontsource API hands back **ONE STATIC WEIGHT** for the latin subset, so `font-weight:100 900` on it is a lie and every heading is synthetically bolded. The installed 24 exist precisely to ship the real variable file.
- **THE `fonts.ts` IMPORT STAYS AND IS SAID TO BE BELT-AND-BRACES**, rather than deleted or credited with something it does not do: `__root.tsx` imports the file so it must exist, and the checked-in copy is what lets the template build standalone with a typeface.

- **A `font-family` IS A REQUEST FOR A FILE, NOT A STYLE OPINION — and this is where nearly every typeface now arrives.** `fontsIn` reads the families back out of the sheet, the Worker fetches each, and the container emits the `@font-face` and the npm import. **Resolved against the WHOLE Fontsource catalogue rather than the installed 24**, which the first draft got wrong in the expensive direction: matching only the shortlist reported `Cormorant Garamond` as unhostable while `fetchSiteFonts` fetches it happily — a warning printed to a customer about a typeface that works.
  - **A STACK BEHIND A CUSTOM PROPERTY IS THE COMMON CASE AND THE FIRST DRAFT SKIPPED IT**, on the reasoning that the variable's own declaration would be scanned as a `font-family`. It is not — `--font-sans: "Lora", serif` is a custom property — so the family was named, never matched and never fetched. **It is exactly how the template's own `styles.css` is written**, so it is the shape a model copying it produces. Resolved by REFERENCE (`font-family: var(--x)`) rather than by a naming convention, which would miss `--type-display` and wrongly claim `--font-size`.
  - **A SYSTEM FACE IS SILENT, and that list exists to stop a FALSE ALARM rather than to enable anything.** `font-family: Georgia, serif` is complete, working and deliberate. Measured: 19 of 20 common system faces come back `unknown` from `resolveFont`, so without the list every one would have been reported. `Baskerville` is the exception and is deliberately absent — it resolves to Fontsource's own `baskervville`, which is a better answer than a fallback.
- **ONE PAGE'S OWN LOOK IS WIDER THAN THE FIELD IT REPLACES, NOT LOST.** `tokensPage` scoped a colour or a typeface to one route and refused corners and spacing by name (those were derived at `:root` and could not be scoped). `<body>` carries the route as `data-page`, so raw CSS scopes ANYTHING — and the tool says so, because `data-page` is a stamp of ours that a model has no way to guess. That is the `publicView` failure — a capability conditioned on a fact the model was never given — which has cost this platform a whole build twice.
- **THE DOCKERFILE GUARD CAUGHT A PRODUCTION BREAKER ON ITS FIRST RUN**: `site-freecss.mjs` was not COPYd into the build image, so the build service could not have started. Third time that check has earned its keep.
- **THE EVAL-SCOPE CANARY IS FOUND NOW, NOT PINNED, AND THAT IS THE SECOND TIME IT BROKE THIS WAY.** It named `SITE_STYLE_AXES` as the identifier to withhold — a fact about what the tool happened to contain — so it failed against correct code the moment that name left. It tries every scope name and requires at least one to produce a `ReferenceError`, which also makes the real failure expressible: if NONE does, the check above it is watching nothing whatever it reports.
- **NINE GUARDS WENT RED ON CORRECT CHANGES AND SEVEN WERE ARITY PINS** — `fontCss(pair, written, pageScopes)`, `fontImports(pair, pageScopes)`, `writeFonts(…, payload.pageFonts)`, `fetchSiteFonts(pair, pages = [])`, `concat(tokens, style)`, `!pageTokensMoved && !pageFontsMoved)`, and a rollback pinned to one `for` loop. Every one failed because an honest extra argument or term joined it. **This repo's most repeated own-goal, seven more instances in one change.** And my own new fetch guard hit the OTHER recorded trap on its first run: a bare `fetchSiteFonts(` matched the function's own DECLARATION, so it reported a call site that does not exist.
- **TWELVE GUARDS ASSERTED THE POLICY BEING REVERSED and each was replaced by its INVERSE**, on the precedent that replaced the repair-pass tests with *"a second call never happens"* — because an absence rots silently where a presence goes red. A field quietly restored beside `css` gives the model two ways to decide one look and the container applies BOTH.
- **THE SWEEP FOUND A FIXTURE THAT COULD NOT EXPRESS ITS OWN FAILURE.** `"a{color:red}"` is 12 characters and `MAX_CSS` is 60,000, a multiple of 12 — so a naive `slice(0, MAX_CSS)` landed exactly on a `}` and `endsWith("}")` was true whether or not the rule-boundary search existed at all. A mutant replacing the whole search with `-1` survived. 13 characters now, **with the misalignment asserted** so it cannot go quietly vacuous again, and the mutant dies.
- **AND FIVE REAL GAPS, EVERY ONE OF THEM A GUARD WATCHING THE LAYER BELOW THE BREAK.** Three are the gates that decide whether a look edit happens at all — and `tokens` and `style` are gone from the tool, so `tokensMoved` and `styleMoved` are false on every build there is and `css` is the only thing a look edit can move, which makes those conditions the whole lane. Dropping `!cssMoved` from the no-change gate makes a sheet that really moved read as nothing moved, and `named` is still true, so the lane answers *"Your site already looks like that — nothing to change."*: **the customer's colour change not applied, not published, and reported as already done.** Dropping `!priorCss` from the escalation gate sends every site whose design lives in the stylesheet to a ~27-credit page rewrite that recompiles from the very same sheet. And dropping `|| storedCss` from the BUILD route's `editState` gate hands such a site's revise no name, no stylesheet and no `EDIT_RULE` at all — it designs from scratch, which is the re-roll the anchoring exists to stop.
- **THE OTHER TWO ARE THE FONT CHAIN, AND THEY WERE TOTAL.** Deleting the `extra` loop from `fontCss` or from `fontImports` survived the entire suite — because the chain guard asserts each function is CALLED with `cssFaces`, which is a source-read and stays green while the loop inside does nothing. **`css` is the only route a typeface has now**, so a fetched family got no `@font-face` and an installed one got no package, and both render the fallback while every layer reports success. Driven through the real functions now, the two halves asserted apart because they fail differently, and each fixture asserts it is exercising the source it claims to.
- **TEN OF THE FIRST SWEEP'S THIRTY-ONE MUTANTS NEVER APPLIED, FROM TWO SHELL COLLISIONS, AND ONE OF THE TEN WAS THE CONTROL.** The field separator was `|` and JavaScript is full of `||`; the perl `-e` was double-quoted, so a `"` or a backtick in a pattern terminated the shell string, and a `/` in a replacement terminated the `s///`. **A sweep whose control never applied is a sweep with no control**, which is the state where "everything died" stops being evidence. Re-run with `@@@` as the separator and both halves passed through the ENVIRONMENT into a single-quoted `-e`, so no character in either is special to the shell or to perl: **12 listed, 0 never applied, the control survived as it must** — and three of the four survivors were the real gaps above, which the first run could not have found. A mutant that never applied reports as coverage that is not there — the mirror of the inert-mutant trap this repo has recorded sixteen times.
- 4022 tests and **`site build` 234/0 against the real container**, the largest count that harness has run. The ten free-CSS checks are in it: the model's rules reach the compiled stylesheet, every stored-theme `--background` comes BEFORE the model's, a named family gets a real `@font-face` AND its file beside it, a `body[data-page]` rule survives the compiler, and a build sending no `css` carries none of it while keeping its own typeface. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against it, so no model has written a stylesheet.

## EVERY CEILING CAME OFF, AND THE MODEL WAS ALREADY WRITING ITS OWN CSS (2026-08-22, owner's call)

**"lets do the 2 arms again, with grok, and we gonna delete any timeout there is anywhere, pls, just let the model work."** Five bounds on the build path plus the runner cap, raised past any binding value rather than deleted — so `isCallTimeout`, `raceDeadline`, `capMs` and every derived guard stay standing and only the numbers stop mattering. `BUILDER_CALL_MS` 600000 → 3600000 · `BUILD_BUDGET_MS` 900000 → 7200000 · `CONTAINER_CALL_MS` 600000 → 3600000 · `STEP_TIMEOUT` 150000 → 1800000 · `DISPATCH_CALL_MS` 120000 → 600000 · `timeout-minutes` 30 → 350.

- **THE ~285s WALL IS NOT A WALL, AND FIVE READINGS IN ONE PLACE MADE IT LOOK LIKE ONE.** Arm B's connection held for **549.6s** before `ECONNRESET` — nearly twice every previously recorded reset (286.0 · 285.3 · 274.3 · 291.9 · 264.6). It is a distribution, not a ceiling, and anything designed around 285s is designed around a coincidence. **This file said the reset was "repeatable and not noise" on two readings seven tenths of a second apart; that was true of those two and false as a general claim.**
- **NO CEILING OF OURS HAD EVER FIRED, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A TUNING MISS.** `BUILDER_CALL_MS` and the whole-build deadline are both `setTimeout` **INSIDE the Worker isolate**. Attempt 1 of this experiment was killed by the runner cap at 26m48s and attempt 2 by Cloudflare's reset at 264.6s — both from OUTSIDE, so the timers died with the thing they were bounding. **A bound that lives in the thing being bounded cannot fire when that thing dies**, which is why raising them costs less than the numbers suggest and why backlog #175 (the build as a job rather than a held socket) is still the real fix.
- **THE HARNESS STOPPED DEPENDING ON THE SOCKET, and that is the half that actually produced a URL.** A reset used to be `fail()` here, on reasoning that predates `ctx.waitUntil`: Cloudflare cancels a Worker when its client goes away. **Run 14 refuted it and arm B is the second proof — this time by design rather than by luck**: the reset landed at 549.6s, the script watched the site and the trace instead of exiting, and the build published **32 seconds later**. Under the old code that run would have exited red on a site that was half a minute from existing and already paid for, which is exactly what attempt 2 did an hour earlier.

**AND THEN THE FINDING THAT CHANGES WHAT THE EXPERIMENT MEANS: THE MODEL AUTHORED ITS OWN BACKDROP THROUGH THE 29 AXES.** Arm B's response died with the socket, so the `authored` field was gone — recovered from the served stylesheet instead. Its `body` rule is `linear-gradient(#0000 72%, #98b8bd1a), radial-gradient(90% 55% at 92% -8%, #f5c6a461, #0000 58%), linear-gradient(168deg, #efe4cf, #f1e7d3)`, with a hand-written dark counterpart.

- **FOUR CHECKS, AND THE HEX IS THE ONE THAT DECIDES.** `BACKDROP_LAYERS` and `DECOR_LAYERS` emit **0 hex literals** and **0 percentage-sized radials** between them — measured over both blocks — and arm B's gradients are entirely hex with two percentage ellipses. **oklch SURVIVES elsewhere in the same bundle** (`--scrim: oklch(13.39% .0137 67.26/.72)`), so Lightning CSS did not downconvert. And the `free-css arm` marker is **absent**, which rules out the experimental door entirely: this came through the axes.
- **IT CORRECTS THE RECORD RUN 14 GOT WRONG, AND WITH A BETTER TELL.** That entry reports the authored path as never having fired live, because a named `drift` looked authored once Lightning CSS stripped a redundant `circle` keyword — geometry is a weak signature. **Hex is one no named emitter can produce**, since every option in both tables goes through `css()`, which emits oklch.
- **SO ARM B IS NOT "THE MODEL PICKS FROM 29 MENUS", AND THE COMPARISON HAS TO BE STATED THAT WAY.** The model is already writing raw declarations; what the axes supply is the SELECTOR and the property allow-list. That makes arm A's question far narrower than it was posed: not "can the model write CSS" — it demonstrably does — but **what does removing our selector and our allow-list buy on top of that.**
- Other axes that fired on the same build: `.lucide{stroke-width:1.5px}` (icon), `--scrim` in both modes, `:active` (pressed). No ambient, no view-transition.

**THREE OBSERVERS REPORTED A CLEAN OR EMPTY RESULT WHILE BROKEN, ALL IN ONE SITTING, AND ALL MINE.**

- **`?head_sha=` DOES NOT MATCH AN ABBREVIATED SHA.** The first watch queried `982a0a9` and GitHub answered `total_count: 0` — so it reported nothing for eight minutes while every workflow ran, and "no events" is indistinguishable from "quiet build". Then the replacement was **rate-limited**: GitHub allows 60 unauthenticated calls an hour and a 30-second poll is 120, so throttled bodies parsed to `total undefined` and printed as `missing` — **a rate limit reading as a missing job.** Now: by RUN ID (authoritative), API every three minutes, and the SITE every thirty seconds because it is free and it is the thing that matters.
- **`site_builds.steps` IS AN ARRAY OF `{s, ms}` AND THE NEW TRACE LINE READ IT WITH `Object.keys`**, which on an array yields INDICES — so arm B's whole watch printed `last=19`, `last=21`, `last=22`. Numbers that read like marks and name nothing, in the one line whose entire job is saying WHICH STEP. It reads the row's own `at` column now (written by `rowFor` from the same array, so the two cannot disagree) plus the last three marks with durations, because a name alone does not say whether the build is still moving.
- **AND ONE REAL BUG IN A GUARD'S OWN SCANNER, EXPOSED BY ADDING A COMMENT.** `bare()` in `exit-reason.test.mjs` blanked string literals with `[^'\\]`, which matches a NEWLINE — so one unpaired apostrophe in prose ("the owner's call") opened a string that ran FILE-WIDE to the next one, and `" ".repeat(m.length)` turned every newline between them into a space. **The blanked source came back with fewer lines than the original**, and the guard went red claiming `run()` had stopped delegating to `runStep`. Fixed by blanking whole-line comments FIRST and refusing to let a string cross a newline; **proved it still catches the real bug** by re-pointing `run()` at something else and watching it fail.

**THE HEADLESS BROWSER STILL HAS NO OUTBOUND EGRESS HERE**, re-confirmed: `curl` gets 200 from the same address Chromium answers `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` for. So looking at a published site means mirroring it locally — and a mirror gets two things wrong that have to be handled rather than ignored: no data API (stub `/api/db/*` with `[]` so lists render their EMPTY state rather than an error) and scroll-driven reveals (a `fullPage` capture expands the viewport without scrolling, so every section below the fold stays at `opacity: 0`). **A screenshot from a mirror must say which parts are the mirror**: arm B's empty menu is the stub, and the real site's data API serves seeded rows.

**ARM A PUBLISHED AND THE AXES WON, ON A RULE-LEVEL DIFF RATHER THAN ON TASTE.** `lido-free-a` — same brief, same picker, same ceilings, the 29 axes swapped for one free `css` string. **Arm B carried 24 rules the other did not; arm A carried 7** — and of those 7, four are Tailwind and the palette, one is the type scale, one is shadows switched off, and one is `.lucide{stroke-width:2px}`, **the template's own DEFAULT rather than a choice**. Given a free hand and no slots, the model wrote nothing.

- **THE COMPARISON IS FAIR BECAUSE ARM B'S BACKDROP WAS AUTHORED**, so this is not a menu beating a blank page — it is an authored stylesheet inside our selectors beating an authored stylesheet with no selectors. What the axes supply is the SLOT, what it LANDS ON, and the properties it owns; removing those three things cost everything.
- **AND THE ENUMS WERE ALREADY GONE, WHICH IS WORTH STATING BECAUSE I MISREPORTED IT.** Asked for "the list of 29 axes" I printed the engine's internal option tables, which reads as a menu the model picks from. Measured against the REAL tool instead: **29 axes on the wire, 0 carrying an enum** — every declaration axis is a `type: "string"` telling the model what it lands on and which properties it owns, every ramp a `type: "object"` (`scale` is `{ratio: 1 to 1.6}`), and `backdropCss`/`decorCss` carry no enum either. The names survive ONLY as defaults, because every site published before 2026-08-22 stores one and re-parses it on every publish — deleting them re-styles the platform on somebody's typo fix.
- **THE THREE WIRE ALIASES, folded back at `parseStyle`'s door**: `border`→`borderWeight` (kept apart from the border COLOUR token, which is a different axis a customer can name), `backdrop`→`backdropCss`, `decor`→`decorCss`.
- **SO THE DOOR CAME OUT (owner's call: "We are gonna stick with the axes").** `FREE_CSS_FIELD`, the tool swap, `freeCssArm`, the `css` payload field, `writeFreeCss`, `OWNER_FREE_CSS`, the probe and its workflow — **817 lines deleted against 75 added**. Kept as an ABSENCE rather than only deleted, on the precedent that replaced the repair-pass tests with *"a second call never happens"*: no path may drop `style` out of the tool, **paired with a check that the field is still there**, since the two refusals above pass perfectly against a tool that offers no style at all. Proved to fire by putting the arm back.
- Arm A: **72 credits** (220 → 148), 3 photographs, published 10m21s after the POST, connection reset at **289.3s**. `img(407906ms)` — 6.8 minutes of image models, two thirds of the build.

**AND ONE PRODUCT OBSERVATION WORTH DECIDING ON SEPARATELY: the model wrote TEN picture slots and the budget bought TWO.** Everything else on arm B's home page is a `SafeImage` placeholder. That is correct behaviour — the owner fills them after the build — and it is also what a customer sees on day one, so whether a fifth is the right ratio is a call somebody should make deliberately rather than inherit.

- Arm B: **`lido-axes-b.gofarther.app`** — "The Lido Café", 3 routes, 2 photographs, `page=app`, **49 credits** (269 → 220), published 9m42s after the POST.
- 4019 tests. Three guards asserted the policy being reversed and each kept its LOWER bound — the half that stops a tuning mistake refusing an honest build — losing only the upper, with the decision recorded beside it. `DISPATCH_CALL_MS > 0` stays and says why: `AbortSignal.timeout(0)` aborts on the next tick, indistinguishable from the provider hanging up.

## SIX MORE AXES, 23 → 29, AND EVERY ONE WAS MEASURED ABSENT BEFORE IT WAS BUILT (2026-08-22, owner's call)

**"ok now add the all the axis from the listy you gave me."** Five surfaces the palette and the kit between them left to somebody ELSE — the browser, the operating system, or a flat literal — plus `pressed`, which is the only feedback a phone gets. Nothing here is a taste axis somebody thought of; each is a place where a customer had no say at all, and the count beside it is what was measured first.

- **`pressed` — `hover` IS SWITCHED OFF ON A PHONE AND NOTHING WAS BEHIND IT.** `hoverCss` wraps itself in `@media (hover: hover)` for a real reason (on a touch screen `:hover` STICKS after a tap), and the consequence nobody had followed through is that on the device most visitors to these sites use, the hover state is deliberately dead. Measured: **`:active` in 0 of the 2,112 kit components and 0 of the 329 corpus pages**, and `button.tsx` carries `hover:`, `focus-visible:` and `disabled:` variants and no `active:` at all. **NO MEDIA QUERY HERE, which is the one structural difference from its sibling** — guarding `:active` the way hover is guarded switches off the thing being added.
- **`scrim` — ALL FOUR OVERLAYS WERE `bg-black/80`, HARDCODED.** One flat black behind every dialog, sheet and mobile menu on every site whatever the theme. **IT DARKENS IN BOTH MODES, WHICH IS WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE THE INK**: in light mode the ink IS the dark anchor, in dark mode it is nearly white, so an ink-derived scrim would BRIGHTEN the page behind the panel — renders, compiles, and the only symptom is opening a menu on a dark site lighting the page up. Derived from whichever anchor is DARKER, pulled further toward black, **chroma capped at 0.03** because a scrim covers the whole viewport and a saturated brand at full chroma reads as a coloured filter over the site. Measured over four palettes × both modes: 8 of 8 darken, and the composited result sits at ≤75% of the page's own luminance.
- **`selection` — SET BY 1 OF 2,112 KIT COMPONENTS**, so highlighting text on a generated site showed the BROWSER's blue. **THE ALLOW-LIST IS FOUR PROPERTIES BECAUSE THE SPEC ALLOWS FOUR** — a padding written into that block is not refused by us, it is silently dropped by the browser, which is the one failure shape a validator can prevent. Every option is a **fitted token PAIR** (`--primary`/`--primary-foreground`), never a colour chosen here, so brand-coloured selected text cannot come out unreadable.
- **`controls` — `accent-color` APPEARED 0 TIMES ANYWHERE, against 101 native checkboxes, radios, ranges and progress bars across 85 kit files.** So a form on a barber's site rendered in Windows blue on one visitor's machine and macOS pink on another's.
