One property is the whole mechanism, and the browser picks the checkmark's own colour for contrast, so there is no legibility question to get wrong. `ink` is not redundant: a page of checkboxes in a saturated brand is louder than the brand should be at that size, and that is still the SITE's decision rather than the OS's.
- **`imagery` — the photo treatment, on `SafeImage`'s own `<img>`**, which is the one element every real picture goes through (202 direct uses plus 194 drawn by 20 components that all render through it). **THE PLACEHOLDER IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED**: it is already a duotone wash built from the theme's own tokens, so a grayscale filter over it greys out the one thing on a fresh site that is not grey. **`mix-blend-mode` IS THE ONE EXCLUSION WORTH STATING** — what a blend produces depends entirely on what is behind it, which is unknowable when the block is written, so the model would be choosing a result it cannot see.
- **`link` — 187 PROSE LINKS ACROSS 176 OF THE 324 CORPUS PAGES AND NOT ONE NAMES A COLOUR**, because `lintPages` refuses a page that does. So a link took the body ink and was marked by its underline alone — a real editorial choice, and the only one available. **THE HOOK IS `a.underline`, NEVER A BARE `a`**: that is Tailwind's own utility and therefore exactly the mark the generator already puts on a link it means as prose, where a bare `a` would repaint the nav, the footer, every card that is a link and every button rendered as an anchor. The colour goes through `displayColor` rather than the raw accent, for the reason that function exists — the accent is tuned to CARRY white button text rather than to BE text on paper.

- **NONE OF THE SIX HAS A DEFAULT THAT MOVES AN EXISTING SITE, and that is the rule rather than caution.** `applyStyle` runs on EVERY publish of EVERY site — a text fix, a colour change, a swapped picture — so a live default is the whole platform re-styled by somebody's typo fix. Asserted per axis, as a whole stylesheet, AND against a real compiled bundle, because one emitter defaulting on is invisible in a byte comparison of the other four.
- **TWO NEW HOOKS IN THE KIT, STAMPED IN THE SAME CHANGE THAT NEEDED THEM** — `data-slot="overlay"` on the four overlays and `data-slot="photo"` on `SafeImage`'s `<img>`. The derived `STYLE_TARGETS` guard refuses a target naming a hook nothing carries, which is the dead-axis failure arriving one layer up; and a separate guard asserts the kit really READS `--scrim`, because a token nothing references is the state this template was already in — the `display` axis was dead for exactly that reason.
- **ONE SCRIM DERIVATION, SHARED.** `paletteFor` emits `--scrim` and `scrimCss` re-emits it at another alpha; two copies drift on rounding, and what a drift costs is a scrim whose alpha the axis moved and whose colour it did not.
- **THE PALETTE'S OPACITY CONTRACT GAINED EXACTLY ONE NAMED EXCEPTION rather than being loosened.** `--scrim` is translucent by definition — an opaque one is not a scrim, it is a black rectangle hiding the site — so the guard allows an alpha **for that name only** and still demands opacity of every other colour token. Widening the pattern globally would let an alpha appear on `--foreground` and pass.
- **THREE OF MY OWN CONTAINER ASSERTIONS WERE WRONG AND THE ENGINE WAS RIGHT ALL THREE TIMES.** (1) **Lightning CSS UNQUOTES ATTRIBUTE SELECTORS** — measured, 94 in one bundle, every one `[data-slot=photo]` — so `[data-slot="photo"]` is a spelling the compiler never emits and the axis was reported missing while its rule sat in the sheet. **The `41.17%`-for-`0.4117` class, and that one is here too**: `--scrim` lands as `oklch(9.37% .0087 59.15/.72)`, a percentage where the emitter wrote a fraction. (2) `background-color:#0000` appears 10 times in EVERY build and is **transparent**, not black — a four-digit hex whose last digit is alpha, so the flat-black check was a false alarm on correct code. (3) The KIT emits two of the five shapes itself: `native-select.tsx` carries `selection:bg-primary`, and **Tailwind v4 ships `accent-*` UTILITIES**, so `::selection` and `accent-color` are in every bundle and are byte-identical to our own `brand` option — the control build asks for options the kit cannot produce, and the leak check reads the SELECTOR.
- **AND THAT MEASUREMENT FOUND AN OLDER GUARD THAT COULD NEVER FIRE.** `!/\[data-slot="card"\][^{}]*\{[^{}]*display:\s*none/` — the quoted form, against compiled CSS. A negative assertion matching nothing, green for as long as it existed. Fixed quoting-agnostically **and paired with a check that the card selector is in the bundle at all**, because a negative assertion has to prove its observer is alive first.
- **A FALSE ALARM OF MINE, RECORDED BECAUSE THE FIX GENERALISES.** `test/site-render.test.mjs` asked *"does any overlay file mention `data-slot`"* to hold the claim that this template's overlay TRIGGERS are raw Radix — and went red the moment `data-slot="overlay"` was stamped on the shade BEHIND the panel, which is not a trigger, cannot be clicked, and leaves every sentence in that comment true. It measures the five TRIGGER slots by name now, derived from `OVERLAY_TRIGGERS` itself. **`probeOverlay` is unaffected and it is worth knowing why rather than being lucky**: it finds the panel by `[data-state="open"][data-slot$="-content"]`, and `overlay` does not end in `-content`, so the deliberately-translucent scrim can never be measured AS the panel and reported see-through.
- **AND MY FIRST DRAFT OF THE `pressed` GUARDS WAS WRONG WHILE THE CODE WAS RIGHT** — they set a BARE STRING on the theme (`{ ...theme, pressed: "transform: scale(0.97)" }`) and `authored()` reads `{ css }`, so the value fell through to the named branch and emitted nothing. A fixture that cannot express the shape under test reports a failure that is not there. Driven through the real `readAuthoredAxis` now.
- **A COUNT IN A COMMENT WENT STALE ON THE NEXT CHANGE**, as it always does: the hint guard read *"the other 21 are described by `authoredFieldHint`"* and it is 27. Both ends are already DERIVED from `AXIS_DECLS[a].image` — here and in `worker.js` — so an axis added to either shape lands in the right hint with nothing to remember; only the prose was wrong.
- **THE SWEEP FOUND FIVE GAPS AND EVERY ONE WAS IN MY OWN TESTS RATHER THAN THE CODE.** 17/17 as expected on the re-run, with a comment-only control that had to survive. Worth recording because four of the five are the same shape — **a guard that drives one branch and reads as covering both**: the authored `imagery` selector and the named `pressed` selector were each covered by nothing, because every assertion beside them drove the OTHER path. The `hover: lift` gap this file already records, twice more.
  - **THE HOVER-GUARD CHECK WAS VACUOUS AND IT IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING.** It counted `@media (hover: hover) {` opens against `}` closes in the whole stylesheet before the press rule — and a full theme has thousands of closing braces, so the comparison was true whatever happened. A mutant wrapping the press in the guard — which is the exact bug the axis exists to avoid — survived it. Asked of `pressedCss`'s OWN output now, where "no media query at all" is decidable and cannot be satisfied by something else in the sheet.
  - **THE PROTOTYPE KEY SLIPPED BECAUSE THE JUNK VALUE WAS THE WRONG JUNK.** "An unrecognised name is silence" was driven with `"no-such-option"`, which is genuinely undefined and therefore falsy — so a truthiness check passed it. `SELECTIONS["constructor"]` is `Object.prototype.constructor`, truthy, falls past every named branch and emits the LAST one. All five tables are now driven with five prototype keys each, **paired with a check that the real options still emit**, or the sweep is satisfied by an emitter that has stopped emitting anything.
  - **AND THE CHROMA CAP WAS UNTESTED BECAUSE MY FIXTURES WERE THE UNUSUAL ONES.** Every palette I had written used a near-neutral ink, so the cap never bound. **Measured: it binds on 14 of 16 theme-modes across ordinary dark inks — a plain navy (`#0b1020`) is already over it.** The guard now asserts the cap holds AND that it BOUND on at least 6 of 10, because a cap nothing exercises is protection that reads real and is not — the favicon chroma-cap finding, one file over.
  - **THE SWEEP REFUSED TO RUN AT ALL ON ITS FIRST ATTEMPT, which is it working.** The isolated copy's baseline was red: `render-sandbox.test.mjs` drops privileges to `nobody`, and `nobody` cannot traverse the symlink standing in for `node_modules`. Excluded and **said out loud** — the same exclusion this file already records for the same file — rather than tolerated, because a red baseline measures nothing.
- 4008 tests (+9), template typechecks, **`site build` 224/224** against the real container, **17/17 mutations as expected** with a comment-only control that had to survive. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against any of the six, so no model has authored one; every layer below the model call was driven through the real container.

## THE ENUMS ARE GONE — THE MODEL WRITES ITS OWN CSS ON ALL 23 AXES (2026-08-22, owner's call)

**"i thought for all of them it was gonna be authored dude, and no names, i just want the model to write its own css cmon, lets make it no name."** Two axes gained an authored escape hatch on 2026-08-22 morning; this is that hatch on every one of them, and the names are gone from the wire.

- **RUN 14 IS WHY THE HATCH ALONE WAS NOT ENOUGH, and it is a correction of what this file said hours earlier.** I reported that build as proof option (b) had fired live. **It had not.** The `radial-gradient(40rem at 24% 28%, …)` I read as an authored backdrop is `ambientCss` emitting the named option `drift` — two things hid it: **Lightning CSS strips a redundant `circle` keyword** (measured: `radial-gradient(40rem circle at 24% 28%, …)` compiles to exactly the shipped form — the `41.17%`-for-`0.4117` class, third instance, walked into while watching for it), and the emitter's own geometry table is `[["40rem","24%","28%"],["34rem","78%","18%"]]` at `38s`, which is `drift` to the digit. `body`'s `background-image` on that site carries **one SVG texture and zero gradients**, so the `backdrop` axis was never set. **The model authored NOTHING on the style axes**: it had the hatch on two and picked names on both. A hatch beside a full menu is a hatch nobody opens.
- **THE AXES ARE TWO SHAPES AND FORCING THEM INTO ONE WOULD BE A LIE.** Fourteen ARE a declaration block — `hover: lift` is `transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: …` inside `@media (hover: hover)`, and the name is the only thing between the model and writing that. Nine are NOT: `scale` is a ratio eight tokens derive from, `tracking` is six per-size steps, `motion` is a duration and an easing. There is no declaration to write there, so authoring means **writing the numbers the emitter reads**, which is what the option table already holds. Both are "author it rather than choose it".
- **WE OWN THE SELECTOR, THE MODEL OWNS THE DECLARATIONS — `site-css.mjs`'s argument generalised exactly.** Every emitter already owned its selector and its guard; what differs between its options is only what is inside. So a model writing RULES is never on the table: it writes declarations, `readDecls` parses them into pairs, and **we RE-EMIT them**, which means the bytes in a customer's stylesheet were assembled here. A value carrying `;` or `}` is refused rather than escaped — there is no correct escape for arbitrary text in a CSS value.
- **WHAT THE ENUM WAS BUYING, AND WHAT REPLACES IT.** Its own comment said the enum made an option the engine would refuse IMPOSSIBLE rather than merely dropped. That cannot survive — "any CSS" has no enumerable domain — so it is replaced rather than abandoned: **the guarantee moves from "cannot be said" to "cannot be said and reach the page"**, which is the rule `site-tokens.mjs` already lives under (*the notation exists BECAUSE it has a parser*). The names are gone from the WIRE and still standing behind it as defaults, asserted — an axis with no options left is one where a refused answer degrades to nothing at all.
- **THE PROPERTY ALLOW-LIST IS PER AXIS AND IS NOT A LIST OF LOOKS.** The objection was to picking from `fine | regular | heavy`; it was not to being unable to write `display: none` on a card. That one blanks every list on the site, `position: fixed` on a section pins the page, `content:` is page copy arriving through a field nobody reviews — none is an injection and all three publish green. An axis that owns `border-radius` can write ANY radius.
- **EVERY GUARD STAYS OURS, and each is a failure invisible on the machine that publishes the site.** `@media (hover: hover)` (on a touch screen `:hover` STICKS after a tap); `:focus-visible` and never `:focus` (a mouse click on a plain `:focus` leaves a ring behind); reveal's `@supports` + `no-preference` pair (the opacity-0 start exists only inside both, so no support means the section is simply visible); the transition's reduced-motion block SUPPRESSING rather than omitting (dropping our rule leaves the browser's own cross-fade, so less-motion gets MORE); ambient's `pointer-events: none` (without it a fixed full-viewport layer swallows every click); display's `:not(:where(.bg-primary *))` (the one place this can make text unreadable).
- **HOVER PICKS ITS SELECTOR FROM WHAT THE BLOCK DOES** — the rule already in the source generalised rather than dropped. A block that MOVES something reaches buttons and cards only (a raised input box reads as a fault, a badge is a label); one that only recolours reaches everything reactive. Asking the model to know that would be a rule it eventually forgets.
- **THE TOOL GOT SMALLER, MEASURED: 122,556 → 82,651 characters, ~33% off the cached block.** The 23 labelled enums were far larger than the descriptions replacing them. What the labels were CARRYING went with them (`icon: fine` read *"drawn thin — jeweller, gallery, tailoring"*, a whole brief in six words), so the hint says what the axis IS, what the declarations LAND ON, and which properties it owns — all derived from the engine's tables. **The selector is the half that decides whether the answer is any good**: a hover state written blind is a guess about whether it applies to the button or the card.
- **AUTHORED IS DECIDED BY SHAPE, NOT BY FIELD NAME, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT SAFE TO DEPLOY.** Every site already published stores names and re-parses them on EVERY publish; reading a bare string as CSS would refuse all of them and each axis would fall back to the default on the customer's next unrelated edit — **the whole platform re-styled by a typo fix, reported as a success**. So a string that IS one of that axis's own options is a name and anything else is a block, unambiguous because a declaration needs a colon.
- **SHADOW NARROWS AND SAYS SO**: the named options carry a geometry table per Tailwind step and one authored block cannot express five, so the steps stop differing on a site that authors one.
- **FIVE BUGS FOUND BY DRIVING RATHER THAN READING, and three of them predate this work.** **THREE PROTOTYPE-KEY BUGS IN `site-theme.mjs`** — `SHADOW_GEOMETRY["constructor"]` is truthy so `!geo` is false and `geo[s].map` throws; `DECOR_LAYERS` and `BACKDROP_LAYERS` are truthy and then CALLED, returning something not iterable. Latent (`parseStyle` refuses an unknown option first) and fixed because that guarantee lives in another module. The bug that shipped once in the Stripe plan lookup and again in `resolveTheme`; `motionCss` already guarded against it and would have **lost the guard to a shared helper that did not**. Plus **the unit was shared and is per field** (with a rem default, `border: {width: 2}` emits a 32-pixel border on every element, compiles, publishes, and looks like a bug in the kit) and **a declaration block accepted an ARRAY** (`String(["transform: none"])` — the coercion this repo has shipped three times).
- **AND THE WIRING GAP, CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED.** `applyStyle` put authored values in a `theme.authored` BAG and the emitters read `theme.<axis>`. `worldCss` reads the bag (it composites two modes and needs both together); every other emitter reads the axis. **A value reaching only one of them is the failure this repo has recorded twelve times** — every layer correct, one hop cut, the build succeeds and the look is silently unapplied.
- **THREE GUARDS WENT RED AND EVERY ONE WAS RIGHT TO.** `api-auth`'s schema walk — the **SIXTH** time that stand-in has been too simple, and its own comment states the rule it missed (*"bind for real anything that IS a schema and anything that DECIDES one"*); it failed LOUDLY, which is the good direction. And two `site-style` guards asserting the enum policy that just changed, one of them pinned to `SITE_AUTHORED_AXES.map((a) => [a + "Css"` — a spelling true of the two-axis shape that says nothing about the property. **This repo's most repeated own-goal, twice more.** The Dockerfile guard also caught the new module missing from the build image, which is a build service that cannot start rather than a failed test.
- 3992 tests. All 23 axes move the stylesheet when authored, every stored name still parses and still emits, and a site that authors nothing is byte-identical.

## RUN 14: THE SITE PUBLISHED FIVE MINUTES AFTER ITS CONNECTION DIED (2026-08-22)

**`pierhead-lido.gofarther.app` is live, and the run refutes the hang theory the two entries below it were written around.** POST 08:14:30, `ECONNRESET` at **291.9s**, and the build carried on and published at **08:24:30** — `done: true, page: "app", ok: true, total_ms 592460`. 110 credits (395 → 285), two photographs bought and placed, five routes, served by its own Worker (`x-site-build: mt441l11-56n5gz`).

- **NOTHING WAS EVER HUNG, and the four new marks are what proved it.** The void between `fonts` and `container` is now a breakdown: **design 48.8s · Grok writing the pages 6m31s · photographs 32.6s · container 96.3s · publish 13.8s.** The pages call RETURNED. `BUILDER_CALL_MS` was right not to fire — 391s is comfortably inside its 600s — and the whole-build deadline never fired either, because there was nothing to refuse.
- **SO THE FAULT IS ONE NUMBER: the connection dies at ~290s and a Grok build of this brief needs ~590.** Four instances now — 286.0s · 285.3s · 274.3s · **291.9s** — and this is the first where we can see what the build was doing at the moment it died: **still generating pages.** Run 13's 26.5 minutes of silence was the same slow call with a socket that happened not to reset, and its trace stopped at `fonts` only because `gen` did not exist yet.
- **`ctx.waitUntil` IS THE REASON THERE IS A SITE AT ALL, and this is its first instrumented proof.** Run 8 published after its client was killed and that was luck; here the row records the build walking through `img`, `compile`, `container` and `pages` with no client attached to any of it. The reset cost the ANSWER and nothing else. — **CORRECTED 2026-08-23 AND KEPT AS WRITTEN, because the observation is right and the attribution is not.** `ctx.waitUntil` is documented as **thirty seconds**; this build ran 300 seconds past its own reset, which that cannot explain. What kept it alive is that Cloudflare did not OBSERVE the disconnect — a Worker has no duration limit while the client looks connected — so it was luck here too, of a kind that fails on the one disconnect Cloudflare always sees: somebody closing the tab. See the queue entry at the top.
- **WHICH MEANS THE BOUNDS WERE THE WRONG LAYER, and that is worth stating plainly rather than hiding.** A fifteen-minute budget cannot help a request the network abandons at five. Both fixes were still right to build — the marks are the only reason any of this is known — but the thing that decides whether a customer gets an answer is that **the answer must not depend on the socket.**
- **AND A REAL CUSTOMER HAS EXACTLY THIS PROBLEM, unmeasured but structural.** `public/chat.js` posts to the same route from a browser. A Grok build of this size cannot answer in-request, so the customer sees a dead connection while the site publishes — and there is **no server-side list of a user's sites**, so a client that never learned the slug cannot find what it just paid for. The residue this file already recorded as a decision is now the ordinary outcome rather than an edge case.
- **THE NEXT STEP IS THE JOB MODEL, and most of it exists.** Return a build id immediately, let `waitUntil` do the work, poll `site_builds` for progress — the row is live, the marks are meaningful, and `readReactStream` in the client has handled `phase`/`agent`/`image`/`code`/`done`/`error` since before the React engine shipped. What is missing is a status route and the client change. Owner's call, because it changes what a build feels like.
- **ONE MORE UNBOUNDED AWAIT FOUND AND FIXED ON THE WAY, by elimination rather than by guessing.** `uploadSiteWorker` PUT the site's whole packaged script to the Cloudflare API with no signal; `deleteSiteWorker` the same. Bounded at `DISPATCH_CALL_MS`. **Explicitly NOT run 13's hang** — `putSiteWorker` runs after the `og` mark and that build stopped at `fonts`. Every other await between `fonts` and `container` was checked and is bounded: the pages call (600s), each photograph (150s, parallel), the container (composed), the ledger RPCs (10s), and the translation loop runs zero times on a build because the build path deliberately sends no languages.
- 3925 tests, 10/10 mutations as expected with a comment-only control that survived — two caught by HANGING, which is a catch.

## RUN 13: THE BUDGET WAS CORRECT AND THE BUILD RAN 26.5 MINUTES ANYWAY (2026-08-22)

**Every bound the entry below describes shipped, was threaded correctly, and is proved by a derived guard — and the build still answered nothing.** POST at 07:25:39, killed by the runner's cap at 07:52:11, `lantern-lido` 404. The ledger moved **406 → 398**: the Grok schema call settled at eight credits and the pages call was never charged.

- **THE ARITHMETIC SAID IT HAD TO ANSWER BY MINUTE FIFTEEN, and that is what makes this a finding rather than another failed build.** The trace records `fonts` at 79s, so the pages call was bounded at `capMs(600000)` = 600s and had to abort by t=679s; the container then gets what is left; the whole thing is refused at t=900s. Six of those minutes were never used. **So the hang is in an await that has NO SIGNAL, because nobody put one there.**
- **AND THAT IS THE GENERAL LESSON, not a missing entry on a list.** A per-call cap can only ever bound the calls somebody thought of. The R2 writes, the Supabase RPCs, `fetchSiteFonts` and whatever is added next are each **one forgotten `signal:` away** from being the next twenty-six minutes of silence — and the failure is silent by construction, because an await nobody bounded is an await nobody is watching.
- **ITS OWN TRACE COULD NOT SAY WHERE, ON THE RUN BUILT TO SAY WHERE.** `site_builds` held **eighteen marks in the first eighty seconds and then nothing**: `auth 157 · body 0 · gate 478 · design 62068 · owner 328 · normalize 0 · prov:project 5501 · prov:database 819 · prov:auth 1580 · prov:data_api 1571 · prov:record 156 · prov:route 195 · schema 5043 · jobs 318 · seed 848 · merge 231 · fonts 0`. Between `fonts` and the response there was ONE unbroken void covering generation, the photographs, the typecheck, vite, the prerender and the render check.
  - **THE GAP WAS KNOWN AND WRITTEN DOWN, AS A TIMING PROBLEM.** The `container` mark's own comment says it *"is the first one since `fonts` and its delta covers generate + typecheck + vite + prerender + render"* — so it closed the SPAN rather than splitting it. Right for attributing time; useless for locating a hang. **The instrumentation was dense exactly where nothing goes wrong.**

**TWO FIXES, and the first is the one that generalises.**

- **THE ROUTE RACES THE BUILD AGAINST ITS OWN DEADLINE — ONE race, at the top.** `raceDeadline(buildDone, { ms: budget.remainingMs(), onExpire })`. That bounds work it knows nothing about, **including awaits nobody has thought of yet**, which is the only shape that cannot be incomplete. The per-call caps stay — they give each step a sensible ceiling and they fail with a diagnosis — but the customer's answer no longer depends on the list being exhaustive.
  - **THE BUILD IS NOT CANCELLED, deliberately.** It is already on `ctx.waitUntil`, so it keeps running and may still publish — strictly better than abandoning work that was minutes from finishing. **What is bounded is the WAIT, not the work.**
  - **IT IS A `step`, NEVER A `finish`.** `finish` CLOSES the recorder, so the row would say "deadline" for ever even on a build that published two minutes later. The record has to end up saying what really happened, and the real finish is what should write it — so `done` stays false, which is true.
  - **SO THE NOTE SAYS NOTHING ABOUT MONEY**, exactly as `budgetNote` already refuses to. A build that publishes after this answer is charged after it, and a sentence promising a refund the ledger then does not make is the worse of the two lies.
  - **A BROKEN `onExpire` DEGRADES TO NO DEADLINE, never to a 500.** Resolving with the throw turns every slow build into an error the customer cannot act on; leaving the race to the work restores precisely the behaviour of not having a deadline, which costs nothing that was not already being paid.
- **FOUR MARKS SPLIT THE VOID: `gen` · `img` · `compile` · `container`.** The page model, the image models, the container, the publish — **each names a DIFFERENT provider and a different fix**, where before all four wore one silence. `budgetStage(steps)` maps a trace step to the three words the customer-facing sentence speaks, and **walks BACKWARDS to the last name it knows** rather than reading only the final step: the build path is exactly the file that grows new marks, and a default would tell somebody with a live database that nothing was set up. Falling back to the last RECOGNISED step is the honest floor — "at least this far" is always true.
- **THE DERIVED GUARD FOUND TWO GAPS IN MY OWN TABLE ON ITS FIRST RUN** — `pages` (real: the build's last mark had no stage) and `route` (a **false alarm**: `ensureSiteBackend` reports through `(n) => tr.at("prov:" + n)`, so it reaches the trace as `prov:route`, which the prefix rule already answers). The scan reads the literal and the trace holds the prefixed name; scoped to `buildAndPublishPages`, whose marks are passed through unprefixed. A false alarm on correct code is worse than the miss.
- **THE HOIST IS WHAT MAKES THE RACE POSSIBLE AT ALL, and it is guarded as a scope fact.** `rec`/`tr`/`budget` were the wrapper's first three statements — fine for the build and useless for the thing that has to answer when the build does not, since `Promise.race` needs them in the same scope as the promise it races. Moved back inside, the route stops compiling, which is the good failure; the bad one is somebody tidying them back in and reaching for a side channel.
- **TWO EXISTING GUARDS WENT RED ON CORRECT CHANGES, both pinned to a spelling, and one of them one line below a comment warning about exactly that.** `return buildDone;` matched character for character (the property is that the return names the build and does NOT carry the swallow), and `images: (pages, { balance, reserve }) => buySitePhotos(` likewise, under a comment reading *"ANCHORED ON THE DECISION, NOT ITS SPELLING — which is what the comment already claimed while pinning it character for character"*. **This repo's most repeated own-goal, twice more.**
- **AND THE SWEEP'S FIRST RUN WEDGED ON ITS OWN FIRST MUTANT**, because making the race inert leaves a test awaiting a promise that never settles — a hang rather than a failure. The runner bounds each mutant and **reports a hang AS a catch**, which it is: a mutation that makes the suite never finish is not a survivor.
- 3922 tests. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — run 14 is the measurement, and it is the first build that cannot be silent: it publishes, or it is refused at fifteen minutes naming its stage, or its row names the exact mark it died on.

## THE BUILD WAS NEVER BOUNDED, AND THE AUDIT DID NOT BREAK IT (2026-08-22)

**Five builds in a row died without answering, and the working theory — "it used to work before the audit" — was REFUTED by measurement rather than argued down.** What was actually wrong is that a build had exactly two bounds on it, both on model calls, and nothing at all on the rest.

- **THE AUDIT WINDOW ADDS NO WORK TO PAGE GENERATION, and it was proved four ways.** The tree was exported at each revision and the REAL `pagesRequest` imported from each: the request is **128,581 bytes at `793b445` (the last good build) and 128,581 bytes at `0380390` (the first failure)** — zero growth, +306 bytes since run 6. Every module governing the build path is **byte-identical** across the window (`page-gen.mjs`, `publish-pages.mjs`, `site-images.mjs`, `build-server.mjs`, `Dockerfile`, `site-langs.mjs`, `site-translate.mjs`, `site-theme.mjs`, `wrangler.jsonc`, fifteen more). The `generate` dep (1,142 bytes) and the **`compile` dep (9,163 bytes — the translation loop AND the container fetch)** are byte-identical. `generateSitePages` and `designSiteSchema` are byte-identical. A comment-stripped diff of the whole of `worker.js` is 179 added code lines, and **every one lands either before the design call — which demonstrably succeeded every time — or after the container returns.**
- **THE BILINGUAL HAIKU CALL WAS THE HEADLINE SUSPECT AND IT IS NOT NEW.** `4a07518`'s title is *"every bilingual publish spent Haiku the ledger never saw"* and what it changed is **billing only**: `git show 793b445:worker.js` already has the identical translation loop, and `translateStrings` goes through `anthropicMessages`, which is bounded at 20s. Every `langUsage` call site it touched is an EDIT lane.
- **AND TWO OF MY OWN PREMISES WERE WRONG, which is why the theory survived as long as it did.** Run 8 — the "last successful build" — was **itself killed by its own 15-minute CI cap at 11m58s** and published server-side afterwards; its own workflow file records it. So the series is **378s (run 6) → 507s (run 7) → >718s (run 8) → failures**, and **the climb entirely predates the window.** The ~285s `ECONNRESET` predates it too: runs 3 and 4 died at 301s and 286.0s *fourteen hours before* `793b445`. And the language theory was already dead before run 11 refuted it — **run 7 was Arabic, on Grok, and published at 507s.**
- **SO THE REAL FINDING IS AN ABSENCE: the container fetch was UNBOUNDED on both publish spines** (`worker.js`'s build path and `recompileAndPublish`), and had been since it was written. `BUILDER_CALL_MS` bounds the two MODEL calls; once the model answered, **nothing anywhere could stop a build.** Run 9's 25m46s and run 12's 26.9 minutes are equally consistent with a hung Grok call and a hung container, and nothing in the response could tell them apart, because both were unbounded awaits.
- **IT IS WORSE THAN ONE BUILD, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES IT URGENT.** `getContainer(env.SITE_BUILD_CONTAINER)` is called **with no id** and the build service is `oneAtATime` **for the whole platform** — so a wedged run does not stall one customer, it queues **every other build behind it**, on a fetch that also could not time out.

**FOUR FIXES, and each closes a distinct half of the failure.**

- **THE BUILD SURVIVES THE CLIENT.** Cloudflare cancels a Worker when its client disconnects, and the build route runs for minutes — so every reset killed the build in flight and left a claimed slug, a live Neon project, a settled schema charge and no site. The whole build block is now an async IIFE registered on `ctx.waitUntil`, so a reset costs the ANSWER and no longer costs the SITE. **Run 8 already proves the mechanism works**: it published server-side after its client was killed — that was luck, and it is now the design. Driven through the real router rather than read, because a source-read for `waitUntil(` is satisfied by any of the other twenty-eight calls in the file.
- **`builder/build-budget.mjs` — ONE BUDGET FOR THE BUILD, not one per call.** Fifteen minutes, and the arithmetic is why a per-call bound could never work: design 600s + provision 40s + pages 600s + container ~500s is **~29 minutes with no hang anywhere**, against a 30-minute runner cap. There is no single call to refuse. `capMs(cap)` hands back the SOONER of a call's own ceiling and what is left, so the bounds **compose rather than stack** — a pages call starting at minute fourteen gets sixty seconds, not another ten minutes. **Never zero**: `AbortSignal.timeout(0)` aborts on the next tick, indistinguishable from the provider hanging up, which is the exact confusion `isCallTimeout` exists to end. A nonsense budget is the DEFAULT and a clock that throws reads as NO time elapsed — the fail-SAFE direction here is the opposite of the usual one, because this module is not what the customer paid for and refusing a healthy build is the more expensive mistake.
- **`CONTAINER_CALL_MS` — the last unbounded await.** Ten minutes, ~2.3x the measured 261s container slice, composed with the budget on the build path and flat on the cheap-edit spine (which has no build clock: seven edit lanes and the rebuild drain reach it). Guarded as a DERIVED property over every container fetch, so a third spine is covered without anybody remembering the file.
- **`builder/build-record.mjs` — the trace is written down WHILE the build runs.** `makeTrace` handed its account back on the RESPONSE, which is the one thing a failing build never produces: for all five, the trace existed, was correct, and was lost — and "which step was it in" was the one question nothing could answer. `makeTrace` grew an `onStep` observer, and the route upserts to a Supabase `site_builds` row (slug PK, RLS on with NO policies, service-key only, `uid` cascading with the account). **One row per SLUG, so the table is bounded by sites rather than by builds**; a row left at `done: false` never reached the end and its last step says how far it got. It **coalesces** — only the latest snapshot is ever in flight, so ~15 marks cost round trips bounded by how fast Supabase answers rather than by how many steps a build has — and it **carries no secret by construction**, because a trace step is a NAME and finite NUMBERS and `makeTrace` has deliberately no way to attach free text.

**AND THE BUGS FOUND ON THE WAY, every one by measuring rather than reading.**

- **THE BUDGET ON `req` WOULD HAVE 400'd EVERY ANTHROPIC BUILD.** The first draft set `req.budget = budget` in both callers, which reads perfectly — and `callBuilderModel`'s Anthropic branch sends `JSON.stringify(req)`, so it would have gone out as `"budget":{"totalMs":900000}`, an unknown top-level field that API refuses. **The xAI branch would have been fine** (`toXaiRequest` names the fields it sends), so a Grok test run would have passed clean and the failure would have arrived live on the other provider. It is a third ARGUMENT now, asserted as an absence.
- **THE RECORDER BUILT ITS ROW AT STEP TIME, so the whole buffered prologue captured `slug: null`** — flushed as a row with no key, dropped by the writer, and lost exactly as if it had never been held, which is the one thing buffering exists to prevent. Caught by the first test that drove it; the row is built at pump time now, with the slug in hand.
- **MY OWN COMMENT STRIPPER ATE THE URLs.** `replace(/\/\/[^\n]*/g, …)` blanks from `//build/build` onward, so the container-bound scan found **ZERO fetches and reported a clean sweep over nothing** — on its first run. Whole-line comments only, which is the rule `site-locale.mjs`'s guard already lives under.
- **FIVE GUARDS WENT RED ON A CORRECT CHANGE and every one was pinned to an ARGUMENT LIST rather than a property** — `callBuilderModel(env, req)` twice, `designSiteSchema(…, attached.blocks)`, the `files = []` default, and `AbortSignal.timeout(BUILDER_CALL_MS)` matched as a spelling. All re-anchored; the timeout one now RESOLVES its bound to its definition rather than matching the expression, the trick the view-transition work already needed for a minified router flag.
- **AND MY REPLACEMENTS HAD THE FLAT-SCAN BUG, in the guards written to fix a spelling pin.** `\(([^)]*)\)` stops at the `(` inside `model = modelsFor().design`, so the signature read four parameters short — failed on its first run, which is the guard working, and it is the **fifth** time this repo has written a flat scan where a depth-aware one was needed.
- **AN INTERRUPTED SWEEP LEFT A LIVE MUTANT**, in the isolated copy — which is exactly why the sweep runs in `git archive HEAD` with a symlinked `node_modules` rather than in the real tree. Cause: `node --test` **consumed the mutation heredoc from stdin**, so the loop ran a truncated list and the `.orig` restores went out of step. `< /dev/null` on the runner.
- 3914 tests, **22/22 mutations as expected across three sweeps** from verified-green baselines, with a comment-only control that had to survive. **FIVE REAL GAPS, and every one was the same shape — the plumbing asserted and the CONNECTION not.** The route omitting `budget` from the design call; `const callMs = BUILDER_CALL_MS` computing the composed bound and ignoring it; the fetch bounded by `BUILDER_CALL_MS` directly, which satisfies the per-call-ceiling guard completely while throwing the composition away; and `finish`'s write not being held, invisible because a STEP write is held too and `held.length >= 1` was satisfied by the wrong one. **A budget threaded through four functions and discarded at the last line passes every check that looks at the threading.**
- **NOT PROVEN LIVE.** No build has run against any of it.

Zephyr — an AI image/video/voice generator at https://isibi.ai — **high-contrast LIGHT: white surfaces, near-black ink, black accents** (`--split` is a near-black gradient on buttons/active states), Space Grotesk wordmark. Black-and-white platform since 2026-07-23 (owner's call — see the comment at the top of `styles.css`, which is the authority). The old dark studio look and the pink → amber accents are gone; that brand gradient survives ONLY on the landing chatbox, as `--halo`. (This paragraph described the dark theme until 2026-07-28 — five days stale, and it misrendered a screenshot before anyone noticed.) **The SIGN-IN GATE and the auth-code EMAIL were still on the dark theme until 2026-07-30**, which is the same failure one layer down: the gate's scrim was `rgba(8,7,12,.68)` over a white page and its inputs were a 30%-black fill carrying near-black text, so it was a legibility bug rather than a stale preference — and none of it is visible from reading the CSS, only from rendering it. The email is worse to leave stale because it is the first thing a new customer sees and it is NOT token-driven: mail clients strip `<style>` blocks and several ignore custom properties, so every colour in `supabase/functions/send-email/index.ts` is inline and literal and has to be changed BY HAND whenever the brand does. (The old LaserFlow beam on the home thread was removed 2026-07-05.) Root (`/`) opens straight into the Zephyr chatbox behind a Supabase login gate; the workspace is a single page, view-switched. **The old Home landing was removed 2026-07-15 — the Builder chatbox is now the home screen** (`viewHome`). The sidebar is kept slim (chats only). The other views — Gallery/Avatar/Media Agent — are **top-bar tabs** (`data-act="view"`), with Integrations + Settings (both undocumented before) reachable from the top-right **profile-pop menu** (`toggleProfileMenu`). (**the Products feature was removed entirely 2026-07-16, owner's call** — page, scanner, presets, picker source; the `.pr-head`/`.pr-or`/`.pr-manual` header CSS pattern survives on the Avatar page.) (The old floating-logo menu — `#floatNav`/`toggleFloatMenu` — is gone; any lingering refs are dead.) `showView('landing')` now redirects to `'home'`; `renderLanding` is dead code. **Studio (the iMovie-style video editor) was removed 2026-07-12** — the platform is AI-native, so all video editing is moving into the Builder chatbox (attach a clip → say the change → an AI edit model does it). The on-device ffmpeg engine (`public/ffmpeg-edit.js`) was KEPT — the QR-burn feature runs on it.

## Structure

- Static frontend in `public/` (plain HTML/CSS/JS, no framework): `index.html` (the Zephyr chatbox — the only page), shared `styles.css` + `chat.js`, `auth.js` (Supabase email/password + email-code sign-in via GoTrue fetch, session in localStorage)
- `worker.js` — Cloudflare Worker: serves assets, `/api/video` + `/api/image` + `/api/audio` (fal.ai queue, per-kind model allowlists), `/api/direct` (director via ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, tool-use for structured output — Sonnet 5 rejects prefill; effort-routed: Haiku 4.5 writes Low/Medium compose/revise prompts AND the ask/error steps, Sonnet 5 handles High/Ultra/Max compose/revise (the `studio` step is dead code — Studio was removed, no client sends it); the ask step also returns `needsWeb`, and when true the frontend runs a `research` step — Sonnet 5 + Anthropic `web_search_20250305`, `max_uses:4`, ~$0.01/search — that returns a factual brief + sources folded into compose via `webFacts`, so "the newest X" gets depicted as the real current thing; gated behind that judgment so most generations never search), `/api/import/fetch` (gallery import-from-link: server-side fetch of a user-pasted URL behind auth + the SSRF guard/safeFetch, Chrome UA; direct image/video/audio → base64+kind back to the client; an HTML page runs `pageImageCandidates` — JSON-LD → og/twitter → microdata → link image_src → lazy-load/srcset `<img>` scan, candidates tried in order with retry — and when the free path comes up dry (bot wall or no image) it AUTO-FALLS-BACK to the paid AI lookup: Sonnet 5 + web_search finds direct image links / alternate open pages, **✦3 charged up front, refunded on any failure**, `scanai` quota 20/day, response carries `balance` for the pill; the client then pipes the base64 through the normal `/api/save` gates), `/api/video/poll` (proxies fal status/result so FAL_KEY stays server-side), `/api/save` (copies finished fal outputs into Supabase Storage `media` bucket using the caller's JWT). All `/api/*` require a Supabase-authenticated user (verified via GoTrue `/auth/v1/user`).
- Supabase project: fifa-tournament-hub (`ujrqdmmtcptvimazlhom`) — auth + public `media` storage bucket (INSERT-only RLS for authenticated users). Settings account controls: "Sign out on all devices" (GoTrue `logout?scope=global`) and "Delete account" (`delete_account()` RPC, SECURITY DEFINER auth-only — deletes chats/credits/usage_log/storage rows (via the `storage.allow_delete_query` GUC)/GoTrue child rows/auth user; **`purchases` are deleted too** — full wipe on account deletion is the owner's call (2026-07-15), so `purchases.user_id` cascades with the auth user by design; client wipes its storage files via the Storage API first, then every `zephyr_*` localStorage key)
- Chats persist in localStorage (`zephyr_chats_v1`, 30 chats × 80 msgs) AND sync cross-device to a Supabase `chats` table (pushChats/pullChats); media messages store the permanent Supabase Storage URL. **Avatars sync cross-device too (2026-07-16)**: one `user_assets` row per user (avatars jsonb, RLS own-row, FK-cascades on account deletion; the table's `products` column is orphaned since the Products removal — harmless, ignore it), whole-object last-writer-wins like `user_memory` (pushAssets debounced from saveAvatars, pullAssets at boot); images are compacted to ≤800px JPEG before push (hosted URLs pass through), so the originating device keeps full-res locally until another device edits
- **Media Agent** — Instagram/YouTube manager (Composio, `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` server-side). Analytics/Posts/Comments (read) + **comment auto-reply** (prompt-driven, cron every 2 min, Haiku drafts, `INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_COMMENT_REPLIES`) are live; DM auto-reply is blocked (Instagram `instagram_manage_messages` needs Meta App Review). **A "Schedule post" tab (Instagram only) was added 2026-07-17 — FRONTEND ONLY: compose media+caption+datetime → a local queue in `localStorage` (`zephyr_ig_scheduled_v1`), nothing publishes yet. Media is previewed locally (no upload). Backend wiring (Composio create-post at the scheduled time + persistence) is the pending next step — the composer carries a "Preview · not published yet" flag.** Config in `user_autoreply`, dedup in `autoreply_log`, cron gated by `AUTOREPLY_ALLOW`. **For tool permissions, rate limits, engine caps, cost, and the scaling concern → see `docs/media-agent.md` (pull it up when the user asks any of that).**
- **Universal memory** — a **backend/system feature with NO front-end** (user's call): auto-learned creative taste, applied to EVERY generation across all chats (not per-chat). It learns from BOTH generations and plain conversation: the **ask** step (runs on every chat message) returns an evolved `memory` list that commits immediately (no approval gate — chat itself is the signal), and the **compose/revise** `write_prompt` tool also returns one that commits on approval (`pendingMemory`→`commitMemory`, mirroring the brief). Both feed compose/revise/ask via `directorContext().memory` → `memoryLine` in the worker (≤12 short durable phrases, project-specifics excluded). Stored in `zephyr_memory_v1` + a per-user `user_memory` Supabase row (items jsonb, enabled bool, RLS own-row; pushMemory/pullMemory last-writer-wins; in `delete_account` + the local wipes). Gated off for audio. **No UI at all** — the Memory floating button and its `viewMemory` "space" page were removed; the feature is entirely invisible/backend.

## Deploy

Push to `main` → GitHub Actions → Wrangler → Cloudflare Workers → isibi.ai (+ www). Secrets in GitHub Actions: `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `FAL_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (uploaded to the Worker each deploy). Work happens on a feature branch, merged to `main` via PR; deploys land in ~30-40s.

## Working rules

- **Always show UI changes as screenshots in the chat** (render the page headless and send the image) — the user reviews everything visually here.
- The user directs design; don't restyle beyond what's asked.
- Don't spend fal credits or Workers AI calls on tests without asking first.
- **THE WEBSITE BUILDER WAS DELETED 2026-07-27 (owner's call). It is being rebuilt from zero — do not restore any of it, and do not do builder work uninvited.** What went: all 368 files of the generation engine (the 258-component kit, the 5 starters, the capability registry, page recipes, both pipelines, the Lovable-clone pipeline, the eval harnesses, both build containers), the `/api/site/react-build` · `/api/site/react-revise` · `/api/site` POST handlers in `worker.js` (~1,340 lines), 17 test files and 13 CI workflows. **The only survivor is `builder/lovable/template/` — the shadcn UI, kept whole** (46 `src/components/ui/*.tsx` in new-york style, the shadcn theme in `styles.css`, `components.json`, plus the React 19 + Tailwind v4 + TanStack Router scaffold around it). The rebuild starts there and is **live end to end as of 2026-07-28** — brief → schema → Neon database → data API → generated pages → published React app (see the two bullets below).
- **Per-site data moved from Cloudflare D1 to Neon Postgres 2026-07-27 — D1 is gone from the repo entirely.** **ONE NEON PROJECT PER SITE as of 2026-07-29 (owner's call, was one per user)**, with the site's database inside it. Chosen over schema-per-tenant in the existing Supabase project because a Supabase project is one database, and over a Supabase-project-per-user because that bills per signup; Neon has no per-project fee and idle projects scale to zero. `site-db.mjs` = provisioning + the query layer (`sqlQuery`/`sqlExec`); `site-schema.mjs` = the schema engine. Both are plain modules, importable and tested outside the Worker. **`site_backends` now holds `neon_db` (a database name); the connection string lives in `user_site_project`, RLS on with NO policies, service-key only — it carries a PASSWORD, and `site_backends` has an "own read" policy that would have leaked it to any signed-in user.**
- **The old D1 site runtime was deleted 2026-07-27 (owner's call, data was demo-only).** All 37 `/api/site/*` and `/api/db/*` route handlers (20,569 lines) plus 626 orphaned helpers (4,577 lines) — `worker.js` went 31,585 → ~6,100 lines. Also gone: `test/backend` (386 files). What survived: the schema engine, `/s/<slug>/` serving from R2, and every core platform route. **R2 stays** — it holds published HTML served to the public and has no egress fees; Neon storage is ~23× the price and serving statics from it would keep computes awake and destroy the scale-to-zero economics.
- **`POST /api/site/react-build`** (also answers `/api/site/build` and `/api/site/react-revise`) — auth-gated, the builder's whole send path, and what `public/chat.js` already posts to. Idempotent (revise re-runs it); a slug is claimed by whoever built it first (409). The pipeline: brief → `designSiteSchema` (Sonnet 5, tool-use) → Neon database + `applySiteSchema` → `generateSitePages` (Sonnet 5, tool-use, same shape) → `tsc --noEmit` + `vite build` in the **`SiteBuildContainer`** (`builder/Dockerfile`, binding `SITE_BUILD_CONTAINER`) → dist published to R2 at `/s/<slug>/`. Responds `{ok, slug, url, backend, brand, tables, schema, page, files, notes, problems, cost, buildMs}` — **`page` is `"app"` or `"placeholder"`**, so a fallback is never mistaken for a built site. **Page generation is best-effort by design**: it runs after the database is live, so a generator or compile failure leaves the caller a working backend plus the placeholder page rather than losing the build (and a *revise* whose pages fail leaves the already-published site alone — the placeholder is only written when nothing is published at that slug yet).
- **`DELETE /api/site/<slug>`** — owner-only; drops the site's Neon database, removes its published R2 objects, then deletes the `site_backends` row, **in that order** (the row is both the ownership record it authorises against and the last thing keeping a failed delete retryable; the DB drop is best-effort so a failure there can't leave the files up). Before this a site could only be REPLACED, never removed, so a slug whose row had gone kept serving a React shell whose every data call 404s. **An unknown slug is 404, not a permitted delete** — files can't be deleted by guessing slugs, which is asserted in the smoke test along with 401 for unauthenticated. `deleteSitePrefix` follows R2's list cursor and stops when the cursor is absent as well as when the page isn't truncated, so it can't spin; `writeSiteDistToR2` wipes through the same helper. **Consequence of that 404 rule:** an already-orphaned prefix has no row to authorise against, so it needs the operator sweeper — `.github/workflows/sweep-orphan-site.yml` (manual, takes a slug), which re-attaches the orphan to a throwaway account and deletes it through the same route rather than growing a second, untested deletion path. It refuses any slug that still has an owner.
- **`publicView` was declarable, enforced — and never STATED to the page generator (2026-07-29).** Rule 9 tells the model not to call `usePublicRows` on a table without one, but `schemaDigest` — "what the schema permits, stated so the model cannot get it wrong" — never said which tables had one, so the rule was conditioned on a fact the model was never given. Measured live: the generator correctly deduced `bookings` had none, could not build the taken-slots hint, and **the whole site came out as the placeholder over one optional enhancement**. Now: the digest prints `usePublicRows: YES/NO` for **every** non-`display` table (an absent line reads as an omission, not an answer) and names exactly the published columns; rule 9 says a NO means ship the ordinary form; and `lintPages` flags the call, the same class as its other schema-mismatch checks. `hasPublicView` lives in `site-access.mjs` so the lint and the data path ask ONE question — two copies drift into a page the lint passes and the API 404s, guarded by a test that reads all three files.
- **`usePublicRows` could not be called correctly at all (2026-07-29).** It was typed `<T extends Row>`, and `Row` requires `id: number` — the one field a `publicView` can NEVER carry, because `parseSchemaSpec` strips `id` and `owner_id` from a projection and the API selects only the declared columns. So an honest type was a compile error (`TS2344`, measured live) and the only type that compiled was a lie leaving `row.id` undefined at runtime — a React `key` of `undefined` on every row. Now `export type PublicRow = Record<string, unknown>` and `<T = PublicRow>`; the generator is told these rows have no `id` and to key on a published column. Guarded both ways: a test asserts the signature no longer demands `Row`, and another asserts `site-schema.mjs` still strips `id`, since `PublicRow` is typed on that premise.
- **The page generator** — `builder/GENERATOR.md` is the contract, `builder/lovable/template/src/routes/index.tsx` is the reference page it is derived from (**when the two disagree, the file wins**), and `builder/page-gen.mjs` is the model-facing half: the rules, the `write_pages` tool, `schemaDigest` (what the schema permits, stated so the model cannot get it wrong), `validatePages` (paths, dedup, an index is required) and `lintPages`. **The lint is the important one** — it catches, without running anything, the class of page that typechecks, bundles and then 403s: listing a `collect` table, submitting to a `display` one, naming a table the schema never declared, calling `fetch`, importing a ui component that does not exist, or reaching for `useUpdateRow`/`useDeleteRow` (the API refuses PATCH and DELETE). **There is NO repair pass — one model call a build (removed 2026-08-04, owner's call).** A compile error or a lint problem used to buy a second whole generation; output is 80% of what a build costs, so a failing build cost ~2x a working one, and a working one is already about break-even against the 22 credits charged. A compile failure now falls back to the placeholder and a lint problem is reported on a site that still publishes. **Billed only when a real app is published** (owner's call 2026-08-05) — metered on real token usage (~26 credits warm, 38 cold), gated by a floor (`MIN_CREDITS`) and not by the worst case, since a new account is granted 20. **A placeholder costs the customer nothing**, by all three routes to one (no pages, no home page, a compile failure): measured live, a build spent 68s, returned `pages: []` and took 23 credits off an account granted 20 — the same price as a working site, for nothing. The charge now runs AFTER `publish`, so a publish that throws cannot bill either; `usage` is still returned on every path, so what WE spent is visible even when nothing is billed. The schema call's flat 2 credits still applies — the database really is live and a revise reuses it. **The four token kinds are priced APART** — fresh input, output, cache read (0.1x) and cache write (1.25x) — from ONE table in `publish-pages.mjs` that the eval imports rather than restates. Summing them into one `usedIn` billed a cache read at the fresh rate, ten times over on the largest input component, and overcharged a warm build by 35%. `page-gen.mjs` is a plain module, so all of it is tested outside the Worker (`test/page-gen.test.mjs`, 35 tests) — including drift guards asserting its copies of the reference page and the ui-component list still match the files on disk.
- **Every `display` table is SEEDED at build time** (2026-07-28) — `seed` is a required field on the `design_schema` tool (3-6 realistic rows per display table), inserted by `seedSiteRows` in `site-schema.mjs` right after `applySiteSchema`. **This is not decoration:** nothing can write to a `display` table after a build — not a visitor, not the owner, there is no route — so an unseeded table is an empty list forever, and a form whose required Select reads that table renders with **zero options**, meaning nobody can submit it. Measured live 2026-07-28: every site the builder produced was a brochure with a dead form. Seeding is `display`-only (fabricating `collect` rows would put fake customers in the owner's booking list), skips any table that already has rows (so a revise cannot duplicate the menu), drops undeclared and managed columns the way the data API does, survives one bad row without losing the rest, and is capped at `MAX_SEED_ROWS` 12. Non-fatal — the build already succeeded by then. The response carries `seeded: {table: count}`. `test/seed-rows.test.mjs` (15 tests, all mutation-checked).
- **`builder/publish-pages.mjs`** is the other half — the orchestration that spends the money and picks what gets served: the credit floor, charge-after-the-call, and publish-or-placeholder. It lived inline in `worker.js` (which cannot be imported — believed unimportable at the time; CORRECTED 2026-08-13, it CAN be, though extracting it was still right for the injection it bought) and so ran untested; every side effect is now injected (`generate`/`compile`/`publish`/`readCredits`/`useCredits`) the way `site-data.mjs` takes its database functions, and `worker.js` keeps only the wiring that supplies the real ones. `test/publish-pages.test.mjs` (22 tests) drives the decisions against fakes — no model call, no container, no R2 — and each one was mutation-checked. The repair-pass tests were replaced by their inverse: that a SECOND call never happens, on every route that used to trigger one, asserted at the dep boundary as well as the branch. **A site with no `index.tsx` is refused rather than published** — `validatePages` only flags it (it cannot know which of five pages is home), the repair used to paper over it, and publishing anyway ships a site whose root URL renders nothing. `stage`/`error` are returned rather than only logged. The credit floor **fails closed** — an unreadable ledger means no paid call.
- **The build smoke test is 45 checks and names its own site.** It proves the whole path in one pass against the deployed Worker — brief → schema → Neon database → seeded rows → generated pages → compiled bundle → published site, then a real browser loads it, submits its form and the row lands in Postgres, then the owner deletes the site and the files are gone. **A green run is the strongest signal in the repo**; a `page=placeholder` result is generator variance (one call, then fallback by design) and the response now carries `stage`/`error` so which is which does not need a second run to find. A slug is claimed by whoever built it first, across every account, so letting the designer name the site from a fixed brief meant it kept proposing the same good name — and the moment any real user (or an earlier manual test) owned it, the build correctly answered 409 and the whole smoke run failed on something that was not a bug. It failed exactly that way 2026-07-28 against `sharp-fade-barbershop`. It now sends an explicit `smoke-<random>` slug: a test must not depend on a global namespace it does not control.
- **`test/integration/site-build.mjs` + CI workflow `site-build`** — GENERATOR.md's definition of done made repeatable, and $0: runs `builder/build-server.mjs` against a sandbox copy of the template and asserts a generated-shaped two-page site typechecks and builds, that a page with a type error is **refused** (`stage:"typecheck"`) rather than bundled, and that `src/routes` is reset between builds so one site's pages can never leak into another's. No model call, no container, no Neon project. **Note for deploys:** the image bakes the template's dependencies, so a deploy now builds two container images instead of one.
- **Postgres dialect notes (things that bit, or would have).** Triggers: SQLite inlines the body, Postgres needs a function per trigger — `pgTrigger()` in `site-schema.mjs` emits both. Postgres `WHEN` clauses cannot contain a subquery, so the `maxRows` count and the `enforceRefs` `NOT EXISTS` live in the trigger body as `IF … RAISE`. SQLite's `IS` is null-safe → `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM`. Timestamp columns are TEXT and app code parses SQLite's `"YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"`, so defaults use `to_char(now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', …)` — bare `now()` is `timestamptz` and will not implicitly cast into TEXT at all. **Provisioning is async**: create-project returns when the work is SCHEDULED, and Neon rejects further calls while operations are in flight, so `waitForProject()` polls `/projects/{id}/operations` after creating a project AND after creating a database.
- **FTS is now a generated `tsvector` column + GIN index**, replacing the FTS5 virtual table and its three sync triggers — the database maintains it, so it cannot drift from the row. `to_tsvector` needs an explicit `'english'` regconfig to be IMMUTABLE enough for a generated column.
- **`noOverlap` IS a real `EXCLUDE USING gist` constraint** (`int4range(start,end) WITH &&`, plus `btree_gist` so the scope columns can use `=`) — the CLAUDE.md line claiming it was "still the hand-rolled INSERT … WHERE NOT EXISTS" and that a gist exclusion was "not yet done" was stale, corrected 2026-07-28. It **requires start/end to be INTEGER columns** and is SILENTLY SKIPPED otherwise (`console.error("noOverlap skipped")`), which is why the designer is told to use plain `unique` unless it has actually declared the integers. Partial UNIQUE indexes work too, and the partial form is what stops a CANCELLED booking holding a slot forever.
- **A whole tier of schema features is parsed, validated, persisted to `_meta` — and acted on by NOTHING** (surveyed 2026-07-28): `publicView`, `teamRead`, `transitions`, `sla`, `mask`, `fieldRoles`, `webhooks`, `geo`, `currency`, `formulas`, `roundRobin`, `assignBy`, `searchWeights`, `jsonShapes`, `checks`, `computed`, `defaultSort`. Their only appearance in `applySiteSchema` is the `norm.push` that copies them into `_meta`. `maskFields()` is even written and never called. The module's own header comment claims this is "where unique / noOverlap / publicView / teamRead / transitions / sequence / sla / trash actually live" — true for four of those, false for the other four. **Nothing can declare them** (the designer's tool never offered them), so no site is silently broken today — but do not assume a declared feature does anything without checking for its DDL.
- **What IS enforced**, verified by reading the DDL: `unique`, `uniqueCI`, `oncePerUser`, `maxRows`, `enforceRefs`, `noOverlap`, `sequence`, `trash`, `ordered`, `expires`, `pinnable`, `scheduled`, `version`, `sync`, `audit`, `history`, `archivable`, `fts`, `slug`.
- **The designer could not declare a single constraint until 2026-07-28.** `design_schema` offered exactly `name`, `access`, `columns`, `timestamps`, `fts` — so `unique`, `uniqueCI`, `maxRows` and `noOverlap` were fully implemented, tested, and unreachable on every site the builder has ever made. **Measured live: two customers booked the same 14:00 slot on a generated barber shop and both were accepted.** The tool now offers those four, with the booking case named explicitly (`unique` on a booking table is the headline; `noOverlap` only when integer start/end columns were actually declared, since it is silently skipped otherwise). Proven live the same day: second booking for a taken slot → **409 `duplicate`**, a different slot → 201.
- **`isibi.schema.json` is still the table-declaration format** — `parseSchemaSpec` + `applySiteSchema` live in `site-schema.mjs`, so a rebuilt generator that emits one gets tables, scoping, `unique`/`noOverlap`/`teamRead`/`transitions`/`sequence`/`sla`/`trash` for free. Proven against a real database by `test/integration/neon-e2e.mjs` (CI workflow `neon-e2e`, needs the `NEON_API_KEY` GitHub secret): it provisions a throwaway project, applies a schema, checks the triggers/FTS/guards actually fire, and deletes the project in a `finally`.

## THE DEFAULT BUILDER IS GROK, AND THE COLD-START SHORTFALL CLOSED WITH IT (2026-08-22, owner's call)

**`DEFAULT_PICKER` was `sonnet` and the Anthropic balance was empty, so the platform's PRIMARY FEATURE answered `400 billing:true` in about a second to anybody who did not know to change the picker.** `schema gen eval` had been red for three consecutive runs saying exactly that. One line, plus the client's copy of it.

- **THE SECOND REASON IS THE ONE THAT WOULD HOLD ON A FUNDED ACCOUNT, and it is the better argument.** Measured: **`buildFloor("claude-sonnet-5")` is 22 and `buildFloor("grok-4.6")` is 16**, against a free grant of 20 that the routing call has already taken 1 from. So the default was **3 credits short of its own gate** — a new account could not build cold, which this repo has had recorded as open since 2026-08-13 and which the owner had explicitly declined to fix by raising the grant. Flipping the default took a cold first build from 23 to 17 and closed it as a side effect. **Same class as the `auto` regression, in the opposite direction.**
- **EARNED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `build-models.mjs` said *"Flipping DEFAULT_PICKER is one line once a build has been watched end to end"* — Grok has published two (`harbourside-roast` 37 credits, `fold-lane-bakery` 94) against Sonnet's ~128 on a comparable site.
- **THE COST, STATED: Grok is ~3x slower on the pages call** (156s measured against ~50s), so a build eats more of the wall-clock budget before the edge gives up. That is a real risk on a long brief and is why the Arabic runs remain unsolved. `sonnet` stays one click away in the composer.
- **TWO DEFAULTS MOVE OR NEITHER DOES.** The composer keeps its own (`localStorage.getItem(BUILD_PICKER_KEY) || 'grok'`, twice) and a guard already asserted they agree — a composer defaulting to one picker while the server defaults to another means a request that says nothing gets a different model from the one the customer is looking at. **A STORED CHOICE STILL WINS**, which is the point of reading localStorage first, and the cost is worth saying: an existing browser holding `'sonnet'` goes on sending `'sonnet'`. **The flip reaches new sessions, not old ones.**
- **`XAI_API_KEY` BECAME REQUIRED, AND THE FALLBACK IS GONE.** It carried `|| 'not-a-key'` while grok was a third option nobody defaulted to — correct then, and wrong the moment it became the default. The old comment argued the fallback made grok *"fail at the provider with a named 401 rather than a mystery"*; as the DEFAULT that is not graceful degradation, it is **every build failing while the deploy reports success** — which is precisely the state Anthropic running dry produced, and it took a session to notice. **The cost, stated:** an unset key now fails the WHOLE deploy, the 2026-08-07 failure that lost three merges. Safe because the key is **proven set, not assumed** — four live builds reached Grok and were charged; the masked `***` in the log was never the proof.
- **THE PIN DELETED ITSELF, BY ITS OWN INSTRUCTION.** `test/build-models.test.mjs` carried the shortfall as a FACT rather than a requirement — *"a permanently red suite is one people stop reading"* — and its failure message said what to do when it closed: *"Delete this pin and tighten the guard above to include ROUTING_CREDITS."* Exactly that. The guard now counts routing and asserts it FITS, **with a headroom floor of 2**, because a guard that only says "it fits" goes quiet as the margin erodes to nothing.
- **FOUR GUARDS WENT RED ON A CORRECT CHANGE AND EVERY ONE WAS PINNED TO A SPELLING** — `DEFAULT_PICKER === "sonnet"`, `modelsFor("auto")` compared against `modelsFor("sonnet")`, two client literals, and `req.model === "claude-sonnet-5"` in the page-gen suite. All four now derive from `DEFAULT_PICKER`/`modelsFor()`, so the next flip needs no test edited. **This repo's most repeated own-goal, four more instances in one change.**
- 3833 tests, **7/7 mutations as expected** from a verified-green baseline with a comment-only control that had to survive — including both client sites drifting apart from the server independently, and the `XAI_API_KEY` fallback coming back. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no customer build has run since the flip.

## NOTHING COULD REPUBLISH EVERY SITE, AND THE FRAMEWORK IS BUNDLED INTO EACH ONE (2026-08-22)

**Every published site is its own Worker script with React and TanStack compiled INTO it, so each is frozen at the version it was built with — and all 14 callers of `recompileAndPublish` are single-site, triggered by one customer editing one thing.** The day a bundled dependency gets an advisory, the only fix is to republish every site, and there was no operation that could. Not "hard" — absent.

- **THE RUNTIME FORCES IT, WHICH IS WHY THERE IS NO SHARED LAYER TO PATCH.** `src/server.ts` says it: *"A WORKER CANNOT LOAD CODE AT RUNTIME — no eval, no dynamic import of anything not bundled at upload — so 'one Worker that renders whichever site was asked for' is impossible."* That is what makes a script per site necessary and a mass rebuild the ONLY upgrade path.
- **IT COSTS NO CREDITS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** `recompileAndPublish` reads the site's own stored page source out of R2 and drives the container — **no `callBuilderModel`, no `generateSitePages`, no `anthropicMessages`**, asserted as an absence over the whole function. So a platform-wide bump is container time, not model spend.
- **THE SHAPE IS `site-teardown.mjs`'s, AND THE ONE NUMBER THAT MUST NOT BE COPIED IS THE BATCH.** That queue uses 5 because a Neon DELETE is one fast call. A recompile is ~65s of container (vite 37s, render 12s, tsc 9s, publish 7s) against a 120s tick, and the build service is `oneAtATime` **for the whole platform** — so a batch of 2 overlaps ticks and puts a REAL CUSTOMER EDIT behind two bulk rebuilds. `BATCH` is 1, throughput is 30/hour, and both the number and the reason are asserted. **A bulk operation must never starve the interactive path.**
- **THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO, AND THE THIRD IS WHAT THIS QUEUE NEEDED.** `done`/`gone` forget the row; `retry` backs off; **`stuck` PARKS** — a site whose own source no longer compiles will not compile in ten minutes either, so retrying burns a container run every tick forever. It jumps straight to the last rung rather than climbing to it, and **stays in the queue**: dropping the row loses the only record that this site never got the upgrade, which is the state the queue exists to end.
- **`ours` DECIDES RETRY-VERSUS-PARK, AND IT IS READ RATHER THAN RE-DERIVED.** `recompileAndPublish` already sets it for exactly this distinction — *"our container went away"* against *"your change has an error in it"*. The two mistakes are asymmetric and both were mutation-checked: park a healthy site and it sits un-upgraded at the 24-hour rung on the one operation whose point is that nobody is left behind; spin on a broken one and it starves the queue. **Everything unclassified retries**, because being wrong that way costs a retry.
- **"IS THE SITE STILL THERE" IS ASKED, NEVER READ OUT OF AN ERROR MESSAGE.** A deleted site answers `error: "read"` with a sentence about no backend being recorded — matching that sentence is the class of check this repo keeps getting burned by, and it **cannot separate "deleted" from "Supabase is down"**, which need opposite responses. One `site_backends` read gives three unambiguous answers: throws → retry and spend NO container run; false → forget; true → rebuild. The dep **throws on a bad read rather than answering false**, guarded, because reading a blip as deletion drops a live site from the queue permanently.
- **A MISSING STORED SOURCE REFUSES RATHER THAN PUBLISHING.** Publishing with no pages replaces a working site with one that has no routes — strictly worse than not rebuilding it. `loadSiteSource` swallows an R2 blip and a genuinely sourceless site into the same null, so it is `ours: true`: the blip heals, and a site that really has none parks at the cap with that sentence on it.
- **NOTHING ENQUEUES ITSELF, ASSERTED.** Rows come from an operator sweep and nowhere else — if the platform could queue itself, one bug becomes a self-sustaining republish of every site. The sweep writes Supabase DIRECTLY with the service key rather than calling a route: a platform-wide republish is an operator action, so a route would be a new authenticated surface for a thing somebody does roughly never.
- **A SECOND SWEEP MUST NOT RESET A PARKED ROW**, and that was proven against real Postgres rather than reasoned: enqueue → park at attempts 5 with `TS2305` → re-enqueue with a different reason → **the row still reads `attempts 5`, `TS2305`, and the ORIGINAL reason**, `due_now: false`. `resolution=ignore-duplicates` on a slug primary key. Re-queuing would throw away the only record of why a site is stuck.
- **DRY BY DEFAULT, AND IT PRINTS THE DURATION.** "Republish everything" sounds instant and is hours — the sweep prints the site count, what is already queued, every parked row with its error, and the arithmetic at one site per two-minute tick, because that number is what tells an operator to start it now or overnight.
- **THE SURVIVOR WAS MY OWN INERT MUTANT — sixteenth recorded instance.** Setting `alive = false` inside a catch that `continue`s two lines later changes nothing, because `alive` is never read on that path. Re-run in the shape of the REAL bug (delete the `continue`, so the catch falls through to `if (!alive)` and forgets a live site) it is **caught**. A mutant that changes no behaviour reads exactly like a test gap and costs a hunt through checks that are fine.
- **THE REASON TO BUILD IT BEFORE IT IS WANTED, stated:** when it is wanted there will be a CVE with a clock on it, and that is the worst moment to be writing a queue, calibrating a backoff, and discovering that some 2026 site's stored source no longer compiles against the current kit.
- **PROVEN LIVE 2026-08-22, first drain: `x-site-build mt3khm7t-eqcid4 -> mt3ue1ko-sajlpx` on `fold-lane-bakery`, 225 seconds after enqueue.** Queue drained itself to 0, all three routes 200, and the only byte that moved in the served document is TanStack's per-request SSR timestamp — **the asset hashes are IDENTICAL** (`skeleton-Bhui893f.js`, `site-chrome-DHZ2QCa4.js`), so the same source really did produce the same bundles. That pair is what makes it a proof rather than a status code: the header says a NEW build served it, the hashes say the site did not change.
- **AND THE LIVE RUN EXPOSED THE HOLE THE JOBS RUNNER HAD ALREADY CLOSED.** Watching the row sit at `attempts: 0` for 145 seconds made the window visible: **the row is not touched until the rebuild RETURNS** — the ordering that stops a crashed run losing the site — so the cron's 120s tick against a ~65s recompile needs one slow site for two ticks to read the same row as due and both start a container run. `runScheduledSiteJobs` fixed exactly this and its comment is the rule: *"an overlapping tick that reads the same row as due loses here and sends nothing."* Same mechanism now — a conditional PATCH whose **WHERE re-states dueness**, `return=representation`, a row back means we won. **Proven against real Postgres and rolled back: `tick_a_rows: 1, tick_b_rows: 0`.**
- **LOSING A RACE IS NOT A FAILURE**, and getting that wrong would be worse than the bug. No attempt counted, no backoff climbed, no `last_error` written — the tick that won is doing the work, and recording a loss would park a healthy site after five ticks of ordinary contention. `CLAIM_SEC` is 600: ~9x the measured run so an overlap cannot squeeze through, short enough that a run whose ISOLATE DIED — leaving neither a forget nor a defer — is picked up again soon. That dead-isolate case is the only thing the number bounds; every ordinary outcome overwrites `next_try_at` on its way out.
- **THE SWEEP'S THREE GAPS WERE ALL IN THE WORKER'S `claim`, and all three are total.** The module's tests cover the DECISION and cannot see whether the PATCH producing that boolean is atomic. Dropping the dueness filter makes both ticks win (the guard reads as present and protects nothing); dropping the `r.ok` check makes a read-only Supabase answer true on every tick (duplicate runs continuously rather than occasionally); and **`return=minimal` sends no body, so the claim can NEVER win and the drain rebuilds nothing at all, silently** — a queue that fills and is worked through by nobody, which is the exact state the feature exists to end. Each is now asserted as a property, and each was re-run and caught.
- 3834 tests (+41), **20/20 mutations as expected** across three sweeps from verified-green baselines, each with a comment-only control that had to survive, plus one survivor re-run honestly (my own inert mutant). Every database claim here was driven against the real database and rolled back.

## A DROPPED CONNECTION NO LONGER COSTS THE SITE (2026-08-22, owner's call)

**Cloudflare cancels a Worker when its client disconnects, and the build route runs for minutes — so every reset killed the build mid-flight and left a claimed slug, a live Neon project, a settled schema charge and NO SITE.** `ctx.waitUntil` is the whole fix and it is five lines. Owner picked it over retrying the wall.

- **RUN 11 KILLED THE LANGUAGE THEORY, and that is the finding rather than the failed build.** This file recorded the ~285s reset as Arabic-only: *"FOUR Arabic attempts, ZERO sites… against TWO English attempts, TWO published sites (runs 6 and 8, at 378s and >718s, both past the 285s mark)."* Run 11 was **English**, the same four page shapes as run 8, and died at **274.3s with ECONNRESET**. So the reset is not a property of the brief — the two successes were the lucky side of something intermittent, and reading them as a pattern was wrong. Three instances now: 286.0s · 285.3s · 274.3s.
- **WHAT THE FIX CHANGES IS WHICH HALF IS LOST.** The work registered on `waitUntil` outlives the response, so a reset connection costs the ANSWER and no longer costs the SITE. The build finishes, the site publishes, the Neon project is a site rather than an orphan, and the schema charge bought something.
- **A TIMEOUT IN EITHER DIRECTION IS STILL NOT THIS**, which is why the bound built for run 10 has never fired. `BUILDER_CALL_MS` is ten minutes; both times it was measured, something else reached the customer first — 285s and 274s. A shorter bound refuses sooner and still produces no site; a longer one changes nothing.
- **THE BODY IS NOT RE-INDENTED, deliberately.** It is 1,800 lines and the one route every site on the platform is built by; re-indenting it makes a diff nobody can review for a change that is four lines of behaviour. **Verified there is no fall-through** before wrapping — the block's last top-level statement is an unconditional `Response.json(...)`, so the wrapper can never resolve `undefined`, which would be every build answering 500 instantly.
- **TWO OPPOSITE MISTAKES, and only one is visible without a test.** Registering the RAW promise means an unhandled rejection whenever a build throws; registering a SWALLOWED one and returning THAT means a build that threw answers 200 with an empty body — strictly worse than the crash it replaced. The shape satisfying both is `.then(noop, noop)` to `waitUntil` and the ORIGINAL returned, and the two spellings differ by one character.
