- **DRIVEN THROUGH THE REAL ROUTER, never read.** This is the wiring layer where twelve features have died: a source-read for `waitUntil(` is satisfied by any of the other twenty-eight calls in the file, by a comment, and by a call whose result is discarded. `test/build-survives-disconnect.test.mjs` drives all three build paths with a recording `ctx` — **3/3 mutations caught**, and the silent-200 shape fails all four checks.
- **`ctx` IS GUARDED because it is a runtime argument rather than a language guarantee.** One caller today, always passes one; a second added later without it would turn every build into a TypeError instead of behaving as it did before.

**AND THE CLIENT HAS BEEN WRITTEN FOR A STREAMING BUILD ALL ALONG.** `readReactStream` in `public/chat.js` handles `phase`, `agent`, `image`, `code`, `done` and `error` events, and branches on `content-type: ndjson` — and **the build route has never streamed**: measured, zero `ndjson` and zero `TransformStream` in its 1,800 lines. It returns `Response.json` after 200-700 seconds of total silence. A reader fully built for a producer that does not exist, which is this file's most-recorded shape pointed the other way.

- **STREAMING IS THE NATURAL NEXT STEP AND IS NOT THIS CHANGE.** Bytes flowing make an idle-connection reset far less likely, the customer sees live progress instead of five minutes of nothing, and the client needs no change at all. What stops it being a one-line win: refusals currently carry real HTTP statuses (`402`, `409`, `422`, `503`) that `build smoke` and `build-as-owner` read off `r.status`, and a streamed 200 moves those into the body — so the harnesses that would verify it are the harnesses it breaks. Worth doing deliberately, with those two updated in the same change.
- **THE RESIDUE, STATED: a build whose answer is lost is a site the customer cannot find.** The project list is `zephyr_sites_v1` in localStorage and there is NO server-side list of a user's sites, so a client that never learned the slug — the designer names it, which is a feature — has no way to discover the site that just published. The honest fix is a client-generated build id recorded against the site plus a route to look it up; not built here, and it is a decision rather than an oversight.

## THE MODEL WRITES ITS OWN BACKDROP, AND THREE HOPS WERE CUT (2026-08-22, owner's call)

**"On the style axes, instead of having options — the axis is good, but the OPTIONS the model should make, not choose from the ones there is here."** `backdrop` and `decor` now take either one of their six/twenty names OR a `{light:[...], dark:[...]}` of real CSS the model wrote. `builder/site-css.mjs` is the validator; the wiring is where the whole thing had died.

- **I ADVISED AGAINST THIS AND THE OWNER REAFFIRMED IT, which is recorded because the reasoning survived the decision rather than being abandoned by it.** Three shapes were put up — (a) free-text on every axis, (b) raw CSS on the two that are raw CSS underneath, (c) a wider enum — and (b) is what shipped. The concern was that a value we cannot PARSE is a contrast floor we cannot prove; the answer is that `site-tokens.mjs`'s own rule already covers it — *"the notation exists BECAUSE it has a parser, so 'accepted but unreadable' is not a thing to remember, it is unrepresentable"* — so the validator refuses anything whose stops cannot be read, and the guarantee is identical to the hand-written table's rather than merely similar.
- **ONLY TWO AXES, AND THE OTHER TWENTY-ONE ARE NOT ARBITRARY EXCLUSIONS.** These two ARE a `background-image` value and nothing else, so an authored one is the same kind of thing the named option already is. The rest carry a NUMBER (`scale`, `border`, `motion` — where a continuum is what is wanted, not free CSS) or name a whole block of rules with no single value underneath to author.
- **THE MODEL WRITES A VALUE, NEVER A RULE, and that is the whole security argument.** `worldCss` owns `body { background-image: … }`, so there is no selector to escape from and the character rules can simply REFUSE what an escape would need. `url()` is absent from the allow-list on purpose (a fetch the CSP refuses, or a `data:` URI putting arbitrary bytes on a customer's site through a field meant to describe a colour ramp).
- **`color-mix()` WAS IN THE ALLOW-LIST UNTIL IT WAS MEASURED.** The tempting argument is that a mix must sit between its endpoints, so reading the endpoints is a safe superset. **Measured over 40,000 random pairs interpolated in OKLCH the way a browser does: 9.08% land OUTSIDE their endpoints' luminance range, worst by 0.212** — two stops at 0.519 and 0.527 mixing to 0.739. Chroma interpolates linearly and WCAG luminance is not linear in it. So the endpoint range is an UNDER-estimate, which is the direction that silently drops the floor.

**AND THEN THE WIRING, WHICH IS WHERE IT ACTUALLY DIED — THREE SEPARATE HOPS, each of which a module test at either end passes cleanly through.**

- **`mergeStyle` RETURNED `.style` ALONE.** That is what is stored in `_meta.site_style` AND what is sent to the container, so an authored value was validated, reported, and thrown away before anything could render it. **The whole feature was unreachable from a real build.** The merged patch now carries authored axes as their RAW SPEC — which is exactly the shape `parseStyle` takes as INPUT, so the stored patch round-trips and the container re-reads it with a palette in hand.
- **`build-server.mjs` HANDED `writeTheme` THE PARSED ENUM MAP**, which by construction never contains an authored value (`parseStyle` keeps those in `.authored`). One line, and it dropped a hand-written backdrop on the floor at the last hop before the only function that could render it.
- **`parseStyle`'s `vars` WAS SUPPLIED BY NO CALL SITE**, so every layer naming `var(--accent)` was refused for *"names a colour the theme does not define"* — a permission in the allow-list that could never be exercised, and the exact described-then-refused drift the hint's own comment warns about. `themeVars` is the fix: this site's palette as custom properties, per mode, **through the same `css` emitter `themeCss` uses**, because that is the one place this platform decides how a palette colour is spelled and a second formatter drifts on rounding — which for a stop being read back for a contrast floor is a floor measured against a colour the page does not have.
- **`applyStyle` IS THE ONLY CALLER, because it is the only place both the value and the palette are in hand.** `normalizeSeeds` runs in the CONTAINER, so the Worker holds three hex seeds and none of the 31 derived tokens.
- **THAT SPLIT NEEDED `needsVars`, or the fix would have introduced a lie.** Exactly one refusal depends on the theme; every other one (a `url()`, a semicolon, an unbalanced bracket, a misspelt unit) is a fact about the TEXT and is decidable anywhere. Without the flag the Worker's note would tell a customer their backdrop was refused while the container accepted it and it painted — the two-readings-disagree failure landing on the half they read. **Asserted in both directions**, because a flag set too widely stops the Worker refusing anything.
- **WHAT SHIPS IS THE SUBSTITUTED LITERAL, not the `var()`.** `readLayer` returns the resolved text and that is what `worldCss` emits, so the colour the floor was measured against is exactly the colour that paints — there is no runtime token read to diverge from it. The cost, stated: an authored layer freezes the palette at build time, so a later colour change moves the page and not the wash. That is the right way round (the wash was authored against those colours) and it is the same publish that re-runs this anyway.

**NO UNION, AND THAT REVERSES MY OWN FIRST DRAFT — on a decision this tool had already made once.** The `webhooks` field a few hundred lines up refused one for a stated reason that is still true: *"this tool has ZERO uses of `anyOf`/`oneOf`, and a union here would be an untested JSON Schema construct in the one tool whose rejection 400s every build on the platform."* I shipped an `anyOf` anyway and then found that comment.

- **THE ENUM IS WHAT IS BEING PRESERVED, which is the point rather than caution.** A union means dropping `type: "string"`, and the enum is what makes an option the engine would refuse IMPOSSIBLE instead of merely dropped — the property that block's own comment exists for. A SIBLING FIELD (`backdropCss`) keeps all twenty-three enums exactly as they are, and the wire name is folded onto its axis at the door of `parseStyle`, so the cap counts it once, the merge stores it under the axis, and a refusal is reported against the name the customer would recognise rather than a field they never saw.
- **Asserted as an ABSENCE**, so it cannot come back as a tidy-up; overturning it means proving the API takes one, which the `grok probe` exists to do for two cents.
- **`var(--accent)` IS NOT THE BRAND, and the hint said it was.** Measured: in this palette it is a pale hover surface at **L 0.94** against `--primary`'s **0.56** — shadcn's meaning, not the seed's. A hint recommending it would have produced a wash nobody asked for on every site that took the advice. The hint names `--primary` and warns off `--accent` by name, and **it names the REFUSALS as well as the permissions**, because `url()` and `color-mix()` are the two a model reaches for unprompted and an answer spent on either is an axis silently dropped.

**FOUR GUARDS FIRED ON THE WAY AND EVERY ONE WAS RIGHT TO.**

- **The tool-schema checker answered `design_schema: unresolved`** — its retry bound was **a budget of 12** and each attempt binds one more undefined name, so adding two identifiers ran it out. The tool went unchecked and the message named neither the shape nor the missing name. Derived now, and it says which name it stopped on.
- **BINDING ONE HALF OF A DECISION IS BINDING NEITHER, and my first fix did exactly that.** `SITE_AUTHORED_AXES.includes(a)` is asked about a name from `SITE_STYLE_AXES` — stubbed, so the property was called `"x"`, the test was `["backdrop","decor"].includes("x")`, and the branch stayed unbuilt: **a clean pass over a shape nobody looked at**, which is worse than the false alarm the `seeds` fragment produced. **FIFTH time this stand-in has been too simple** and the first where the miss was silent. The rule it generalises to: bind for real anything that IS a schema and anything that DECIDES one.
- **`themeVars` threw on a theme shape `paletteFor` cannot read** — and `applyStyle` never touched the palette before, so that is a NEW way for a malformed theme to lose its whole look (the container's catch answers *"the theme could not be rendered, so the site kept the default"*). Per mode, so a readable half still resolves.
- **`schema-eval-scope` caught the eval's hand-written scope drifting**, which is precisely the job it was written for after that harness sat dead for a day.

**And the recorded own-goals, three more times.** Two container guards pinned to a SPELLING (`writeTheme(payload.seeds, { style: styleUsed })` and the exact `parseStyle` expression) went red on a correct change — both re-anchored on the property, and the second is now the honest statement that the transition's two halves share a SOURCE rather than an expression. And **an absence check matched its own explanation**: the comment arguing against a union necessarily spells `anyOf`/`oneOf`, so the guard failed against correct code until comments were blanked. Prose containing the thing it forbids, in a lint, a router guard, an absence check, a scope scan — and now here.

- 3874 tests. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — the Anthropic account is empty and no build has run against it, so no model has yet written a backdrop of its own. Every layer below the model call was driven through the real container.

## THE 74-AGENT BUILD-ROUTE AUDIT — 80 FINDINGS, ALL FIXED (2026-08-21/22)

**Owner asked for an honest audit of the whole build route, then "ok go fix all of it".** 74 agents over coherent slices, every medium-or-worse finding put to an independent skeptic: **3 critical · 27 high · 31 medium · 18 low · 1 note**, 60 confirmed. `worker.js` held 35 of the 80 — one file, one writer, so that half could not parallelise and was worked through by hand. **3617 → 3788 tests.**

- **THE THREE CRITICALS.** A revise silently FLIPPED a pair-declared table's access to `collect` (`coerceTable` stamping the preset a table never named), so a public menu became write-only on the customer's next edit. The prerender executed model-written page code in the build service's own long-lived, shared process — rebuilt as a spawned child. And **"put the site back online" restored the FILES and never the Worker script**, so the site 404'd at every address while the owner was told it was live.

- **THE SAME MISREAD, FOUR TIMES, AND IT KEEPS BEING THE PAIR.** `normalizeSchema` stamps `access: "collect"` on any table declared with a `read`/`write` pair — and the design tool tells the model to do exactly that when no preset fits. So four separate readers described a PUBLIC table as write-only: the lint's write gate, the digest's PAID line, the response's own `schema` field, and — found this round — **the placeholder page a failed build leaves the owner**, which is the one page they have. A cell with no preset name now gets a sentence built from its two axes rather than falling through to collect's, which was the same lie one step along the same expression.

- **THE WIRING LAYER AGAIN, SEVEN MORE TIMES.** `xaiSkipped` was exported, tested, and documented as "the route folds this in" with ZERO callers, so a PDF on the Grok picker was accepted into `blocks`, dropped at the xAI boundary, and reported in neither refusal list — a café paid ~24-38 credits for an invented menu with every field saying its price list was used. `langUsage` was accumulated and read by nothing (real Haiku spend on every bilingual publish the ledger never saw). `resolveLangs().refused` was destructured away while `mergeLook` had already STORED the refused tag. `builds`/`retriedBuild`/`killedAt`/`repaired` were computed and forwarded by nothing, so `build smoke`'s retry report read four fields that could never arrive — and `killedAt` is the one that decides money. `saveSiteSource`'s boolean was discarded at both call sites. The cheap-edit spine read `site_icon` and never put it on the wire, **killing the icon lane on its own lane**. And `siteRedirectFor` did not exist at all: see below.

- **THE MANIFEST MOVED AND THE READER STAYED.** The publish computes the route list and redirect map on every publish and writes them to the meta SIDECAR; the only reader parses them out of `sites/<slug>/index.html`, which Start does not publish. So `injectMeta`/`metaTags` — the only code that ever turned those fields into tags — have had zero callers since, and **renaming or deleting a page turned every indexed URL and every shared link into a hard 404**, silently, on the feature that threads an explicit `{from,to}` all the way through to prevent it.

- **AND THE GUARD THAT COULD NOT FIRE AT ALL.** On a failed build the route writes the schema placeholder unless a HEAD finds something published — the guard whose own comment says a failed revise "must leave the site that IS working alone". It HEADed `index.html`. Start publishes none, so the head always missed, `!live` was always true, and **a failed revise could overwrite a live site with the placeholder** on every site built since. `SITE_LIVE_FILE` is the marker written for exactly this question.

- **THREE THINGS THAT COST OR LOST MONEY.** Six refusals called `refundCredits` as a bare statement and discarded the boolean that function was given specifically so a failed reversal stops being invisible — then answered `cost: 0` while the customer kept being charged up to 21 credits. `persistSiteJobs` hardcoded `enabled: true` on a merge-duplicates upsert, so **the owner's off switch was taken back by the next publish** and the job resumed spending their own Twilio/Resend key on their own customers. And the build route ran an unmetered server-side fetch of an attacker-chosen URL BEFORE the credit gate, while the identical primitive one route over is metered.

- **A CRASH ON THE EXACT PATH THE RECOVERY CODE WAS WRITTEN FOR.** `(designed.tables || []).filter(...)` threw a TypeError on the two non-array shapes the normaliser deliberately accepts — a JSON string (measured at ~1 in 20 samples) and a name→definition map — killing the whole revise and returning 503 "the designer is busy", blaming the provider for our own crash while `seedGaps`, taught both shapes on purpose to recover exactly this, never ran. The narrowing sat one layer ABOVE the tolerance and defeated it.

- **"WE COULD NOT TELL" FLATTENED INTO "NOTHING IS LIVE".** `salvagePlan` refuses to stub anything when it was not told what is live — the whole thing keeping salvage from being a regression on every existing site — and the call site wrote `Array.isArray(x) ? x : []`, which always produces an array. So an unreadable prior source arrived as an explicit `[]`, every working page went into `stub`, and it was published over the customer's live menu and charged for. The module was made to fail safe and the call site undid it.

- **I WROTE THE `vidRefN` BUG FIVE TIMES IN ONE SITTING, AND CAUGHT ALL FIVE.** The early ownership check read `cleanSlug` in its temporal dead zone — `node --check` passes, esbuild bundles it, and EVERY revise throws. Then four more: the refusal branches return BEFORE their lane publishes, so naming `dPub`/`nPub`/`pPub` in an `eCharge` there is the same read (and semantically wrong — nothing was published to translate). A fifth named a variable that does not exist. **The guard is derived from the publish variables themselves and asserts the ordering**, so it fires on exactly that mistake rather than on a list of today's lanes.

- **AND MY OWN TEST CAUGHT A REAL BUG IN MY OWN FIX.** The bilingual sitemap expansion took its snapshot INSIDE the prefix loop, so a third language expanded over the second's output and produced `/fr/es/menu` — an address the site does not have, in the file a crawler is told to trust. A two-language site is right either way, which is why only the three-language case shows it.

- **THEN I WROTE IT A SIXTH TIME AND IT REACHED PRODUCTION — `main` ANSWERED `500 {}` TO EVERY BUILD FOR ABOUT AN HOUR.** `sourceStored` was declared in `buildAndPublishPages` and read in `handleRequest` when composing the response: **two different functions**, so it is not a TDZ read the existing scanner walks forward to find — it is the `du.id` shape, a name that is simply not in scope. Written into the fix for one of the four dead fields above. `node --check` passes it, esbuild bundles it, and **all 3,788 tests were green.**
  - **NOTHING WAS CHARGED AND NO SITE WAS DAMAGED**, which is the one good thing about where it landed: it throws while composing the RESPONSE, after the work and after the ledger, and the paid path was already refusing on the empty account anyway.
  - **THE ONLY SIGNAL WAS TWO PAID CHECKS GOING RED ON A RUN WHERE NOTHING THEY COVER HAD CHANGED.** `confirm smoke` and `member smoke` both failed on a commit touching neither confirmations nor members — which is exactly what a smoke test is for and exactly the reading that a green unit suite makes easy to dismiss. Both went back green on the fix, which is the live proof; and the build route now answers a structured `503 {stage:"design", upstream:400, billing:true}` where it had answered a bare `500 {}`.
  - **THE GUARD IS DERIVED, and it is the one the five earlier instances did not produce:** every identifier the build response literal reads BARE must be bound in the enclosing function. It needs a depth-aware splitter, because the last two false alarms of its calibration were a multi-declarator `let` whose second name a naive scan cannot see — 38 false alarms, then 3, then **0 on correct code**, which is the bar it had to clear before it could exist. It fires on the restored bug.
  - **AND THE GUARD I HAD WRITTEN HOURS EARLIER FOR THAT VERY FIELD WENT RED ON THE CORRECT REPAIR**, because it pinned the exact expression rather than the property — the twelfth instance this round, in a check of my own from the same sitting.

- **ELEVEN GUARDS WENT RED ON CORRECT CHANGES, and every one was pinned to a spelling rather than a property** — an argument list, a call that moved file, a `const` that became a `let`, an exact occurrence COUNT, and **three arities in one file that had each already been widened once before**. Plus a NINTH byte-sized source window outrun by its own subject, in a guard whose immediate neighbour already carries a comment warning about exactly that. The rule holds: **never size a source-read window in bytes, and assert the property, not the spelling.**

- **`enabled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true` WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED**, and the fix rests on it: omitting the column gives a NEW row `true` and leaves an EXISTING row as the owner set it. Had it been nullable, the same omission would have written NULL and the runner's `enabled=is.true` would have silently stopped every newly declared job from ever firing.

- **THE SWEEP FOUND TWO MORE GAPS AND BOTH WERE ON A FAILURE PATH NOBODY DRIVES.** 12 mutants over the `worker.js` fixes: **10 caught, 2 survived, control survived as it must.** (1) Deleting `stage: "pack"` passed everything — `putSiteWorker` reports an unrunnable bundle AS an upload that never happened (`status: 0`) so it rides both existing branches with no new wiring, and the stage is the ONLY thing keeping them apart; collapsed, an operator reads "check the dispatch credentials" about a bug in our own container. (2) Rewriting `refundFields` from `if (await refundCredits(…))` to a bare `await refundCredits(…); return { cost: 0 }` also passed everything — **the audit finding restored, on the money path**, because the existing guard is `assert.match(seg, /refundShort/)` and the mutation leaves that word in the file, merely unreachable. **A presence standing in for a property, in the check written for that exact finding.** Both replacements assert over EVERY occurrence rather than one spelling, so a second reversal or a third compiling path is covered without anybody editing the file.
- **FIVE OF THE TWELVE DID NOT APPLY ON THE FIRST PASS, AND THAT IS NOT A PASS.** A `|` inside a perl pattern collided with the runner's own `|` field separator, an escaped `builder\/model-xai.mjs` was a path `cp` could not find, and three patterns simply did not match the real source. The runner PRINTS `NOT-APPLIED` rather than counting it — a mutant that never applied reports as coverage that is not there, which is the mirror of the inert-mutant trap this file has recorded fifteen times. All five were re-run with corrected patterns: four caught, one (`refund-fields`) the real gap above.
- **AND THE SITEMAP MUTANT HUNG RATHER THAN FAILING, which is a finding about the fix.** Aliasing the snapshot (`const primary = routes`) makes `for…of` re-read the growing length of the array being pushed into — **an infinite loop, so a bilingual publish never returns.** The compounding `/fr/es/menu` bug is what the snapshot was written for; the aliased form is strictly worse, and only running it showed that. Re-run in the shape of the REAL bug (the snapshot moved inside the loop) it is caught.
- **THE SWEEP RAN IN AN ISOLATED COPY OF THE TREE, and that is the process fix.** A killed run skips its `finally` and leaves a live mutant where a commit picks it up — this repo has lost a session to exactly that, and lost one earlier the same round. `git archive HEAD` plus a symlinked `node_modules` costs seconds and makes the real repo untouchable. **One test had to be excluded and it is said out loud**: `render-sandbox.test.mjs` drops privileges to `nobody`, which cannot traverse the symlink, so the baseline is 3773 rather than 3789 — no mutant touches that path, and a red baseline proves nothing.

- **VERIFIED LIVE ON GROK, mid-round** (`fold-lane-bakery.gofarther.app`, 94 credits, 524 → 430): a public `loaves` table serving seeded rows to a signed-out visitor, `orders` answering **42501 permission denied** to a public read — the write-only guarantee holding on a real customer table — `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">`, a real photograph bought, published through the rebuilt spawned-child sandbox. **The Anthropic account is still empty**, so `build smoke`, `edit smoke` and both evals cannot run; Grok is the only picker that can build.

## RUN 10: THE BOUND NEVER FIRED, BECAUSE THE CONNECTION DIED FIRST (2026-08-22)

**Same brief, same picker, same slug discipline as run 9, with `BUILDER_CALL_MS` added — and it failed at a completely different place: `ECONNRESET` at 285.3s, from the FAR end.** Balance 425 → 416 (nine credits, a cold Grok schema call), slug claimed, Neon project provisioned, no site.

- **THE TIMELINE SAYS THE SAME THING RUN 9's DID, ONE STEP EARLIER.** POST 02:18:43 · `site_backends` row 02:20:16 — so design and provisioning took **93 seconds and worked**, for the third time on an Arabic brief. Page generation then ran ~192 seconds and the connection was reset.
- **MY BOUND DID NOT FIRE AND COULD NOT HAVE.** It is 600s; this died at 285.3s. So the ten-minute ceiling is **still unproven live** — a different failure reached the customer first, which is worth saying plainly rather than letting the fix look exercised.
- **IT IS RUN 4 REPRODUCED TO THE SECOND.** Run 4 died at **286.0s** with `ECONNRESET` from the far end; run 10 at **285.3s**, the same way. Two independent runs, seven tenths of a second apart. That is a real, repeatable reset and not noise.
- **AND RUN 9 REFUTES IT AS A HARD CEILING**, which is why this is not simply "the 285s wall is back". The same brief on the same picker held the connection for **1546 seconds** forty minutes earlier. So something resets at ~285s **intermittently**; a session cannot read the Cloudflare log, so naming what would be an inference wearing the shape of a measurement.
- **THE SCOREBOARD IS THE FINDING, and it is now big enough to act on: FOUR Arabic attempts, ZERO sites** (runs 3, 4, 9, 10 — 301s, 286s, 1546s, 285s) against **TWO English attempts, TWO published sites** (runs 6 and 8, at 378s and >718s, both past the 285s mark). The connection outcome varies; **Arabic page generation finishing does not — it never has.**
- **THE FIX FOR THIS ONE IS NOT A TIMEOUT IN EITHER DIRECTION.** A shorter bound refuses sooner and still produces no site; a longer one changes nothing, because the connection dies at 285s regardless. What it needs is a build that does not depend on the client staying connected — `waitUntil` or a resumable build — which this file already records as **architecture, not a patch**, and which is also the fix for a real customer closing a tab.
- **STOPPED SPENDING HERE, deliberately.** Three funded Arabic attempts tonight cost ~19 credits and produced three husks. A fourth buys the same information.

## AN ARABIC SITE STILL CANNOT BE BUILT, AND THE WALL IS NOT WHERE IT WAS (2026-08-22)

**Run 9, Grok, `qahwa-almadina`: design and provisioning worked in 79 seconds and page generation ran for 25 minutes 46 seconds without returning.** The runner's own 30-minute job cap killed it with the request still open. **Balance 430 → 425 — five credits, the Grok schema call, settled correctly** — and no site: 404 at both `qahwa-almadina.gofarther.app` and `/s/qahwa-almadina/`.

- **THE TIMELINE IS THE FINDING, and it rules out the old wall entirely.** POST 01:13:47 · Neon project `gentle-voice-74143156` 01:15:03 · `site_backends` row 01:15:06 · killed 01:40:52. Provisioning runs only after `designSiteSchema` RETURNS TABLES, so **the designer read an Arabic brief and answered correctly** — that half is proven for the first time. What did not return is the pages call. The 2026-08-21 cluster died at **286-301s** and was CPU (`limits.cpu_ms`, since raised, run 6 published at 378s); this is **five times** that and a different question.
- **THE ONLY VARIABLE AGAINST A KNOWN-GOOD RUN WAS THE LANGUAGE, deliberately.** Run 8 was the same picker, the same slug discipline and the same four page shapes in English, and it published. So the comparison is clean: **Arabic page generation on Grok did not finish**, and nothing else about the path changed. Not proven is WHY — token volume, or the provider hanging — and a session cannot read the Cloudflare log, so calling it either would be an inference wearing the shape of a measurement.
- **THE BUILD'S MODEL CALLS ARE THE ONLY UNBOUNDED FETCHES IN `worker.js`.** Every other one carries an `AbortSignal.timeout`; these carry none, on an explicit 2026-08-04 call whose reasoning was *"a cut connection pays for the tokens anyway"*. That is true and it assumed the call RETURNS. It does not bound the case where it never does — so the customer waits with no ceiling and no message, which is the *"THE BUILD PATH HAS NO TIME BUDGET AND NOTHING WARNS"* gap biting a second time, now measured at 26 minutes rather than 5.
- **WHAT IT COSTS A REAL CUSTOMER, measured rather than reasoned: a claimed slug, a live Neon project, a five-credit charge and no site** — and 27 minutes of waiting to find that out. Cheaper than the 2026-08-21 husks (20 credits) because the Grok schema call is cheap, and the same shape.
- **RIGHT-TO-LEFT IS STILL UNPROVEN LIVE.** Three attempts now (runs 3, 4, 9), three different causes, no site. Every claim about it continues to rest on local renders, the compiled-CSS cascade check and the unit suite.
- **NOT RETRIED, deliberately.** A second run at the same brief buys the same 26-minute hang; a retry is worth spending only behind a time budget that turns it into an honest refusal with a refund, or on an English brief, which answers a different question.
- **SO THE BOUND WAS BUILT INSTEAD, AND IT IS FREE.** `BUILDER_CALL_MS` is **10 minutes**, applied in `callBuilderModel` — the one place the provider is decided — so both fetches and both providers share it and cannot drift apart. Calibrated against the slowest MEASURED generation (156s, Grok run 6) and the observed hang (1546s): roughly 4x the worst honest call, under half the hang. **The cost of being wrong that way is stated rather than hidden**: a build that genuinely would have finished at eleven minutes is now refused — the better trade, because a refusal here is free and says so (`generate` is not in `CHARGED_STAGES`, and the design catch refunds the deposit in full) where the hang charged and stayed silent.
- **A TIMEOUT IS TOLD FROM AN OUTAGE BY NAME, NEVER BY MESSAGE.** `AbortSignal.timeout` rejects with no HTTP response, so `status` is undefined and `upstreamKind` has nothing to read — without asking, a timeout fell through to *"The designer is busy — try again in a moment"*, blaming the provider for a ceiling of ours and inviting a retry into the same wait. `isCallTimeout` reads `e.name` (`TimeoutError` **and** `AbortError`, since the same abort reaches workerd and Node under both) rather than matching the message, which is the runtime's and differs between engines — the cross-engine string comparison this repo has already been bitten by twice.
- **AND THE DESIGN REFUSAL NOW SAYS WHAT IT COST.** That branch refunded the deposit in full and mentioned money nowhere, so somebody watching a build fail could not tell whether they had paid for it. `cost: 0` rides on it.
- **NOT A BLANKET RULE ON EVERY FETCH, and that was measured before choosing:** 18 of the 127 `fetch(` calls in `worker.js` carry no signal, and most are legitimate — the Worker's own entry dispatch, pass-throughs, wrappers whose caller supplies the init, and the container calls that have their own `STEP_TIMEOUT`. Flagging all 18 is a false alarm on correct code, which this repo rates worse than the miss.
- **THE GUARD IS DERIVED OVER THE FUNCTION BODY**, so a third provider added later is covered without anybody remembering the file, with a depth-aware scan because a request init is full of braces and a flat one has been written wrong here four times. **6/6 mutations caught** — and two survived the first sweep: one was my own mutation hitting the wrong of 29 `cost: 0,` in the file (**a mutant applied to the wrong target proves nothing**), and the other was real — `/isCallTimeout\(e\)/` is satisfied by `false && isCallTimeout(e)`, which leaves the arm dead. **A presence standing in for a property, third instance in one sitting.**

## GROK ANSWERS THE REAL TOOL — 15/15, 3 CREDITS AGAINST 21, AND THREE TIMES SLOWER (2026-08-21)

**`grok probe` is the cheapest honest test of the one thing nobody knew, and it passed clean.** One call, the REAL 23-field / 13-required / 80,502-character `design_schema` tool out of the real `worker.js`, through the REAL translator: it made the forced tool call, filled every required field, seeded its display table, wrote a palette our own `normalizeSeeds` accepts, and named a page list and a 20-component manifest. `normalizeSchema` kept both tables. **No platform credits at all** — no Neon project, no container, no publish, no account — and **no deploy**, because it calls xAI directly with the runner's secret.

- **THE PRICE IS REAL: 7 credits cold, 3 warm, against Sonnet's measured 21.** The prefix cache works — run two reported `in 20 · cached 22144`, so the 80KB tool block is a cache read on every call after the first.
- **AND IT IS THREE TIMES SLOWER, WHICH MAY MATTER MORE THAN THE PRICE.** 110.5s, 86.5s, 88.3s against Sonnet's ~29s. A build dies past **~285s** at the edge (measured twice the same day on the Arabic brief), so a designer that eats 88s of that budget leaves page generation less room than Sonnet does — and page generation is the longer call. **Cheaper per build is worth nothing if the build cannot finish**, so the next question is the pages call's latency, not its bill.
- **THE ONE FAILING CHECK WAS MINE, TWICE, AND IT NEARLY BOUGHT A FIX TO CORRECT CODE.** I asserted `seeds.light.paper` against a field that is FLAT (`{name, paper, ink, accent, dark?}`) — so Grok had answered perfectly on both runs while the harness called it wrong, and the obvious next step was "add tolerance to `normalizeSeeds`" for a shape it already accepts. Driven locally with Grok's exact answer, the real normaliser takes it and derives the full palette plus the mirrored dark half. **A restated shape can disagree with the real one, and when it does the harness reports a failure that is not there — the mirror of a vacuous pass and just as expensive.** The check asks the engine now.
- **ITS FIRST FAILURE COULD NOT NAME ITSELF EITHER**: the detail string was conditioned on the very shape under test, so it printed *nothing at all*. In a probe written to diagnose. Fixed to dump what actually arrived, which is what identified the flat shape in one further run.
- **`npm ci` IS NEEDED and the first run proved it in 16 seconds** — the final gate is `normalizeSchema`, which reaches `site-db.mjs` and `@neondatabase/serverless`. Nothing is called against a database; the import chain alone needs it.
- **`readSchemaTool` MOVED TO `test/integration/schema-tool.mjs` so both harnesses share ONE extraction.** The eval is a top-level SCRIPT — importing it runs it and spends model credits — so the alternative was a second copy of exactly what that function's own header argues against. `schema-eval-scope` went red on the move and was retargeted; the guard working.
- **NO OPT-IN MARKER, unlike `build as owner`, and the difference is the cost**: two cents of xAI and nothing from the ledger, against ~130 credits. A path filter is proportionate, and running it freely before betting a build is the whole point.

## GROK IS A THIRD PICKER, AND THE TRANSLATION LIVES AT THE BOUNDARY (2026-08-21, owner's call)

**xAI has NO Anthropic-compatible endpoint — verified against their API reference, it is OpenAI-shaped (`/v1/chat/completions`) — so `builder/model-xai.mjs` translates both ways and NOT ONE LINE DOWNSTREAM KNOWS.** Both call sites read `j.stop_reason`, `j.content[].input` off a `tool_use` block and the four Anthropic usage fields, and so do the truncation guards, the `shape` diagnostic, `pageCredits` and the ledger. Teaching every reader two shapes is how a provider difference becomes a billing bug in a month.

- **THE MONEY IS WHY IT IS WORTH TRYING.** Output is ~92% of a build and Grok 4.6 is **$6/M against Sonnet's $15/M**. Priced against GatherHire's real token counts: cold **~34 credits of model spend against ~71**, warm **~24 against ~50**.
- **CACHED TOKENS ARE SUBTRACTED OUT OF `in`, and this is the one that costs real money if it is wrong.** Anthropic's `input_tokens` EXCLUDES cache reads and reports them separately, which is what lets `pageCredits` price them at 0.1x; OpenAI's `prompt_tokens` INCLUDES them. Passing it straight through prices every cached token at the fresh rate — the exact 35% overcharge this repo already shipped once by summing the four kinds. `cacheWrite` is 0 because xAI has **no write surcharge**: those tokens are already inside `in` at the ordinary rate.
- **A THIRD OPTION, NOT THE DEFAULT, and that split is the whole safety.** The pipeline rests on a forced tool call returning a well-formed object against a 23-field schema, and whether Grok holds up there is unknown until it has run. Default-first would break **every** build on the platform at once instead of the one somebody deliberately picked. Flipping `DEFAULT_PICKER` is one line once a build has been watched.
- **`callBuilderModel` IS THE ONE PLACE THE PROVIDER IS DECIDED.** Each call site had its own `fetch`; adding a provider to both is two copies of the routing, and the failure that produces is one call site still posting a Grok model id to Anthropic on a path nobody drove.
- **THE NESTED TOOL FORM, IN ONE PLACE, BECAUSE THE DOCS ARE AMBIGUOUS.** xAI's function-calling page shows a FLAT declaration beside a NESTED `tool_choice` — the Responses API's shape leaking into a chat/completions example. The nested form is what OpenAI compatibility guarantees, and the first live test is deliberately the **cheap schema call** so a wrong guess costs ~10 credits rather than a build.
- **`isXaiModel` IS A PREFIX, DELIBERATELY THE OPPOSITE OF `modelsFor`.** That one reads a caller-controlled field and must refuse the unknown; this reads a model id our own table put there, so `grok-5` routes without a new entry. What it must NOT do is route without a RATE — `ratesFor` fails dear and a derived test asserts every pickable model is priced. **It still refuses a non-string**: `String(["grok-4.6"])` is `"grok-4.6"`, the coercion this repo has shipped as a real bug twice, and my own test caught it on the first run.
- **A PDF CANNOT CROSS and is counted rather than dropped in silence** — the chat shape has no document part, so an attached price list that was ignored would otherwise be indistinguishable from one that was read.
- **FOUR EXISTING GUARDS WENT RED ON CORRECT CHANGES, and every one was right to.** The composer/server picker parity (fixed by DERIVING the menu from `BUILD_PICKERS` rather than a hand-list — strictly better, and the guard now checks the map plus that the menu is still derived); the rate-row shape check, which assumed `^claude-` and also has to admit a **dot** (`grok-4.6`); and the eval-parity check, whose "follow the const to the stringify" now follows it to `callBuilderModel` instead. **And my own new wiring guard outran a 4,000-byte window on `designSiteSchema`** — the sized-window own-goal, hit in a test written the same hour as the warning about it.
- 3606 tests, **11/11 mutations as expected** with a comment-only control that had to survive. **NOTHING HAS RUN** — no key was set when this landed, and no Grok build has been made.

## AN ARABIC SITE CANNOT BE BUILT — TWICE, AT THE SAME WALL (2026-08-21)

**Two attempts at one Arabic brief, both dead before a response, neither published, 40 credits gone — and the second one was NOT our client.** Run 3 died at **301s** on `undici`'s headers timeout (ours, fixed below). Run 4, through `node:https` with no timeout of its own, died at **286s** with `ECONNRESET` **from the far end**. An English brief through the identical path returned at **272.2s** an hour earlier and published perfectly.

- **SO THE WALL IS REAL AND IT IS NOT IN THE HARNESS.** Whether it is Cloudflare's own ceiling on a Worker response or the Worker being evicted is NOT established — a session cannot read the Cloudflare log — and over-claiming it as "Cloudflare's 300s limit" would be an inference wearing the shape of a measurement. What IS measured: two Arabic builds ran past ~285s and the connection died before a response; one English build at 272s did not.
- **WHAT EACH FAILED ATTEMPT LEAVES A CUSTOMER: a claimed slug, a live Neon project, a schema charge and no site.** Measured both times (`mathaq-alemarat` / `misty-pine-34527169`, `mathaq-dubai`), balance 705 → 685 → 665, both 404 for ten minutes after. The projects ARE recorded, so this is not the invisible-leak class — but the customer has paid for a site they cannot see, and the only route back is a revise of an empty husk.
- **"THE ANTHROPIC ACCOUNT IS EMPTY" WAS RAISED AND IS RULED OUT AS THE CAUSE, by our own ledger.** An empty balance answers **400 in about a second** with `billing: true` — the 2026-08-09/11/12 shape — and the deposit refunds. Both Arabic attempts instead **provisioned a Neon project** (`misty-pine-34527169` at 09:14:57, `small-bread-72232876` at 09:32:09, each ~35-40s after its POST) and **settled 20 credits**, and provisioning runs only after `designSiteSchema` RETURNS TABLES. So the design call worked, twice. It may well be empty NOW — two Sonnet generations plus GatherHire is real spend — but an empty balance cannot produce a 286-second hang, and reading it as the cause would send the next session at the wrong layer. **Check it before the next build anyway: with no credit nothing builds at all.**
- **AND THE 20-SECOND ABORT ON `anthropicMessages` IS NOT ON THESE CALLS.** That function serves the edit lanes; the design and pages calls each `fetch` directly with **no timeout at all** (owner's call 2026-08-04 — a cut connection pays for the tokens anyway). Reading the shared helper's ceiling as theirs contradicts the measured 29s design and 92s generation, which is how the contradiction surfaced.
- **TWO HYPOTHESES, NEITHER PROVEN, AND THEY WANT OPPOSITE FIXES.** (1) **Arabic costs more tokens per character**, so page generation runs long — GatherHire's `genMs` was 92.5s inside a 210s container step, and a 2-3x generation would put the total past the wall on its own. (2) **The designer answered `langs` with a second language** — plausible for Dubai — which fires the build-path translation wired the same morning: a Haiku call over every string, per language, inside the compile dep, on code that had never run live. Distinguishing them costs one build and needs the stored `site_look`, which lives in the site's own Neon `_meta`.
- **THE BUILD PATH HAS NO TIME BUDGET AND NOTHING WARNS.** Every other expensive step is bounded — `STEP_TIMEOUT` in the container, `MAX_STYLE`, `IMAGE_CAP`, the credit floor — and total wall-clock is bounded by nothing, so the first sign is a dead socket. **Nothing in CI could have caught it**: `site build` drives the container directly and never crosses the edge, and `build smoke`'s English brief sits ~30s under the wall.
- **A RE-RUN OF A DEAD BUILD IS A REVISE**, because ownership decides `revise` and the husk owns the name — so `OWNER_SLUG` exists to keep a retry a genuine first build.

## HANGING UP KILLS A BUILD, AND THE CLIENT'S CEILING WAS 300 SECONDS (2026-08-21)

**An Arabic RTL build ran past five minutes, Node's `fetch` gave up, and the build DIED — leaving a claimed slug, a live Neon project, a 20-credit schema charge and no site.** `undici`'s `headersTimeout` is 300s and is **not raisable from the fetch options** (an `AbortSignal` set longer does not help — the headers timeout fires first). GatherHire returned at **272.2s** an hour earlier, so the ceiling had always been one slow build away.

- **THE COST IS NOT A LOST LOG LINE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN HARNESS TIDINESS.** Cloudflare cancels a Worker when the client goes away, so the disconnect cancelled the build in flight. Measured on that run: `site_backends` and `site_project` rows written at 09:14:57–09:15:00 (Neon project `misty-pine-34527169` — recorded, so not the invisible-leak class), balance 705 → **685 at 09:14:52** (the schema settlement alone), the site **404 for ten minutes after**, and nothing further. **The client staying connected is what lets a build finish at all.**
- **AND THE SAME HAZARD EXISTS FOR A REAL CUSTOMER, unmeasured.** `public/chat.js` posts to the same route from a browser: a closed tab, a dropped phone connection or a network switch is the identical disconnect, and the customer is left with the identical husk plus a schema charge. A browser has no 300s fetch ceiling, so this is not the *same* limit — but the failure it produced is reachable by any disconnect. **Not fixed here** (surviving a disconnect means `waitUntil` or a resumable build, which is architecture, not a patch); recorded so it is a decision rather than an oversight.
- **`node:https` HAS NO SUCH TIMEOUT, which is the whole reason `postLong` exists** rather than a fetch option. Everything else in the script stays on `fetch` — those calls answer in milliseconds and none of them is worth a second mechanism.
- **A RETRY OF A DEAD BUILD IS A REVISE, so the harness can name a slug.** The husk owns the name, and ownership is what decides `revise` — so re-running the same brief would be read as an edit of the empty shell rather than the first build it never got. `OWNER_SLUG` keeps a re-run honest.
- **THE GUARD IS `test/build-as-owner.test.mjs`, and it blanks comments first** — the source explains both hazards at length and therefore spells both, so an absence check on the raw text matches the explanation and passes against broken code. Ten-plus recorded instances of that trap. **5/5 mutations as expected**, including a comment-only control that had to survive; the first sweep's control anchor was wrong (a `//` pattern against a `*` line) and reported SKIP rather than passing vacuously.

## THE OPT-IN MARKER FIRED ON ITS OWN EXPLANATION, AND A SIGN-IN BAN IS WHAT STOPPED THE SPEND (2026-08-21)

**`build as owner` ran the first owner-account build live (GatherHire, 128 credits, the platform's first three real photographs) and its workflow fired on ANY push touching its two files — so the fix for its own step-7 crash would have bought a ~130-credit build nobody asked for.** The fix pack: the post-build probe resolves the response's RELATIVE `url` against BASE and can no longer fail the process (it observes the outcome, it is not part of it — run 2 went red with a green, paid-for build behind it), and the workflow gained an opt-in commit-message marker.

- **THE MARKER FIRED ON ITS FIRST OUTING, summoned by the commit message that ADDED it** — the message explained the marker by name, `contains()` matched the explanation, and the job started. The skip-CI-marker trap exactly (third marker-class instance; prose-or-code containing the thing it forbids is at ten-plus across the repo's guards), committed within minutes of re-reading the rule. The discipline is in the workflow's own comment now: write "the owner-build marker", spell it only in the commit deliberately buying a build.
- **`cancel_workflow_run` ANSWERS 403 TO A SESSION, like `workflow_dispatch`** — so a mis-fired paid run cannot be cancelled through the API from here. The lever that worked: a **temporary GoTrue ban on the build account** (`auth.users.banned_until`, +15 min) — the script's step-2 `/verify` answered `403 user_banned`, it FATALed before the balance read and before the build POST, and the unban landed inside a minute. **Zero spent, verified against the ledger (705 before and after), site untouched.** The script's fail-closed sign-in is what made the interception possible at all: a runner that proceeded on a bad session would have had nothing left to refuse.
- **The `made: 3, planned: 4` question that started this was NOT a failure**: no `error`/`empty` on the images object (each is set whenever its cause occurred), the bundle carries exactly 3 slots / 3 distinct files, and the 107-credit pages charge decomposes to tokens + exactly 3 photos. The model placed 3 of its allowance of 4 and skipped /vendors correctly (its pictures are DB-driven vendor photos); its own `notes` miscounted — and that notes string is server-truncated mid-word (~600 chars), which is what made the miscount look load-bearing.

## THE MOBILE MENU SLID IN FROM THE WRONG SIDE ON EVERY RTL SITE (2026-08-21)

**Found by the owner tapping the hamburger on a real published Arabic site** (`layali-dubai`), which is the only way it could have been found: it typechecks, it bundles, it publishes, no test in the repo opened a menu in RTL, and the panel ends up in exactly the right place — it just takes the long way round.

- **THE HORIZONTAL SIDES MIXED ONE LOGICAL PROPERTY WITH ONE PHYSICAL ONE.** `inset-y-0 end-0` is logical and flips (measured: the panel lands at `left: 0` in RTL, which is correct); `slide-in-from-right` compiles to `translate3d(100%, 0, 0)`, and **a CSS transform is PHYSICAL** — `dir` does not touch it. So the panel was anchored left and entered from the right, crossing the whole screen. **The half-mirrored failure this file already names as worse than not mirroring at all**, arriving in the one place the RTL sweep could not reach.
- **THE SWEEP COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT, and that is the useful part.** It converted physical utilities to logical ones — `right-0` → `end-0`, which is why the position is right — and **Tailwind ships NO logical slide utility**: `slide-in-from-start/end` is zero hits in a compiled bundle. So the animation half had nothing to convert to and was left behind, silently, on a sweep that reported 96/96 no-ops.
- **THE FIX IS AN `rtl:` COUNTERPART PER SIDE, PER DIRECTION** — four class additions, `top`/`bottom` untouched because vertical motion does not mirror.
- **AND IT WINS ON SOURCE ORDER, NOT SPECIFICITY, which is why the guard reads the COMPILED CSS.** `rtl:` expands through `:where(:dir(rtl), [dir="rtl"], [dir="rtl"] *)`, and `:where()` contributes nothing — so both rules land at **(0,2,0)** and only Tailwind emitting the rtl one SECOND makes this work. A source-reading test stays green through a Tailwind upgrade that reorders them, while the only symptom is a menu sliding the wrong way on Arabic sites, which nobody connects to a dependency bump. `test/sheet-rtl.test.mjs` therefore runs the template's own compiler and resolves the cascade in a real browser: **`-100%` in RTL, `100%` in LTR**, so the fix is provably a no-op for every site already built.
- **THE GUARD READS THE VARIANT STRINGS, NOT THE FILE**, because the comment explaining the fix necessarily spells the class names being asserted — prose containing the thing it describes, this repo's most-repeated own-goal, and it would have made the check match against broken code.
- **TWO THINGS SEEN IN THE SAME SCREENSHOT ARE NOT BUGS AND ARE RECORDED AS DECISIONS.** The action button is rendered OUTSIDE the sheet, so the site's primary call to action is unreachable while the menu is open — true on every site we build, LTR included, and more visible here only because the panel is otherwise near-empty (two links in a full-height three-quarter-width panel). Neither was changed; both are design calls somebody should make deliberately rather than have folded into a bug fix.
- 3617 tests, template typechecks, **3/3 mutations caught** from a verified-green baseline with a comment-only control that survived — including the live bug restored exactly. **The fix reaches an existing site only on its next publish**, which for a cheap edit is any text or colour change rather than a rebuild.

## THE WALL WAS CPU — PROVEN LIVE, AND GROK BUILT ITS FIRST SITE (2026-08-21)

**A build ran 378.2 SECONDS inside the Worker and published**, where 286s, 291s and 301s had all died the same day. The only thing that changed between run 5 and run 6 is `limits.cpu_ms`. So the ceiling is identified, the fix is confirmed, and the inference the entry above declined to make is now a measurement.

- **`totalMs: 378209`, AND THAT NUMBER IS THE WHOLE PROOF.** It is 77 seconds past the longest build that ever died and 106 past the longest that ever published. Nothing else about the path moved — same route, same container, same publish, same account.
- **THE 30-SECOND DEFAULT EXPLAINS THE ENTIRE CLUSTER, in hindsight and exactly.** A build waits on the network for most of its wall-clock and waiting does not count toward CPU — but the work BETWEEN the waits scales with the build, so total CPU tracks total duration loosely. 272s stayed under 30s of CPU and published; 286/291/301 tipped over and were killed. The correlation with wall-clock was real and indirect, which is why it read as a duration wall and was not one.
- **THE COST BREAKDOWN, MEASURED: `container` 261s of the 378** — `genMs` 156029 (Grok writing the pages), `viteMs` 37393, `renderMs` 11796, `tscMs` 8598, `publishMs` 6995 — plus a 683ms schema apply and 4.5s of Neon provisioning. **Page generation alone is 41% of the build**, which is why a model 3x slower on that call is what made the ceiling reachable at all.
- **GROK PUBLISHED A REAL SITE, first time: 37 CREDITS against Sonnet's 128 on GatherHire.** 7 for the schema (in 22039 · out 1079) and 30 for the pages (in 34150 · out 3031), both `grok-4.6`. **~3.5x cheaper for a comparable site.** It also bought and placed a photograph (`made: 1, planned: 1`), wrote its own honest reply naming the two things it invented (opening hours and a street-less harbourside pin) and why, and left the footer without a phone number *"so nobody rings a number that isn't yours"*.
- **VERIFIED AS A SITE, not as a status code.** 200 at the public host, `/s/` 301s to it, `<title>Harbour Roast`, a real `og:image` on the site's own hostname, four seeded `menu_items` rows off the live data API — and `enquiries` answering **`42501 permission denied`** to a public read, which is the `collect` write-only guarantee holding on a real customer table.
- **THE SCREENSHOT WAS BLANK IN THE MIDDLE AND THE SITE WAS FINE, twice over.** A local mirror has no data API, so on hydration every list collapsed to its error state — a fact about the mirror. And with scripts off it was blank AGAIN, for a different reason: `reveal` is scroll-driven (`animation-timeline: view()`), and **a `fullPage` capture expands the viewport WITHOUT scrolling**, so every section below the fold stays at its `from` state. Measured per section with each centred in view: **opacity 1, all of them.** Two independent artifacts producing the same misleading picture, and the fix for the picture is to settle the animation rather than to believe it.
- **THE PROBE'S FIRST RUN PRINTED TWO VERDICTS IT HAD NOT EARNED, and that is the durable lesson.** `sub` came back 200 in **0.1 seconds** for a 240-second ask — the inner fetch never waited — and the script reported *"A SUBREQUEST CAN BE HELD FOR 420s"*, because all it read was a status and a wall-clock. `burn` was scored `last() || 0`, so a mode that died on its first step printed *"burning stops at 0s"*. Both are survival inferred from a green tick. The inner duration travels back now, a row that did not do its work is **NOT MEASURED** rather than counted, and every verdict is gated on the mode having measured something.
- **AND THE BURN LOOP WAS MEASURING SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY.** Workers freeze `Date.now()` between I/O, so `while (Date.now() - slice < 50)` compares one frozen reading against itself and **never terminates** — what ran was an unbounded spin wearing the label of a 50ms slice, which is why its 264.5s cutoff could not be read as *"240s of CPU was refused"*. It counts a fixed amount of arithmetic per slice now and reports the slices it got through.
- **WHAT IS STILL NOT KNOWN: where the new ceiling is.** 378s published; nothing has been driven past it. `limits.cpu_ms` is at the documented maximum, so there is no further lever — a build that outgrows 5 minutes of CPU needs less work, not more budget.
- 3613 tests, **3/3 mutations caught** with a comment-only control that survived. **PROVEN LIVE**: run `32479658380`, `harbourside-roast.gofarther.app`, balance 661 → 624.

## THE BUILD WALL: DURATION IS RULED OUT, AND `limits` HAD NEVER BEEN SET (2026-08-21)

**Four builds clustered on one ceiling in a single day — 272s published, then 286s, 291s and 301s died — across TWO providers and two languages.** So it is not Anthropic, not Grok and not Arabic; it is ours, it is load-bearing, and until this nothing about it was known: not the number, and not whether the CONNECTION was timing out or the WORKER was being stopped.

- **THAT DISTINCTION DECIDES THE FIX AND THE TWO FIXES ARE OPPOSITES**, which is the whole reason to measure rather than patch. Streaming the response keeps a connection alive and does **nothing** if the Worker is killed; moving the build off the request survives a kill and does nothing if the connection is what expires. Each wrong guess is a dead **~130-credit** build.
- **`/api/_slow` + `scripts/wall-probe.mjs` COST NOTHING** — a route that waits and returns: no model call, no Neon project, no container, no publish, no ledger. It spends wall-clock and that is all. **Auth-gated and bounded (`MAX` 900000ms)**, because an open endpoint that pins a Worker for ten minutes is a denial-of-service primitive anyone could aim at us.
- **FIRST RESULT: IT IS NOT THE CLOCK, and that killed the obvious fix before it cost anything.** Plain AND streamed both returned at 240s, 300s, 360s and **420s** — well past every build that died, first byte 0.2-0.5s on the streamed runs. **So the streaming answer was refuted on a free run** rather than after a paid build.
- **WHAT THAT LEAVES IS WHAT A BUILD DOES BETWEEN THE WAITS, AND THE FIRST CANDIDATE WAS A SETTING NOBODY HAD EVER SET.** Workers Paid gives a request **30 seconds of CPU by default** and allows up to 5 minutes through `limits.cpu_ms` — **`wrangler.jsonc` had no `limits` block at all**, so every build the platform has ever run has been against that default. Waiting on the network does not count toward it; a build's real work between the waits does — an ~80KB tool schema and a ~36,000-token prompt stringified, model answers parsed, and the container's whole dist handled as JSON plus base64 before any of it reaches R2.
- **RAISED TO THE MAXIMUM rather than to a tuned number**, because *"for now put no wall"* is the owner's call and there is no evidence yet for where a sensible ceiling would be. **It does not change the bill** — Workers charge for CPU actually used — so it only stops a build being killed part-way; what it costs is that a genuinely runaway request can now burn 5 minutes of CPU rather than 30 seconds before the platform stops it.
- **SETTING IT IS NOT THE SAME AS PROVING IT, and it is deliberately NOT recorded as solved.** The probe grew three modes that settle it in one run and they are the three UNANSWERED questions: `burn` spends CPU, `mem` holds memory (a Worker has 128MB, and the publish path buffers the whole dist), and **`sub` waits on an OUTBOUND FETCH — the shape a build actually has and the one shape `/api/_slow` had never tested.** A build is not arithmetic for five minutes; it is three long waits in a row.
- **`plain` AND `stream` ARE OUT OF THE DEFAULT MODES because they are answered.** Re-proving them costs 22 minutes apiece and would push the run past its job timeout — a probe that no longer fits its own budget is one nobody runs. `PLAIN_MEASURED` names the first run's number so a verdict comparing against "waiting" is never silently sourced from a mode that did not run in THIS pass; both stay reachable through `WALL_MODES`.
- **`mem` SWEEPS SIZE AND THE OTHERS SWEEP DURATION.** Sharing one loop would have sent it four identical requests wearing four labels — a check that cannot discriminate, reported as four results.
- **THE VERDICT NAMES A FIX PER CEILING, and they are not interchangeable:** CPU is a line of config; **memory is a rewrite** (no setting raises 128MB — the dist has to be streamed rather than held); a subrequest ceiling is a third thing again. And there is a closing line for the case where **nothing tested is the wall**, so a clean sweep does not end on a shrug.
- **`test/worker-limits.test.mjs` GUARDS THE SETTING AS AN ABSENCE, which is the direction that rots.** The danger is not a wrong number, it is the key going missing in a tidy-up — and its absence looks like a build killed part-way with the client seeing a connection reset, which reads as a network fault rather than a setting. Both mutants die: deleting the block fails 3 of 4, raising it past what the plan accepts fails 1 (**a value the plan refuses is not a slow build, it is NO DEPLOY AT ALL** — the class that shipped nothing three merges running on 2026-08-07). The config is also asserted to still PARSE, since a broken `wrangler.jsonc` takes the whole platform down.
- 3610 tests, **2/2 mutations caught**. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against the raised limit, and the probe's three new modes have not run yet.

## THE DESIGNER COULD PICK FROM 279 OF 2,112 COMPONENTS (2026-08-21, owner's call)

**"WE NEED TO WIRE ALL THE COMPONENTS DUDE, THE 2112."** The `components` field offered `KIT_PALETTE` — a frequency-ordered shortlist measured from the 324 corpus pages — so the other **1,833 were on disk, documented in `COMPONENT_API`, linted for, and unreachable from the one field that decides what a page is made of.**

- **THE MEASUREMENT IS WHAT THE PALETTE WAS MADE FROM, AND IT IS A BROCHURE CORPUS.** So a CRM's records screen could not be asked for: `data-table`, `row-actions`, `pagination` and `stat-card` are all real and none of them is in the 279, because no barber shop needs one. Measured live the same day — a CRM brief came back as a login page over a working backend, and the pages it did write reached for cards where a table was the answer.
- **`COMPONENT_MENU` IS THE WHOLE KIT WITH THE FROZEN 279 FIRST**, in their measured order, then the remaining 1,833 alphabetically. **The head is kept because `ALWAYS_API_CORE` takes `KIT_PALETTE.slice(0, 20)`** — reordering the palette silently changes which 20 signatures ship on every build, which is a much larger change wearing the shape of a tidy-up.
- **`builder/ui-components.mjs` IS A NEW LEAF AND IT EXISTS TO BREAK A CYCLE.** `page-gen.mjs` imports `site-plan.mjs`, so the kit's own names could not be read from there — and an ESM cycle does not throw, it yields `undefined`, which here is a menu of nothing on a field the model must answer. `page-gen.mjs` imports and re-exports in **TWO statements**: `export … from` forwards the name and creates NO local binding, so every one of its own uses below would be a `ReferenceError` that `node --check` passes happily (the `asHex` class, third instance).
- **~11,725 TOKENS, MEASURED, AND ALL OF IT CACHED.** It replaced a 279-name list on the same block, so a warm build pays ~0.37 credits and a cold one re-writes a cache it was going to re-write anyway. The field is a name list, not signatures — the per-site manifest is still what decides which signatures are sent.
- **TWO EXISTING GUARDS ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE POLICY, so the suite stayed green with nothing holding the new behaviour**: one said the field is a PALETTE, the other that it is strictly smaller than the kit. Both replaced by their inverse, plus a leaf-stays-a-leaf guard — restoring the cycle is the innocent-looking path change that brings the whole thing back.
- 3570 tests, **3/3 mutations caught** from a verified-green baseline. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against it.

## `site build` WAS RED FOR A DAY ON A FIELD NOTHING READS (2026-08-21)

**Four lines, every run since the seeds change: `broadsheet/editorial/zine/bauhaus: the theme applied -> {"applied":false,"theme":null}`.** The registry left the product on 2026-08-20 and `writeTheme` stopped taking a NAME — it takes three authored colours off `payload.seeds`. `theme-seam.mjs` was converted with it; **`theme-render.mjs` and `page-gen-eval.mjs` were not**, and went on posting `theme: "broadsheet"` into a field the container no longer reads.

A JSON body accepts anything, so from the harness's side a dead key is invisible.
- **FIVE OF THE SIX ASSERTIONS PASSED ON AN UNTHEMED SITE, and that is the part worth fixing rather than the payload.** "builds", "the page has content", "no runtime error" and even **"light and dark actually differ"** were all satisfied — that last one because the TEMPLATE'S own shadcn palette has a `.dark` block, so it was never a claim about the theme. Only a field read off the response caught it, and a field read cannot tell a palette that reached the STYLESHEET from one that reached the SCREEN.
- **THE NEW ASSERTION IS FOUR BUILDS DIFFERING ONLY IN THEIR SEEDS HAVING TO PAINT FOUR DIFFERENT PAGES.** No extra build, no colour-space conversion, no tolerance — and measured both ways: 29/0 as it stands, and with the dead field put back it reports all four rendering identically. Its signature is **paper, ink AND accent**, because background and ink alone false-alarm on two looks differing only in their accent, which is an ordinary thing for two themes to be.
- **`test/build-payload-keys.test.mjs` IS THE DURABLE HALF, DERIVED AT BOTH ENDS.** The allowed set is whatever `build-server.mjs` reads off `payload`, so a field added there needs nothing here and a field removed there fails at every harness still sending it. The 50 build payloads are walked with a **bracket-depth scanner** — a payload is full of braces belonging to something else, and this repo has written the flat version four times — keyed on `files` rather than on the URL, since `site-build.mjs`'s 50-odd payloads go through one `post()` helper several hundred lines from the literals. Floors on BOTH sides: a walker that finds nothing and a container whose reads stopped matching each report a clean sweep.
- **A COMMENT WAS CORRECTED RATHER THAN TRIMMED.** `theme-render.mjs` explains its viewport-not-fullPage capture by a `background-attachment: fixed` that a backdrop emits — and seeds carry three colours, so these four sites have no world layer and nothing emits it today. The capture is still right and the stated reason had stopped being one; it comes back the moment a `style` patch is posted beside them.
- 3574 tests, **4/4 mutations caught** from a verified-green baseline with a comment-only control that had to survive. **`theme render` 24/4 → 29/0, and `site build` is GREEN on main for the first time since the seeds landed** — all 19 steps, run `32439178689`.

## A BAD EVAL RUN ATE THE CORPUS FOUR CHECKS MEASURE AGAINST (2026-08-20)

**Found while merging main: four floor guards were RED on main, for a reason unrelated to any change.** `page gen eval` `git add`s `docs/auth-audit/pages` wholesale every run, and a run whose menu and tool scenarios both failed committed the one site that worked and **DELETED the other two** — 8 pages across 3 sites became 4 across 1.

- **FOUR CHECKS READ THAT DIRECTORY AS A FIXED CORPUS while the eval owned it as per-run OUTPUT**, which is the coupling rather than the symptom. The nav slot-finder, the anchor rule and two order-lane checks measure their false-alarm rate against **the only pages in this repo the GENERATOR wrote** — as opposed to the 324 exemplars, which are pages WE wrote in the house style, so a rule tuned only on those is tuned to us rather than to the thing being linted.
- **THE FLOORS DID THEIR JOB, AND GOING RED EVERY UNLUCKY RUN IS STILL NOT A SIGNAL.** Most of those checks assert an ABSENCE, and an absence over a shrunken corpus is a weaker claim wearing the same green tick — so without the floors they would have gone quietly VACUOUS, which is worse. But a check that fails whenever the generator has a bad day is one everybody learns to ignore, which this file already records as its own failure mode.
- **THE FIX IS THE ONE ALREADY APPLIED TO THE 324 EXEMPLARS: the corpus is not the producer's output directory.** Pinned at `test/fixtures/generated/`, reached through one path (`test/fixtures/generated.mjs`), and refreshed by a deliberate copy from a good run rather than by whichever run happened to go last. `docs/auth-audit/pages/` is untouched and still the eval's rolling latest.
- **GUARDED BOTH WAYS, and the second half is what stops the coupling coming back**: the corpus must still hold 3+ sites, AND no test file may read the eval's output directory — a restored read is an innocent-looking path change that brings the whole thing back.
- **THE GUARD FLAGGED ITSELF ON ITS FIRST RUN**, because the literal it searches for necessarily appears in its own search line. Built at runtime from parts instead of self-exempting, the trick `test/source-bytes.test.mjs` already uses — a self-exemption is a hole somebody later widens. Ninth recorded instance of prose-or-code containing the thing it forbids.
- 3535 tests.

## THE EIGHT PAGE SKELETONS ARE DELETED, AND `shape` ALREADY ASKED THE QUESTION (2026-08-20, owner's call)

**`structure` named one of eight skeletons — single-scroll · bento · sidebar · split-screen · full-bleed-hero · card-grid · editorial · terminal — and it is gone, taking the last two exports of `site-layouts.mjs` and therefore the file with it.** Six plan fields to five, 24 tool fields to 23.

- **MEASURED AS IGNORED BEFORE IT WAS TOUCHED, over the pinned generator corpus — the only pages in this repo the GENERATOR wrote.** `sidebar` — whose own description names `sidebar-layout` — produced **0 pages importing it**. `single-scroll` — *"one page, sections in sequence; the nav is anchor links into them"* — produced **4 separate route files, 0 anchor links, 5 routed `<Link>`s**: the opposite on BOTH halves of its own definition. `editorial` produced a centred column. **Three scenarios, three disobeyed**, and the counts point the same way each time.
- **THE FIRST ANSWER WAS TO KEEP THE FIELD AND DROP THE ENUM — the themes-and-families move — AND `shape` IS WHY IT WAS NOT.** That field already takes two or three lines on what LEADS, what the body runs through, and the rule this kind of site fails by breaking, authored per site. A second free-text field about the arrangement is the same answer twice, and two answers about one thing eventually disagree. **The tell was already in the source**: `shape`'s description had to spend a clause saying *"Do not restate the structure you already picked — say what goes IN it."* A field that needs a rule telling the model not to duplicate its neighbour is a field with a neighbour.
- **THE PAGE LIST WAS BEATING IT ANYWAY, and the booking scenario shows how.** It declared four page paths AND `single-scroll`, which contradict — a single-scroll site is one page — and the model obeyed the concrete list over the adjective. Correct of the model; **the plan let a self-contradictory answer through** and nothing in `normalizePlan` noticed.
- **WHAT REALLY WENT IS THE PHOTOGRAPH BUDGET, and it is a stated cost rather than a thing that moved.** Two branches keyed on the enum's own names: `terminal` returned **0** and `editorial`/`full-bleed-hero` gave the home page **2**. Both are the ordinary 1 now, so a `terminal`-shaped site buys one photograph it should not have (**~19 credits** of real fal spend) and a hero-led one gets one instead of two. **Neither was replaced by an inference, deliberately** — the obvious move is to key on `components`, and the home page defeats it: a barber's home page wants exactly one and would name `hero` and `safe-image`, neither of which is picture-led. Guessing a new signal on no data is how a budget starts being wrong quietly.
- **A STORED SKELETON IS STILL LEGAL INPUT AND MUST BUY NOTHING.** Every site built before today carries one of the eight in its `site_look`, and a revise hands that object straight to `normalizePlan` — so the shape is live, not hypothetical. Asserted both ways: the plan still normalises (refusing it would throw away a good purpose and a good page set over a field WE deleted) and the budget is 1 for all five of `terminal`/`full-bleed-hero`/`editorial`/`sidebar`/`hexagonal`.
- **THE TWO TESTS THAT STOOD HERE WERE REPLACED BY THEIR INVERSE**, on the precedent that replaced the repair-pass tests with *"a second call never happens"*: the field is gone, so what has to be held is its ABSENCE, at every one of the five layers it was live at — an absence rots silently where a presence goes red.
- **AND THE SWEEP FOUND THE ABSENCE GUARD WAS WEAKER THAN IT READ.** Restoring the `Structure —` line to `directiveFromPlan` alone **SURVIVES**, because that function normalises first and the normaliser drops the field, so nothing is left for the restored line to print. The assertion that does the work is the normaliser's; the directive one is belt-and-braces held by a property of another function, **and it says so in the test** rather than reading as independent.
- **MY OWN GUARD HIT THE PROSE TRAP ON ITS FIRST RUN.** `worker.js` explains in a comment where the directive used to come from and that comment names `site-layouts.mjs`, so an absence check on the raw text failed against correct code. Scoped to an IMPORT. **Eighth recorded instance** — a lint, a router guard, an absence check, a scope scan, a mutation, and now this.
- 3568 tests, **4/4 real mutations caught** with a comment-only control that survived, plus a second sweep proving the two apparent survivors add dead code rather than restore the field. **NOT PROVEN LIVE** — no build has run against it.

## THE PAGE TRANSITION, AND THE ONE AXIS WHOSE POLARITY IS INVERTED (2026-08-20, owner's call)

**The four interactive axes shipped that morning were deliberately about ONE element answering a pointer; the owner asked for the whole document as well.** The 23rd axis is `transition` — `cut` · `fade` · `rise` — on the View Transitions API, and it is the only axis in the engine with a half OUTSIDE the stylesheet.

- **EVERY OTHER AXIS IS FINISHED WHEN `themeCss` EMITS IT. This one is not**, because a transition has to be STARTED before there is anything for CSS to animate: `defaultViewTransition` on the router decides whether a navigation is wrapped in `document.startViewTransition`, and `pageCss` decides what it looks like. So the value is baked per site as `SITE_PAGE_TRANSITION` in `site-brand.ts`, beside `SITE_MODE` and `SITE_DIR`, and both halves go through **`transitionOn`, asked once** — two copies of "is it on" disagree silently in BOTH directions, and each direction is a real failure.
- **THE POLARITY IS THE OPPOSITE OF `REVEALS`, AND GETTING IT BACKWARDS IS INVISIBLE.** A reveal that emits no rule leaves the section VISIBLE, which is the safe end and is why its guard is "emit nothing under `reduce`". A page transition that emits no rule leaves **the browser's own cross-fade**, because the UA stylesheet animates these pseudo-elements by default. So `cut` is a real answer (no flag) rather than an absence, and reduced motion **SUPPRESSES** — `animation: none` on both pseudos — rather than dropping our rules and handing a visitor who asked for LESS motion strictly MORE of it than one who did not.
- **THE FLAG IS CONDITIONAL AND THAT IS THE SAME ARGUMENT ONE LAYER UP.** `defaultViewTransition: true` unconditionally is not "no transition": it is a cross-fade on every site on the platform, including every one built before the axis existed, plus a full document snapshot on every navigation for a feature nobody asked for. Asserted as an absence, because "always on" is the tidy-looking edit that reintroduces it.
- **ITS OWN DURATION, NOT `--site-duration`, and that was the call rather than an oversight.** Hanging it off `motion` like the other three reads as consistent and creates a silent no-op: `motion: "none"` pins that variable to 0, so a site asking for `transition: "fade"` AND `motion: "none"` would be told the fade landed and get a cut. The CURVE still follows the motion axis through `var(--site-ease, …)` — a missing custom property falls BACK, where a missing one with no fallback would void the whole `animation` shorthand and hand the page straight back to the UA's default.
- **NO HORIZONTAL SLIDE, left out rather than forgotten.** A slide has a direction, and the kit went logical precisely because half these sites may read right to left; flipping one needs `html[dir="rtl"]` to select through to a view-transition pseudo-element, which has not been rendered here. `rise` is direction-neutral, so it is identical both ways and needs nothing verified that has not been. The `CORNERS` precedent — "we forgot" and "we tried it and it broke" look identical in a list of names a year later.
- **IT COSTS NO NEW WIRING ON ANY PUBLISH PATH, which is the advantage of being a style axis rather than a field like `mode`.** All three container payloads already carry `style`, so a text fix, a colour change and a picture swap all keep it for free — where `mode` needed a derived guard requiring every `lang` hop to have one beside it.
- **THE PATCH IS PARSED ONCE AT THE CALL SITE and handed to both writers.** `writeSiteBrand` and `writeTheme` reading `payload.style` separately is exactly how the two halves come to disagree about whether the axis was named; `parseStyle` is idempotent, so `applyStyle` re-reading it downstream cannot change the answer.
- **THREE CONTAINER CHECKS WERE WRONG ABOUT THE COMPILED FORM AND THE FEATURE WAS RIGHT** — all three found by running it, none by reading. **Lightning CSS normalises `120ms` to `.12s`**, so the duration check pinned a spelling that is never produced (the `41.17%`-for-`0.4117` class, second instance). **It SPLITS a selector list into one rule per selector**, so a pattern written against `old(root), new(root) { … }` matched nothing. And **the router flag is a minified VARIABLE, not a literal** — `defaultViewTransition:IE` with `IE=!0`, and the SAME name on both builds, so comparing the two references would report a site that asked and a site that did not as identical; it is resolved to its definition now.
- **AND THE FOURTH WAS READING TAILWIND'S BLOCK.** `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` appears on EVERY build — Tailwind emits its own `motion-reduce:*` utilities under it, 203 characters of them, on a site with no transition axis at all — so taking the FIRST match read a block with nothing to do with this feature and returned the same verdict either way. It scans for the block that mentions the pseudo-elements, and it was **proved to fail** by stripping the suppression out of a real bundle.
- **A FLAT `split(",")` FALSE-ALARMED ON TWO CORRECT KIT RULES**, the fourth time this repo has written one where a depth-aware splitter was needed: Tailwind emits arbitrary variants as escaped class names, and `.has-\[\>a\,button\]\:x:hover` carries a comma INSIDE the selector.
- **AND THE SCOPE SCANNER'S SIXTH FALSE ALARM, its second from a regex literal.** A character class may hold an unmatched brace, so `/defaultViewTransition:\s*([^,}\s]+)/` closed a block that was still open and an arrow-function `const` read as out of scope **one line below its own declaration** — the least plausible finding that scan can produce and still cost a hunt.
